informal.BCn.range_rootPairing_root: Identifies the root set of the type BCₙ root pairing with the classical type BCₙ root set.

records.title: The nonmeagre lower bound for the rearrangement number
records.abstract: Formalizes the inequality non(M) ≤ rr in ZFC via relational systems, category and slalom bounds, finite-vector constructions, and rearrangements of conditionally convergent real series. The reverse inequality from the accompanying manuscript is outside the upstream Lean formalization.

informal.NonMRR.nonM_le_rr: The uniformity of the meagre ideal is at most the rearrangement number.

records.title: Certified Runge-Kutta Order Conditions
records.abstract: Certifies Runge-Kutta order conditions over planar rooted trees, including RK4 order four, Dormand-Prince order five, and Gauss-Legendre order six.

informal.RungeKuttaOrderConditions.Butcher.satisf: Reduces order-p Runge-Kutta conditions to a finite catalogue check over rooted trees.
informal.RungeKuttaOrderConditions.Butcher.rk4_or: Certifies that classical RK4 satisfies all planar rooted-tree order conditions through order four.
informal.RungeKuttaOrderConditions.Butcher.rk4_no: Shows that RK4 fails a fifth-order condition, pinning its order exactly.
informal.RungeKuttaOrderConditions.Butcher.orderC: Proves order conditions are invariant under permutations of a node's children.
informal.RungeKuttaOrderConditions.Butcher.dp_ord: Certifies the Dormand-Prince RK45 fifth-order tableau through order five.
informal.RungeKuttaOrderConditions.Butcher.gauss_: Certifies the Gauss-Legendre three-stage tableau through order four over Q(sqrt(15)).
Certifies the denominator-cleared (360-scaled) integer Z(sqrt(15)) Gauss-Legendre tableau through order six, the scaled certificate feeding the homogeneity bridge.
Certifies the Gauss-Legendre s=3 tableau through order six over Q(sqrt(15)), via the formalized homogeneity bridge from the 360-scaled integer certificate.

records.title: The Rupert Problem for convex polyhedra
records.abstract: Formalizes the Rupert property for the cube, the regular tetrahedron, and the triakis tetrahedron, exhibiting for each an explicit straight-through hole admitting a congruent copy.

informal.Cube.rupert: Proves that the cube has the Rupert property.
informal.Tetrahedron.rupert: Proves that the regular tetrahedron has the Rupert property.
informal.TriakisTetrahedron.rupert: Proves that the triakis tetrahedron has the Rupert property.

records.title: Sabidussi's compatibility conjecture for Eulerian multigraphs
records.abstract: Formalizes Sabidussi's compatibility conjecture for finite labelled endpoint multigraphs with loops and parallel edges, where a loop contributes two half-edge incidences to the degree of its vertex. Given an Euler tour and minimum degree at least four, the main theorem constructs a partition of all edges into nonempty, edge-connected, 2-regular ordinary circuits such that consecutive edges of the Euler tour never lie in the same circuit. The proof runs a four-colour (F_2^2) algebra over the cyclic transition word, uses an odd balancing parity lemma to choose compatible local frames, and transports the resulting colouring back to a compatible ordinary circuit decomposition.

informal.Sabidussi.LoopMultigraph.loop_sabidussi_: For any finite endpoint multigraph with an Euler tour and minimum degree at least four, the edges partition into ordinary, nonempty, connected, 2-regular circuits that are compatible with the tour: no circuit contains two consecutive tour edges.
The same compatibility statement phrased with the intrinsic even-edge-set circuit decomposition, from which the ordinary-circuit form is derived.

records.title: Every Pisot number is a two-sided limit of Salem numbers
records.abstract: Proves Salem’s two-sided approximation theorem for Pisot numbers, preserving both the polynomial reciprocal-family construction and the exceptional quadratic-unit construction.

informal.SalemTheorem.salem_theorem: Every Pisot number is approached by Salem numbers from both below and above.
informal.SalemTheorem.salem_construction_two_side: For the nondegenerate Pisot polynomial pattern, reciprocal-family polynomials have Salem roots arbitrarily near the Pisot root from either side.
informal.SalemTheorem.salem_quadratic_unit: The quadratic-unit family supplies Salem roots approaching each reciprocal quadratic Pisot unit from either side.

records.title: Moreira's version of Sard's theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes Moreira's strengthening of Sard's theorem, bounding the Hausdorff dimension of critical-value images of C^{k+alpha} maps.

informal.hausdorffMeasure_sardMoreiraBound_image_: Proves Hausdorff-measure nullity for images of points where the derivative rank is bounded by p, at Moreira's Sard bound.
informal.dimH_image_le_sardMoreiraBound_of_finran: Converts the measure-null theorem into the headline Hausdorff-dimension upper bound for critical-value images.

records.title: Jordan–Schönflies theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes the Jordan curve theorem and the extension of every homeomorphism between Jordan curves to a plane homeomorphism.

informal.Schoenflies.jordan_schoenflies_of_homeom: Every homeomorphism between two Jordan curves in the plane extends to a self-homeomorphism of the plane.
informal.Schoenflies.jordan_schoenflies: A homeomorphism between Jordan curves extends to a global homeomorphism agreeing with it on the source curve.
informal.Schoenflies.forall_isSeparating_of_isJor: Every Jordan curve separates the plane into an inside and an outside region.

records.title: Selberg Sieve
records.abstract: Formalizes the Selberg sieve with applications to prime-counting bounds and a Brun-Titchmarsh-style estimate.

informal.fundamental_theorem_simple: Proves the simple Selberg sieve upper-bound theorem.
informal.primeCounting_isBigO_atTop: Derives the asymptotic prime-counting upper bound.
informal.primeCounting_le_mul: Gives an eventual explicit constant upper bound for the prime-counting function.
informal.primesBetween_le: Bounds the number of primes in an interval using the sieve estimate.

records.title: Genus-Zero Pairings and Catalan Numbers
records.abstract: Formalizes the finite combinatorics behind the genus-zero term of the Wigner semicircle law: a pairing of Fin (2n), viewed as a fixed-point-free involution, has genus zero (total cycle count of the rotation product maximal) exactly when it is noncrossing, and these genus-zero pairings are counted by the Catalan number Cₙ. The Catalan recurrence is obtained from an explicit equivalence decomposing a noncrossing pairing by the partner of vertex 0 into independent inside and outside pairings.

informal.card_noncrossingPairing_eq_catalan: The number of noncrossing pairings on 2n points equals the Catalan number catalan n.
informal.Pairing.genus_zero_count: The number of genus-zero pairings of Fin (2n) equals the Catalan number catalan n.
informal.Pairing.genus_zero_iff_noncrossing: A pairing has genus zero if and only if it is noncrossing.

records.title: Wigner Semicircle Distribution
records.abstract: Defines the real Wigner semicircle distribution, its normalized density, affine transformations, and finite-moment integrability.

informal.LeanPool.SemicircleLaw.semicirclePDFReal: Defines the real-valued density of the semicircle distribution with mean μ and variance v.
informal.LeanPool.SemicircleLaw.semicirclePDF: Defines the ℝ≥0∞-valued density of the semicircle distribution.
informal.LeanPool.SemicircleLaw.integral_semicirc: Proves that the real-valued semicircle density integrates to one for nonzero variance.
informal.LeanPool.SemicircleLaw.semicircleReal: Defines the semicircle measure on ℝ, equal to a Dirac mass when the variance is zero.
informal.LeanPool.SemicircleLaw.semicircleReal_ma: Shows that translating a semicircle measure translates its mean parameter.
Shows that scaling by a nonzero constant scales the mean and variance parameters.
informal.LeanPool.SemicircleLaw.memLp_id_semicirc: Shows that the identity has all finite Lp moments under a semicircle distribution.

records.title: Sensitivity Conjecture: sqrt(deg) <= sensitivity
records.abstract: Formalizes the quantitative Nisan-Szegedy/Huang sensitivity theorem for Boolean functions.

informal.LeanPoolSensitivity.sensitivity_ge_sqrt_: Proves that the square root of multilinear degree is bounded above by sensitivity.
informal.LeanPoolSensitivity.degree_le_sensitivit: Derives the degree bound by the square of sensitivity.

records.title: Serre's mass formula for totally ramified local-field extensions
records.abstract: Proves both of Serre's mass formulas for totally ramified separable extensions of a nonarchimedean local field of any positive degree, together with the discriminant bound, tame-ramification criterion, finiteness dichotomy, convergence, and automorphism-weighted orbit count. The proof develops Eisenstein monogenicity, quantitative Newton-Hensel lifting, local constancy of root counts, and Haar measures of lattices over discrete valuation rings.

informal.MassFormula.tsum_one_div_q_pow_c: For every nonarchimedean local field K with residue-field cardinality q and every positive integer n, the sum of q^(-c(L)) over the totally ramified degree-n subextensions L of a separable closure of K is n, where c(L) is the discriminant exponent minus n plus one.
informal.MassFormula.tsum_one_div_w_mul_q_pow_c: For every nonarchimedean local field K, positive n, and set of representatives of K-isomorphism classes of totally ramified separable degree-n extensions, the sum of 1/(|Aut_K(L)| q^c(L)) is one.
informal.MassFormula.sigma_infinite_iff: For positive n, the set of totally ramified separable degree-n subextensions is infinite exactly when K and its residue field have the same characteristic p and p divides n.
informal.MassFormula.sub_one_le_d: For positive n, the discriminant exponent of a totally ramified degree-n extension is at least n-1.
informal.MassFormula.c_eq_zero_iff: For positive n and a totally ramified degree-n extension, the wild discriminant exponent vanishes exactly when the residue characteristic does not divide n.
informal.MassFormula.summable_one_div_q_pow_c: For positive n, the real-valued series of the unweighted mass terms is summable.
informal.MassFormula.ncard_isomorphic_mul_w: For a nonarchimedean local field K and a totally ramified separable extension L of positive degree n, the number of K-isomorphic copies of L inside a separable closure, multiplied by |Aut_K(L)|, is n.

records.title: The Kunen inconsistency theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes elementary embeddings of models of ZF set theory and proves the Kunen inconsistency theorem, that there is no nontrivial elementary embedding of the set-theoretic universe into itself.

informal.SetTheory.kunen_inconsistency_V: Proves the Kunen inconsistency theorem, that every elementary embedding of the von Neumann universe V into itself is the identity.
informal.SetTheory.kunen_inconsistency_vonNeumann: Proves the Kunen inconsistency theorem for von Neumann levels V_μ at a successor-limit ordinal, computing the supremum of the critical-point iterates.
informal.SetTheory.crit: Defines the critical point of a nontrivial elementary embedding as the least ordinal it moves.
informal.NontrivialElementaryEmbedding: Defines a nontrivial elementary embedding of a model of ZF into itself.

records.title: Shannon Entropy Characterization
records.abstract: Formalizes Shannon's finite-alphabet characterization theorem for entropy from the 1948 paper.

informal.LeanPool.Shannon1948Formalization.entrop: Proves that any finite-alphabet uncertainty functional satisfying Shannon's conditions equals natural-log entropy up to a positive scale.
Restates the characterization for any logarithm base greater than one.
Proves the converse, showing that Shannon entropy satisfies the formal condition bundle.
informal.LeanPool.Shannon1948Formalization.chain_: Proves the finite joint-entropy chain rule.
informal.LeanPool.Shannon1948Formalization.entrop: Proves subadditivity of finite joint entropy.

records.title: Quadratic-order prime classification
records.abstract: Formalizes foundational algebra for quadratic orders associated to discriminants, including their power basis, norm and discriminant identities, odd-prime splitting/ramification/inertness criteria via Legendre symbols, and root-counting results for quadratic congruences modulo odd prime powers.

informal.QuadraticOrder.prime_inert_iff: Proves that for an odd rational prime p and a valid discriminant d, the ideal (p) is maximal in the quadratic order O_d exactly when the Legendre symbol (d/p) is -1.
informal.QuadraticOrder.prime_ramified_iff: Proves that for an odd rational prime p and a valid discriminant d, the ideal (p) is not radical in O_d exactly when p divides d.
informal.QuadraticOrder.prime_split_iff: Proves that for an odd rational prime p and a valid discriminant d, the ideal (p) is radical but not maximal exactly when the Legendre symbol (d/p) is 1.
informal.QuadraticOrder.cardSqrts_prime_pow_copri: Counts roots of x^2 = c modulo p^n for odd prime p and p not dividing c, giving two roots when the Legendre symbol is 1 and none otherwise.
informal.QuadraticOrder.cardSqrts_prime_pow_even_: Counts roots of x^2 = p^(2r) u modulo p^n for odd prime p, p not dividing u, and 2r < n, reducing to the coprime case and multiplying by p^r.
informal.QuadraticOrder.tau_sub_tauConj_sq_of_val: Proves the discriminant identity (tau - tauConj)^2 = d for valid quadratic-order discriminants d congruent to 0 or 1 modulo 4.

records.title: Spectral positivity
records.abstract: Perron-Frobenius theory, Jentzsch's theorem, and matrix/operator positivity in Lean 4. At the matrix level it proves that nonnegative matrices have nonnegative powers, the Metzler decomposition and positivity of the matrix exponential of a Metzler matrix, M-matrix inverse positivity, and the Perron-Frobenius theorem for irreducible nonnegative matrices (a positive dominant eigenvalue with a strictly positive eigenvector). At the operator level it proves Jentzsch's theorem for compact self-adjoint positivity-improving operators on L2 — a simple, strictly positive ground state with a spectral gap — together with a kernel positivity criterion.

informal.allpos_has_pos_eigenvec: A matrix with all strictly positive entries has a positive eigenvalue with a strictly positive eigenvector (Perron-Frobenius for positive matrices, via the Collatz-Wielandt characterization).
informal.perron_frobenius: An irreducible (primitive) nonnegative matrix has a positive eigenvalue with a strictly positive eigenvector.
informal.ground_state_strictly_positive: The ground eigenfunction of a compact self-adjoint positivity-improving operator on L2 is strictly positive almost everywhere (Jentzsch).
informal.SpectralPositivity.Matrix.MMatrix.invers: The inverse of a nonsingular irreducible M-matrix is entrywise strictly positive.

records.title: Sharp asymptotic upper bounds for sphere packing
records.abstract: Formalizes the sharp high-dimensional asymptotics of the unrestricted Cohn--Elkies linear program and bridges them to sphere-packing density. The development constructs radial test functions through Mellin, saddle-point, and harmonic analysis, proves radialization preserves the unrestricted optimum, and certifies the exact natural- and base-two exponential rates.

informal.PackingBounds.FullMain.exact_limit: The d-th root of the unrestricted Cohn--Elkies linear-program bound converges to the sharp constant sqrt(e / (2 pi)).
informal.PackingBounds.FullMain.exact_binary_expo: The base-two logarithm of the unrestricted linear-program bound, divided by dimension, converges to -1/2 log_2(2 pi / e).
informal.PackingBounds.PackingBridge.sphere_packi: There is a vanishing error sequence such that, in every positive dimension, sphere-packing density is at most (sqrt(e / (2 pi)) plus that error) to the dimension.
informal.PackingBounds.sharpFullCohnElkiesManuscr: Packages the complete sharp asymptotic conclusions for the unrestricted program, including quotient-root, natural-logarithmic, and base-two limits, vanishing-error formulas, a universal bound for all admissible functions, and a certified decimal exponent interval.

records.title: Verified Stallings folding for finitely generated subgroups of F2
records.abstract: Constructs a finite inverse automaton recognizing the subgroup generated by any finite list of signed words in the rank-two free group. Proves exact subgroup preservation and correctness of canonical reduced-word membership testing. Reusable infrastructure includes inverse-automaton walks, reduction-compatible traversal, finite fold congruences, coset potentials, flower graphs, and basis roses. Folding uses exhaustive finite search over Boolean relations; no complexity bound, core pruning, subgroup basis, intersection, or index algorithm is claimed.

informal.Stallings.folded_recognizer_exists: For every finite list S of signed words on two generators, there exist a finite type of states, a base state, and a partial transition table with inverse-labelled reverse edges, such that traversing the canonical reduced word of any g in FreeGroup (Fin 2) returns to the base exactly when g lies in the subgroup generated by the word values in S. The witness is the computed flower-graph fold.
informal.Stallings.foldWords_loopSubgroup_eq_gene: For every finite input list of signed words in the rank-two free group, the based-loop subgroup of the computed folded flower graph equals the subgroup generated by the input words.
informal.Stallings.foldedMembershipTest_eq_true_i: For any finite generating list S and any rank-two free-group element g, the executable folded-automaton test returns true if and only if g belongs to the subgroup generated by S. There is no efficiency guarantee for constructing the automaton.

records.title: Monotonicity Formula for Stationary Harmonic Maps
records.abstract: Formalizes the monotonicity formula for stationary `W^{1,2}_{loc}` maps with Euclidean target. The proof is target independent: it uses only the displayed weak gradient and a vanishing domain first variation, so no target-manifold structure enters the argument. From a bundled stationary Sobolev witness `StationaryW12LocMap u Omega` it proves, for `0 < s <= r < R0`, that the normalized energy `Theta(Du, a, rho) = rho^(2-n) * integral over B(a, rho) of |Du|^2` is monotone: `weakTheta Du a s <= weakTheta Du a r`, together with the exact increment formula `weakTheta Du a r - weakTheta Du a s = weakMonotonicityRhs Du a s r`. The Sobolev layer is project-defined from Mathlib's `MemLp`, weak-derivative identities, Bochner integration, and Euclidean measure theory, following the De Giorgi-Nash-Moser engineering choice; the internal proof routes through a radial vector-field first variation, a coarea/Radon-Nikodym radius representation, smooth radial cutoffs, and an absolute-continuity boundary step.

informal.LeanStationaryHarmonicMaps.StationaryHar: The public input package: a domain-variation stationary `W^{1,2}_{loc}` Sobolev map bundling a chosen weak gradient (`W12LocMapWitness`) with the vanishing domain first-variation identity. This is the object users construct to invoke the monotonicity theorem.

Witness-style monotonicity: from a stationary `W^{1,2}_{loc}` map package, the normalized weak energy `weakTheta` is monotone in the radius, `weakTheta Du a s <= weakTheta Du a r` for `0 < s <= r < R0`.

Witness-style monotonicity formula: the increment of `weakTheta` equals the nonnegative annular radial-energy term, `weakTheta Du a r - weakTheta Du a s = weakMonotonicityRhs Du a s r` for `0 < s < r < R0`.

Componentwise convenience wrapper: the same monotonicity inequality stated directly from the local `L^2`, measurability, weak-gradient, and first-variation hypotheses, without first constructing the witness package.

records.title: The optimal exponent relating sumsets and difference sets
records.abstract: For a finite integer set A with at least two elements, proves that C(A) = log(|A+A|/|A|) / log(|A-A|/|A|) is strictly below 2, while explicit finite sets have exponents tending to 2. Thus 2 is the supremum and is never attained. Also gives an explicit witness within 10^(-999) of 2. This imports the upstream base-39 row-and-column variant, not the paper's base-12 automaton construction or its quantitative cardinality estimates. Supporting infrastructure includes injective digit expansions and the strict Pluennecke-Petridis equality argument for finite integer sets.

informal.SumDifferenceExponent.growthExponent_lt_: For every finite set A of integers with at least two elements, log(|A+A|/|A|) / log(|A-A|/|A|) is strictly less than 2.
informal.SumDifferenceExponent.tendsto_growthExpo: The growth exponents of the explicit finite integer sets approximatingSet l converge to 2 as l tends to infinity; these sets have at least two elements whenever l is positive.
informal.SumDifferenceExponent.isLUB_admissibleEx: The number 2 is the least upper bound of the growth exponents of all finite integer sets with at least two elements.
informal.SumDifferenceExponent.sSup_admissibleExp: The supremum of the growth exponents of all finite integer sets with at least two elements equals 2.
informal.SumDifferenceExponent.supremum_not_attai: No finite integer set with at least two elements has growth exponent equal to 2.
informal.SumDifferenceExponent.quantitative_examp: The explicitly defined finite integer set quantitativeSet has growth exponent strictly between 2 - 10^(-999) and 2.

records.title: Sums of Three Squares
records.abstract: Formalizes a blueprint step in the three-squares theorem using quadratic forms and geometry of numbers.

informal.LeanPool.SumsThreeSquares.blueprint_case: Proves the mod-8-equals-3 blueprint case for the three-squares theorem.

records.title: Sundog certificates
records.abstract: A referee-free, axiom-clean Lean development of coding-theory certificates: syndrome decoding soundness and lossiness bounds for GF(2) parity-check schemes (with a Reed–Solomon evaluation-dual variant), and a fully machine-checked correctness proof of the Karp reduction chain 3SAT ≤ 3DM ≤ X3C ≤ bounded-weight syndrome decoding. Only the logical iff of each reduction is formalized; polynomial-time bounds, NP classes, and Cook–Levin are unformalized external inputs, so NP-hardness of decoding is conditional on those standard facts.

informal.Sundog.SATReductionMain.sat_iff_decodes: The end-to-end reduction correctness: a formula is satisfiable iff its image under the composed 3SAT-to-decoding reduction is a yes-instance of bounded-weight syndrome decoding.
informal.Sundog.MatchingNPHard.threeDM_iff_X3C: The 3-dimensional matching instance has a perfect matching iff the reduced exact-cover-by-3-sets instance has an exact cover, both directions machine-checked.
informal.Sundog.Certificate.accept_sound: Soundness of the cheap syndrome-decoding verifier when it accepts: an exhibited light same-syndrome witness certifies the body is safe within the decoding radius.
informal.Sundog.Certificate.reject_sound: Soundness of the verifier when it rejects: a sound column-weight lower bound on the minimum same-syndrome weight rules out every light witness, so the body is genuinely unsafe.

records.title: Synthetic Euclidean geometry: Euclid's Elements Book I
records.abstract: Formalizes Book I of Euclid's Elements via an axiomatic synthetic-geometry system (incidence, betweenness, congruence, and area), culminating in the Pythagorean theorem and its converse.

informal.SyntheticEuclid4.IncidenceGeometry: The axiomatic class of synthetic Euclidean geometry, bundling points, lines, circles, and the incidence, betweenness, congruence, and area primitives with Euclid's axioms.
informal.SyntheticEuclid4.square_of_len: Constructs a square on a given segment off a given line.
informal.SyntheticEuclid4.pythagoras_construct: Constructs the three squares and parallelograms on the sides of a triangle used in the proof of the Pythagorean theorem.
informal.SyntheticEuclid4.pythagoras: Euclid I.47, the Pythagorean theorem, that the square on the hypotenuse of a right triangle equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.
informal.SyntheticEuclid4.pythagoras_converse: Euclid I.48, the converse of the Pythagorean theorem, that a triangle whose square areas satisfy the Pythagorean relation has a right angle.

records.title: The Three-Gap (Steinhaus) Theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes the three-gap (Steinhaus, three-distance) theorem: for every real `a` and every `N`, the `N`-point orbit `{i·a mod 1 : i < N}` partitions `[0,1)` into gaps taking at most three distinct lengths, and when exactly three occur the largest is the sum of the other two. The proof works in `[0,1)` via `Int.fract` (not `AddCircle`) through the two first-return times `η⁺` and `η⁻`, and is uniform in the rotation number, covering rational and irrational `a` with no case split.

informal.SteinhausThreeGap.three_gap_card_le_thre: For every real `a` and natural `N`, the gaps of the orbit `{i·a mod 1 : i < N}` take at most three distinct lengths.
informal.SteinhausThreeGap.three_gap_lengths_eq: When the gaps take exactly three distinct lengths, those lengths are precisely the two first returns `η⁺`, `η⁻`, and their sum `η⁺ + η⁻`; in particular the largest gap is the sum of the other two.

records.title: Turán's theorem (the "Book" weighting proof)
records.abstract: Formalizes the weighting/optimization proof of Turán's theorem from Proofs from THE BOOK, bounding the number of edges of a p-clique-free simple graph by (1/2)(1 - 1/(p-1)) n².

informal.Turan3.turans: Turán's theorem — a p-clique-free simple graph on n vertices has at most (1/2)(1 - 1/(p-1)) n² edges.
informal.Turan3.finale_bound: For any weight distribution on a p-clique-free graph, the total edge weight is at most ((p-1)(p-2)/2)·(1/(p-1))², the bound used to derive the edge count.
informal.Turan3.Better_forms_clique: Starting from any weight function, the minimal-support weight-non-decreasing improvement has support that forms a clique.
informal.Turan3.Enhance_total_weight_stricinc: Equalizing weights between a maximum- and minimum-weight vertex in the clique support strictly increases the total edge weight.

records.title: Ulm's theorem for countable reduced abelian p-groups
records.abstract: Formalizes Ulm's classification theorem for countable reduced abelian p-groups in arbitrary Lean universes. The development constructs the transfinite Ulm filtration and invariants, proves their invariance under additive equivalence, establishes Kaplansky's one-generator extension lemma, and completes the countable back-and-forth classification. A finite-group regression distinguishes Z/4 x Z/4 from Z/2 x Z/8 at the zeroth Ulm invariant.

informal.UlmsTheorem.ulm_theorem: For any prime p and any two countable reduced abelian p-groups in the same arbitrary Lean universe, the groups are additively isomorphic if and only if all of their classical Ulm invariants, indexed by universe-zero ordinals, agree.
informal.UlmsTheorem.iso_of_ulm_invariants: Equal Ulm invariants at every universe-zero ordinal imply an additive equivalence between countable reduced abelian p-groups, via finite height-preserving partial isomorphisms and a back-and-forth limit.
informal.UlmsTheorem.ulmInvariant_iso_invariant: An additive equivalence preserves every classical Ulm invariant.
informal.UlmsTheorem.UlmDifferentialRegression.no: The groups Z/4 x Z/4 and Z/2 x Z/8 are not additively isomorphic; the proof exercises the classification theorem and independently detects their different zeroth Ulm invariants.

records.title: Unconditional Schauder Bases
records.abstract: Develops an API for Schauder bases and unconditional Schauder bases of complete normed spaces, including ordered partial-sum convergence, rearrangement criteria for unconditionality, and an arbitrary-index variant built on unconditional summability, then proves a finite sign criterion: a family with dense closed span, nonzero vectors, and a uniform finite sign bound is the basis of an unconditional Schauder basis.

informal.UnconditionalCriterion.exists_unconditio: Finite sign criterion for sequences: if `x : ℕ → E` has dense closed linear span, every `x n` is nonzero, and finite sign changes are uniformly bounded by `C`, then `x` is the basis sequence of an unconditional Schauder basis.

Abstract-index form of the finite sign criterion: under the same dense span, nonzero, and uniform finite sign bound hypotheses for an arbitrarily indexed family, there is an abstractly indexed unconditional Schauder basis whose basis family is exactly `x`.

records.title: Virasoro Project
records.abstract: Formalizes the Virasoro algebra, its Witt-algebra central extension, Verma modules, and the basic bosonic Sugawara construction.

informal.VirasoroProject.VirasoroAlgebra: Defines the Virasoro algebra as a one-dimensional central extension of the Witt algebra.
informal.VirasoroProject.sugawaraRepresentation: Constructs the basic bosonic Sugawara representation of the Virasoro algebra from locally truncated Heisenberg actions.

records.title: Mean-field derivation and well-posedness of the Vlasov equation
records.abstract: Formalizes the mean-field limit, Dobrushin stability, and forward-in-time well-posedness for the Vlasov equation via Wasserstein-1 optimal transport.

informal.Vlasov.vlasovWellPosedness: Forward-in-time existence of a Lagrangian solution to the Vlasov equation on any finite horizon, for interaction forces that are Lipschitz gradients of an even pair potential (class AssW) — with no smallness restriction on the Lipschitz constant.
informal.Vlasov.dobrushin: A Wasserstein-1 form of Dobrushin's 1979 stability estimate (the original uses a truncated metric) - two Lagrangian Vlasov solutions with finite first moments at every time separate at most at an exponential Gronwall rate.
informal.Vlasov.meanFieldLimit: Conditional mean-field limit - given Wasserstein-1 convergence of the initial empirical data and a uniform Dobrushin stability estimate for the empirical curves, the N-particle empirical measures converge to the Vlasov solution uniformly on any finite horizon.
informal.Vlasov.weak_isLagrangianVlasovSolutionOn: On a time window with L * T^2 < 1, a weak solution with the standing regularity (even C^2 pair potential AssW2, finite first moments, narrow continuity, time-continuity of the convolution force at each point, continuity of the convolution-derivative field, and a uniform spatial first-moment bound on the window) is Lagrangian - the pushforward of its initial datum along the characteristic flow.

records.title: The Wallace problem in ZFC
records.abstract: Formalizes in ZFC a Hausdorff countably compact group topology without nontrivial convergent sequences on every torsion-free Abelian group of cardinality continuum. It specializes the construction to the rational direct sum and the additive real group, and derives a commutative Tychonoff countably compact cancellative semigroup that is not a group.

informal.Wallace.torsionFreeAbelianGroup_mainTheo: Every torsion-free Abelian group of cardinality continuum admits a Hausdorff countably compact group topology with no nontrivial convergent sequences.
informal.Wallace.continuumRationalGroup_and_real_: Both the continuum-indexed rational direct sum and the additive group of real numbers admit such Hausdorff countably compact group topologies without nontrivial convergent sequences.
informal.Wallace.commutativeTychonoffWallaceCount: There exists a commutative Tychonoff countably compact topological semigroup with two-sided cancellation which is not a group.

records.title: Whitehead's theorem for CW-complexes
records.abstract: Formalizes Whitehead's theorem — a continuous map between CW-complexes that induces isomorphisms on all homotopy groups is a homotopy equivalence — including the supporting theory of CW-complexes, relative homotopy groups, the homotopy extension property, and compression of maps.

informal.WhiteheadTheorem: Proves that a continuous map between CW-complexes inducing isomorphisms on all homotopy groups is a homotopy equivalence.

records.title: Irrationality of the Riemann zeta function at five
records.abstract: Proves that Mathlib's Riemann zeta function at five is an irrational real number, following Aabir Fauzan's September 2026 preprint. Constructs integer polynomials of degree 37n with positive values at zeta(5) that decay exponentially in n squared. Includes a general integer-polynomial irrationality criterion, Hankel determinant and moment-integral identities, logarithmic-energy estimates, prime-adic integrality bounds, and kernel-checked rational certificates. The formalization uses a different normalizer and a positive decay constant in place of the paper's specific constant 139/5. Reuses the prime number theorem infrastructure already in the MooreBound project.

informal.Zeta5Irrational.irrational_five: There exists an irrational real number x whose complex coercion equals Mathlib's Riemann zeta function evaluated at five.
informal.Zeta5Irrational.main_estimate: There is a positive real c such that, for all sufficiently large n, an integer polynomial Q of degree 37n is a positive rational multiple of the constructed determinant polynomial and satisfies 0 < Q(zeta(5)) < exp(-c*n^2).
informal.Zeta5Irrational.irrational_of_eventually: A real xi is irrational if, eventually, integer polynomials of degree at most d(n) have positive values at xi bounded by epsilon(n), and b^d(n)*epsilon(n) tends to zero for every positive natural b.

records.title: Thakur's hypotheses on power sums of F_q[t]
records.abstract: Formalizes four components of Thakur's hypotheses on power sums over finite polynomial rings, including uniqueness and monotonicity results for the carry-free digit optimization problems and the Laurent-series expansion of finite-field power sums.

informal.ZetaH123.H1.main_theorem: Proves uniqueness of the admissible base-q decomposition maximizing the H1 power-sum weight functional.
informal.ZetaH123.H2.main: Proves the H2 unique-minimizer statement for the recursive digit/carry-free optimization problem defining the values s_d(k).
informal.ZetaH123.H3.main_theorem: Proves the H3 monotonicity statement that s_d(k) is strictly less than s_d(k+1) when p does not divide k.
informal.ZetaH123.Lem41.main: Proves the Lemma 4.1 Laurent-series expansion for S_d(k), with nonzero coefficients indexed by the carry-free tuples.

records.title: Simple zeros of the Riemann zeta function
records.abstract: Formalizes Lamzouri's Hilbert-space proof of lower bounds for simple and distinct zeros of the Riemann zeta function. From explicit Riemann--von Mangoldt and unconditional pair-correlation hypotheses, the development proves that eventually more than 67.25% of nontrivial zeros are simple and on the critical line and more than 83.625% are distinct. It includes the finite-multiset Hilbert-space inequality, zeta-zero multiplicity symmetries, an admissible cutoff construction, and certified trigonometric estimates.

informal.ZetaZeros.simple_proportion_d4: Assuming the stated Riemann--von Mangoldt and unconditional pair-correlation formulas, beyond some height more than 67.25% of nontrivial zeta zeros are simple and lie on the critical line.
informal.ZetaZeros.distinct_proportion_d5: Under the same two explicit analytic hypotheses, beyond some height more than 83.625% of nontrivial zeta zeros are distinct.
informal.ZetaZeros.card_simpleRealPart_lower: Bounds from below the number of multiplicity-one real points in a finite nonempty conjugation-invariant multiset using the squared test-kernel sum of any admissible function.
informal.ZetaZeros.card_lower: Bounds from below the number of distinct points in a finite nonempty conjugation-invariant multiset using the same Hilbert-space kernel method.

records.title: Irrationality of ζ(3)
records.abstract: Formalizes Beukers' proof of Apéry's theorem for ζ(3), including the integral identities, denominator estimates, positivity, upper bounds, and final irrationality contradiction.

informal.LeanPool.Zeta3Irrational.linear_int: Clears denominators in the Apéry integral to produce a linear form in 1 and ζ(3).
informal.LeanPool.Zeta3Irrational.JJ_pos: Proves positivity of the transformed Beukers-Apéry integral.
informal.LeanPool.Zeta3Irrational.JJ_upper: Bounds the Beukers-Apéry integral by a geometric factor times the ζ(3) series.
informal.LeanPool.Zeta3Irrational.fun1_tendsto_ze: Shows that the denominator-cleared Apéry linear forms tend to zero.

records.title: ZFLean
records.abstract: Develops a practical ZFC set-theory framework with von Neumann naturals, integers, rationals, functions, embeddings, isomorphisms, booleans, and sums.

informal.ZFSet.isIso_of_biembedding: Proves a Cantor-Bernstein theorem for ZF sets.
informal.ZFSet.ZFNat.induction: Provides induction for the von Neumann natural numbers.
informal.ZFSet.ZFInt.induction: Provides induction for the quotient construction of ZF integers.

records.title: The Zhang-Yeung non-Shannon information inequality
records.abstract: Formalizes the Zhang-Yeung inequality, the first known non-Shannon-type entropy inequality, together with its dual and averaged forms derived through the copy lemma.

informal.ZhangYeung.zhangYeung: Proves the Zhang-Yeung non-Shannon-type information inequality for four discrete random variables.
informal.ZhangYeung.zhangYeung_dual: Proves the dual form of the Zhang-Yeung inequality.
informal.ZhangYeung.zhangYeung_averaged: Proves the averaged symmetric form of the Zhang-Yeung inequality.

records.title: elliotglazer/erdos501
records.abstract: Erdős problem #501 (Erdős 1961; Erdős–Hajnal 1971, Problem 38): for every real x let A_x be a bounded set of reals of Lebesgue outer measure < 1; must there be an infinite independent set, i.e. an infinite X ⊆ ℝ with x ∉ A_y for all distinct x, y ∈ X?  And if the sets A_x are closed of measure < 1, must there be an independent set of size 3?  This repository formalizes both answers.  Second question: yes — closed sets of measure < 1 admit an infinite independent set (Newelski–Pawlikowski–Seredyński 1987; no boundedness is needed), hence one of size 3.  First question: independent of ZFC.  Under CH (as ℵ₁ = 𝔠) Hechler's 1972 construction gives a family of bounded sets of outer measure < 1 (in fact countable and null) with no infinite independent set — a Mathlib-level theorem — and the negation of the first question holds in the Boolean-valued model of the collapse algebra Col(ω₁, 𝒫(ω)); after adding 𝔠⁺ random reals (Glazer and Sol 2026, adapting the paper's ω₂ random reals over a CH ground) the first question has a positive answer, so it holds in the Boolean-valued model of the random algebra with 𝔠⁺ coordinates.  Both Boolean-valued models are built in a Lean 4 port of Han–van Doorn's Flypitch (the framework of their independence-of-CH proof), and Flypitch's completeness theorem turns them into two-valued models.  The comparator challenge states the results in Mathlib alone: the language of set theory, the theory ZFC (Flypitch's axiomatization: extensionality, empty set, ordered pairs, union, power set, infinity, regularity, Zorn's lemma, strong collection) and the sentence Erdos501 ("every complete ordered field has the Erdős property") are defined in Mathlib's ModelTheory, and independence is stated semantically as ¬ (ZFC ⊨ᵇ Erdos501) ∧ ¬ (ZFC ⊨ᵇ ∼Erdos501); a faithfulness theorem shows that in Mathlib's ZFSet the sentence is equivalent to the Mathlib statement of the first question, verbatim the proposition of google-deepmind/formal-conjectures.  All targets are proved from propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only.  As far as we know this is the first Erdős problem whose resolution is a formally verified independence result.

records.title: A proof of the Regts–Sevenster conjecture, formalized
records.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of the Regts–Sevenster conjecture. A complex-valued graph parameter, normalized at the empty graph and invariant under isomorphism, has exponentially bounded edge-connection rank if and only if it is a mixed partition function. For a natural rank base R, a representing model can be chosen with k even and 2ℓ odd colours satisfying k + 2ℓ ≤ R. The development also proves the even connection-rank growth limit, minimum total colour dimension, minimal parity formulas and prescribed-dimension criterion. Schrijver's factorial argument supplies nilpotent-trace vanishing; semisimplicity and Deligne's fibre-functor theorem give the model; a polynomial commutant estimate gives the sharp colour budget. Deligne's theorem and the required symmetric-group character theory are proved within the development. The appendix's trace-zeta results give rationality and degree bounds, with an independent proof of nilpotent-trace vanishing. The theorems of record use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, checked by pinned audits.

records.title: rwst/Even-Integral
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib development of a paper, which improves on a problem by Dubickas. Dubickas (Glasgow Math. J. 48 (2006), 331–336) splits the reals α > 1 in two: α lies in 𝒵 when some real ξ ≠ 0 makes every integral part ⌊ξαⁿ⌋, n ≥ 1, even, and in 𝒮 otherwise. At α = 3/2 this is Mahler's question, and open; his Problem 5 asks whether 𝒮 has an element greater than 2. This formalization decides 𝒮 versus 𝒵 for every quadratic Pisot number: the golden mean is the only one in 𝒮, so none greater than 2 lies there and Problem 5 loses its whole natural class of candidates, though the problem itself stays open. The case that had resisted the source paper's four constructions is α = 1 + √2, settled by an exact computation rather than an estimate: with ξ = (2−√2)/4 one has ⌊ξ(1+√2)^(n+1)⌋ = Pₙ − [n odd] for the Pell numbers P, so every integral part is even. The mechanism generalizes: for a real quadratic pair with second conjugate in (−1,0), the closed-form multiplier ξ = −β/(α−β) makes m divide ⌊ξαⁿ⌋ for every n ≥ 0 whenever m ∣ a and m ∣ b−1 — an exact congruence, not a confinement of fractional parts — and all but finitely many of those integral parts are then composite. The informal account is the companion paper doi:10.13140/RG.2.2.20582.79689. Credit divides as follows, in contributor terms rather than bibliographic ones: the mathematical discovery and the formalization are the AI agent's; the agent also drafted the prose of the companion paper, which the author revised; the direction and the review are the author's, who is responsible for the mathematical content. Bibliographic authorship of the paper is the author's alone — the agent is credited in its Acknowledgements, not in its byline, as is usual for an AI tool. There is no sorry outside the deliberate placeholders in Challenge.lean, no project-defined axiom, no native_decide, and Mathlib is the only Lake dependency.

records.title: lennrt/palomar-formalizations
records.abstract: A kernel-checked certificate for the finite mathematical core of the paper's explicit 16-vertex counterexample. The compared declarations prove cubicity, bipartiteness, connectivity after every deletion of at most two vertices, Hamiltonicity of the displayed cycle, its exact complementary perfect matching, the displayed oriented facial incidence and dual data, Euler's equality, properness and uniqueness up to global permutation of the face coloring, the induced edge-color classes, their unavoidable intersections with the complementary matching, and the instantiated final obstruction. The topological realization of the incidence data as a sphere embedding and the published algorithm's Property 1 remain external inputs.

records.title: lennrt/palomar-formalizations
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of the paper's standard finite-word semantics for k-uniform two-word π-representability, its neighbourhood-trace bound binomial(k(|A|+1),k)^2, the explicit 20-by-741322 bit-incidence graph B20, and the theorem that B20 is not representable by two 2-uniform words. It also retains the companion's token-order bridge and exact arithmetic endpoints.

records.title: lennrt/palomar-formalizations
records.abstract: Lean formalization of the paper's finite skew-symmetric path instance, exact prefix-deletion completion oracle, deterministic oracle-pruned DFS, correctness and duplicate-freedom, and an executable DFS event trace whose extracted first-output, inter-output, post-output, and no-output work intervals satisfy the paper-level depth/LCP bounds.

records.title: lennrt/palomar-formalizations
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of Lemma 7.1 and the outer-matrix content of Theorem 7.2 for generalized cubic subdivision. It defines the naturally indexed 28n by 28n outer matrix row-by-row from the authenticated released MATLAB masks, including all previous/current/next-sector references. It constructs the paper's explicit topological permutation, proves that the first 24n coordinates are strictly upper triangular and that the remaining diagonal components are n scalar 1/64 blocks and n copies of the displayed 3 by 3 core, and proves unconditionally for every n at least 3 the characteristic polynomial X^(24n)(X-1/64)^n(X-1/32)^n(X-1/16)^n(X-1/8)^n.

records.title: lennrt/palomar-formalizations
records.abstract: A concrete formalization of the infinite-family construction in the source: cycle and Cartesian-product distances on P_m □ C_(6m), the displayed landmarks (0,0), (0,2m), and (m-1,0), the four-piece cycle distance-pair locus, and injectivity of the resulting unordered multiset code for every even m at least 2. This establishes the three-landmark resolving upper bound. It does not formalize the separate general lower bound needed to conclude that the set is a basis or that the multiset dimension equals 3.

records.title: rwst/Square-Roots
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib development of a paper, which answers a problem by Dubickas. Dubickas (Glasgow Math. J. 48 (2006), 331–336) splits the reals α > 1 in two: α lies in 𝒵 when some real ξ ≠ 0 makes every integral part ⌊ξαⁿ⌋, n ≥ 1, even, and in 𝒮 otherwise. At α = 3/2 this is Mahler's question, and open; his Problem 3 asks whether √3 lies in 𝒮 or in 𝒵. This formalization settles that question and the whole square-root slice: √3 ∈ 𝒵 by an explicit ξ = 1.34160899796…, and for an integer m ≥ 2 one has √m ∈ 𝒮 exactly when m = 2. The cells √5, √6, √7, √8 put four explicit points of 𝒵 in the interval (2,3), the only interval where an answer to Dubickas's Problem 5 could live; they are formalized (SZ.exists_mem_MahlerZ_Ioo_two_three) but are not separately compared, being subsumed by the compared Theorem B. The mechanism is not Diophantine approximation but the arithmetic of Cantor sets, and rests on the triviality that √m² = m is an integer: splitting n into even and odd values turns the one orbit into two base-m orbits coupled by x + √m y = σ, and a covering induction — Utz's 1951 theorem on the distance set of the Cantor discontinuum at m = 3, proved here for every base and every modulus — solves that equation inside the restricted-digit set. The same machinery at a general modulus gives, for p ≥ 2 and non-square m ≥ 3 in either of two explicit ranges, a real ξ ≠ 0 with p ∣ ⌊ξ√mⁿ⌋ for every n ≥ 1, hence integral parts that are composite from some point on; and the greedy's branching shows the witnesses for √3 have cardinality 2^ℵ₀, so all but countably many of them are transcendental. The informal account is the companion paper doi:10.13140/RG.2.2.32215.43682. Credit divides as follows, in contributor terms rather than bibliographic ones: the mathematical discovery is the Fable-5 agent's; the formalization is the Fable-5 and Opus-5 agents'; the agents also drafted the prose of the companion paper, which the author revised; the direction and the review are the author's, who is responsible for the mathematical content. Bibliographic authorship of the paper is the author's alone — the collaboration is credited in its Acknowledgements, not in its byline, as is usual for an AI tool. There is no sorry outside the deliberate placeholders in Challenge.lean, no project-defined axiom, no native_decide, and Mathlib is the only Lake dependency of the development itself.

records.title: rwst/Confinement-Certificates
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib development of a paper on the emptiness theory of the sets Z_{p/q}(s, s+t) = {ξ > 0 : {ξ(p/q)ⁿ} ∈ [s, s+t) for all n ≥ 0}, the generalized Z-numbers of Flatto, Lagarias and Pollington, at and beyond the window length 1/p. The paper introduces block certificates --- finite integer witnesses, rechecked from scratch by the Lean proof kernel, whose soundness rests on the aperiodicity lemma alone --- and uses them to pass the length-$1/p$ line: $\Zset_{3/2}(1/6,13/24)=\emptyset$ (window length $3/8>1/3$), $\Zset_{3/2}(961/3600,2427/3600)=\emptyset$ (length $733/1800$), and explicit unions of total length up to $17/24$, against $20/39$ in print. The closed-interval union statement of Dubickas is replicated exactly as printed; no $\xi\ne0$ keeps $\|\xi(3/2)^{n}\|<1/5$ for every $n$, with $\|\cdot\|$ the distance to the nearest integer; and thirty windows of length $1/p$ are certified at five bases in the regime $p>q^{2}$ that Dubickas leaves open. There is no sorry anywhere outside the deliberate placeholders in Challenge.lean, no project-defined axiom, and no native_decide: every block certificate is discharged by `c.ok = true := by decide`, i.e. by kernel reduction of integer arithmetic on the certificate's raw data.

records.title: Three Sharp Bounds for Hansen Polytopes of Cographs
records.abstract: A Lean 4/Mathlib formalisation of three sharp lower bounds for Hansen polytopes of finite nonempty cographs: normalized Mahler volume at least one, at least 3^d nonempty faces, and at least 2^d d! full flags in dimension d. In each result equality holds exactly for threshold graphs.

records.title: Polylogarithmic Descent for Almost All Collatz Orbits in Natural Density
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of four strengthened almost-all results for shortcut and raw Collatz orbits in ordinary natural density: critical polylogarithmic descent with arbitrary positive divergent target and height multipliers, centered trajectory tubes, and actual first-passage clocks; the fixed-exponent common-landing theorem with the exact upper exceptional-rate endpoint; an explicit reciprocal-order lower bound forced by the joint height ceiling; and a quantitative stretched-logarithmic common-landing theorem with smaller relative-height ceilings. These are almost-all statements and do not prove pointwise Collatz convergence.

records.title: BSCAveraging
records.abstract:
Three theorems about binary channels on a doubly symmetric binary source: a pair (𝑋, 𝑌) of
Bernoulli(1/2) bits with P(𝑋 ≠ 𝑌) = 𝑝, together with Markov chains 𝑈 - 𝑋 - 𝑌 - 𝑉 in which 𝑈
and 𝑉 are the outputs of two independent binary channels applied to 𝑋 and to 𝑌. Let 𝒜 be the
set of rate triples (𝑅₀, 𝑅₁, 𝑅₂) with 𝐼(𝑈;𝑋) ≤ 𝑅₁, 𝐼(𝑌;𝑉) ≤ 𝑅₂ and 𝑅₀ ≤ 𝐼(𝑈;𝑉) attainable by
arbitrary binary channels on the two sides, and ℬ the same set with both channels restricted
to be binary symmetric.

(1) conv 𝒜 = conv ℬ for every 𝑝 in [0,1]. (2) At 𝑝 = 0, no pair of binary channels whose rates
do not exceed those of the Z-channel with parameter 𝑎 and the S-channel with parameter 𝑑
attains a larger 𝐼(𝑈;𝑉) than that pair does. (3) At 𝑝 = 0, no pair of binary channels whose
rates are at least those of the Z-channels with parameters 𝑎 and 𝑑 attains a smaller 𝐼(𝑈;𝑉)
than that pair does. Here 𝑎, 𝑑 range over (0,1).

records.title: Refined Arbitrary-Target Transport Through Collatz Endpoints
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of a quantitative stability theorem for the one-block endpoint-pullback operator of the shortcut Collatz map. If an arbitrary target set has at most C N^(1-D) exceptions among the positive integers up to N, then, for every central Renyi order 1/2 < theta < 1, every admissible fixed central window, and every positive transport coefficient below the explicit asymptotic slope, its pullback through one floor(log_2 n)-step endpoint is (K(1+C^(theta/(1+theta)))D^(-theta/(2(1+theta))), transport*D)-dense whenever D is sufficiently small. The cutoff and K depend only on the fixed moment and transport parameters, not on the target set or C,D.

records.title: ukiyois/hs-virial-nbc-identity
records.abstract: A kernel-checked Lean formalization of the exact no-broken-circuit volume identity for hard-sphere Mayer cluster integrals and the stronger dimension-three fork-packing upper bound for each tree-owned NBC region. The development proves finite broken-circuit cancellation, the measurable finite-region decomposition, the anchored Euclidean product-measure theorem, and its explicit flat-coordinate transport.  Its geometric result is the attachment-aware estimate Vol(NBC_T) <= (17/32)^hardSphereNu T * hardSphereKappa^(k-1), where hardSphereNu T is the maximum cardinality of a packing of pairwise vertex-disjoint, order-compatible forks in T.  A formal fork is an ordered triple (a,b,c) with a < b < c, center a, leaves b,c, and tree edges {a,b} and {a,c}.  The central contribution is the complete pointwise-to-integral bridge together with the orientation-aware measure-preserving factorization that realizes the per-fork volume suppression.

records.title: Lean formalization toward Bugeaud Problem 10.61
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib development of criteria for Bugeaud's Problem 10.61 ([Bug12, p. 222], due to Mendès France [MF67]): for a Pisot number α > 2 and the Cantor set C(α) = {(α−1) Σ_{k≥1} ε_k α^{−k} : ε_k ∈ {0,1}}, no ξ ∈ C(α) has (ξαⁿ)_{n≥1} uniformly distributed modulo one. The problem is open; what is proved here are criteria for it and two instances. Every compared statement that concludes Problem 10.61 does so for a *quadratic* setup — a real root α > 1 of X² − aX − b whose conjugate has modulus below one — and the two instances are quadratic; the arbitrary-degree material is conditional ingredients, from which no compared statement derives non-equidistribution. Seventeen statements are compared, in four groups. (A) The reduction to symbolic dynamics is an equivalence, and it is complete. (i) Some ξ ∈ C(α) is u.d. mod 1 iff the full two-shift {0,1}^ℤ carries a shift-invariant Borel probability measure whose push-forward under an explicit factor map F is Lebesgue measure on 𝕋. (ii) 10.61 holds at α iff a finite certificate witnesses it: a mean-zero real trigonometric polynomial G on 𝕋 and a c > 0 with ∫ G∘F dμ ≥ c for every invariant μ. (iii) The pressure bracket that makes such a search terminate, −c/β ≤ ∫ g dμ over every invariant μ whenever the pressure of −βg relative to a finite partition is at most c. (B) A pressure criterion. (ii) A bounded measurable potential annihilated by every counterexample measure, an entropy floor h_min for those measures, and a partition pressure below h_min together prove 10.61 at α; and its machine form, where the potential carries a finite-state transfer bound with an integer vector certificate, the hypothesis comparing the log of the certificate ratio, less the Lebesgue mean, against h_min. (iv) The budget identity A(α)·h_min(α) = log 2, tying the Route A exponent to the floor. (C) A covering criterion for quadratic setups, and arbitrary-degree ingredients. (i) Two real inequalities — the depth slope 1 + L/R − L is negative exactly when (L−1)(R−1) > 1, and at the balanced depth M′ = ⌈M·L/R⌉ the covering total obeys an explicit logarithmic bound linear in M with that slope — and then, for a quadratic setup, a numeric certificate at depths (M, M′) yielding one open interval J ⊆ (0,1), uniform in ξ and in n, that every orbit misses at every time, whence A(α) < 1 implies 10.61 at α. (ii) For a quadratic setup of norm −b, the criterion applies exactly when (log₂ α − 1)(log₂(α/|b|) − 1) > 1. This characterizes when A(α) < 1; it does not decide Problem 10.61 for quadratic α with A(α) ≥ 1, about which nothing is compared. (iii) Three ingredients about the family Xᵈ − aXᵈ⁻¹ − 1, valid at every degree d ≥ 2: for a ≥ 3 the real root exceeding a is a Pisot number; every other conjugate has modulus at most (2/a)^{1/(d−1)}; and the numerical inequality log 2/log α + log 2/log(1/ρ) < 1 holds whenever a ≥ 2^{d+1}, a < α, ρ > 0 and a·ρᵈ⁻¹ ≤ 2. These are ingredients, not a criterion: no compared statement carries them to Problem 10.61 above degree two, because (i) is proved only for quadratic setups. At degree two the family members are quadratic setups, and the first of them is α = 2+√5. (D) The two numbers at which the machinery is run to a conclusion, both quadratic: at α = 2+√5 the strong form — an explicit interval missed by every orbit at every time — and 10.61 itself; and at α = 2+√3, 10.61 by a confinement-gap certificate. The informal account is the repository's paper.pdf: machine-written notes documenting the Lean development, not a prior paper that the development formalizes. Credit in contributor terms rather than bibliographic ones: the mathematics and the Lean text are the agents' work, the Fable-5 agent having written the notes and the Opus-5 agent the formalization, each directed turn by turn by Ralf Stephan, who chose the targets, selected which outputs to keep, and releases the files. He does not endorse the informal arguments and has not independently verified informal-to-formal fidelity; where the prose disagrees with the challenge file, the challenge file wins. Every compared statement depends on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound and nothing else.

records.title: Levi–Civita connections and metric-determined curvature invariants in Lean
records.abstract: Formalizes a coherent static Riemannian theorem family for smooth finite-dimensional manifolds: existence of a global C^1 Levi–Civita covariant derivative, independence of the bundled curvature tensor from the chosen Levi–Civita realization, symmetry of the Ricci contraction, and independence of both Ricci and scalar curvature from that realization. These are standard classical results assembled at the current Mathlib manifold/vector-bundle API boundary. The contribution claimed here is a kernel-checked Lean formalization of the theorem family and its bundled constructions, not a new mathematical discovery or a priority claim.
authors: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz

records.title: Mean Value for Random Ideal Lattices: Lean formalization
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of the geometric, analytic, and arithmetic argument for mean values of lattice-point counts in Haar-random unit-covolume ideal lattices. For cyclotomic fields, it proves the conditional quantitative estimate for every exponent below the assumed subconvexity exponent and its positive power-saving corollary, uniformly over origin-centered balls. The subconvexity, Stark residue, and discriminant-growth inputs remain explicit hypotheses rather than claimed consequences of the formalization.

records.title: The Kőnig–Egerváry Theorem on Matchings and Vertex Covers in Bipartite Graphs
records.abstract: A complete machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of the Kőnig–Egerváry Theorem (1931) and Gallai identities (1959). Proves strong min-max duality matchingNumber(G) = vertexCoverNumber(G) for 2-colorable graphs G via Hall's defect matching theorem, and formalizes Gallai's identity independenceNumber(G) + vertexCoverNumber(G) = |V(G)|. To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.title: A machine-checked bound of 0.6934 for Besicovitch's 1/2-problem
records.abstract:
Besicovitch's 1/2-conjecture asserts that a Borel set in the plane with finite one-dimensional Hausdorff measure whose lower density exceeds 1/2 almost everywhere is countably 1-rectifiable. Writing sigma_1(R^2) for the least threshold that forces countable 1-rectifiability, the conjecture is sigma_1(R^2) = 1/2. The previously published record is sigma_1(R^2) <= 7/10, obtained by De Lellis, Glaudo, Massaccesi and Vittone.
This development proves, with a complete Lean 4 proof term, sigma_1(H) <= 6934/10000 = 0.6934 for every real Hilbert space H, without finite-dimensionality or separability assumptions.

records.title: heilbronn-convex-3-8
records.abstract:
For n = 3 through n = 8, this formalization determines the supremal minimum triangle area among n indexed planar points whose own convex hull has Lebesgue area one. It proves a pointwise upper bound, attainment, and the exact value for every n in that range. The values are 1, 1/2, (5-sqrt(5))/10, 1/6, 1/9, and, at n = 8, the unique root in (79/1000, 81/1000) of 2060x^5 - 2332x^4 + 1064x^3 - 240x^2 + 26x - 1.
For n = 3, 4, 5, 6, and 8 it also proves pairwise uniqueness of optimizers modulo arbitrary relabeling and arbitrary nonsingular affine transformations. Uniqueness is false at n = 7; instead, an explicit real family is proved to attain throughout its full parameter interval and to exhaust all unit-hull optimizers up to the same equivalence. A real subinterval is pairwise inequivalent, exhibiting a continuum-parameterized set of optimizer orbits; an explicit countable subfamily is retained too.
The n = 3 and n = 4 cases are elementary folklore. The sharp n = 6 and n = 7 values were published by Dress-Yang-Zeng and Yang-Zeng, respectively; the Lean developments here independently reprove those results rather than formalizing the published arguments. The full n = 5 result, the explicit n = 7 family and optimizer classification, and the exact n = 8 result and optimizer classification are first presented in this development. The scoped search described below located prior candidate records but no published full n = 5 proof, no prior exhaustive n = 7 optimizer classification, and no published n = 8 proof. This is not an absolute priority claim. These results are intended for researchers in discrete and computational geometry studying extremal configurations, exact geometric bounds, and formalized combinatorial geometry.

records.title: Chip-Firing with Lean 4
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Baker and Norine's Riemann-Roch theorem for finite graphs. Chip configurations on a finite graph, modulo chip-firing moves, form an abelian group analogous to the group of line bundles on a compact Riemann surface. Each class can be assigned a rank, analogous to the dimension of a linear series. These ranks then satisfy a formula of the form r(D) - r(K-D) = deg D + 1 - g, in exact analogy to Riemann surfaces. This formula is formalized, along with the analog of Clifford's theorem for finite graphs.

records.title: The trace form of a tensor product of algebras and the signature product rule, with the trace forms of Q[x]/(x^3 - x - 1), Q[x]/(x^4 - x - 1) and their compositum as instances
records.abstract: GENERAL THEOREMS FIRST. For finite free algebras A, B over a commutative ring R, the trace form of the tensor product A ⊗_R B is the tensor product of the trace forms, and over a linearly ordered field the Sylvester signature of a tensor product of quadratic forms obeys a product rule. Seven compared general statements: (1) the trace of a pure tensor is the product of the traces, Tr_{A⊗B}(a ⊗ b) = Tr_A(a)·Tr_B(b); (2) the trace form on pure tensors is the product of the trace forms; (3) the Gram matrix of a tensor basis bA ⊗ bB (Mathlib's Basis.tensorProduct) is the Kronecker product of the two Gram matrices; (4) the discriminant product formula WITH SIGN, disc(bA ⊗ bB) = disc(bA)^|kappa| · disc(bB)^|iota| for bases indexed by finite types iota, kappa; (5) when 2 is invertible in R, the trace quadratic form of A ⊗ B is the tensor product (Mathlib's QuadraticForm.tmul) of the trace quadratic forms; (6)-(7) THE SIGNATURE PRODUCT RULE: over a linearly ordered field with 2 invertible, for quadratic forms Q1, Q2 on finite-dimensional spaces, sigPos(Q1 ⊗ Q2) = p1 p2 + n1 n2 and sigNeg(Q1 ⊗ Q2) = p1 n2 + n1 p2, with sigPos/sigNeg Mathlib's basis-free invariants (maximal dimension of a positive- resp. negative-definite subspace). (6)-(7) are the (p, n)-refinement of the multiplicativity of the signature homomorphism on the Witt ring of an ordered field (Lam 2005, Chapter VIII), stated for arbitrary (possibly degenerate) forms and proved by orthogonal bases and the uniqueness half of Sylvester's law. The Witt-ring statement gives only the difference p - n; recovering p and n separately for a possibly degenerate tensor product would in addition need the dimension of the radical of a tensor product, which Mathlib does not have either; the entry proves the two counts directly, without the Witt ring, which is not formalized. None of (1)-(7) was in Mathlib at the pin; Mathlib's nearest results are the trace of a tensor product of endomorphisms (LinearMap.trace_tensorProduct'), the determinant of a Kronecker product, the tensor product of quadratic forms and its polar form, orthogonal bases, and sigPos/sigNeg with Sylvester uniqueness — the infrastructure from which (1)-(7) are built. PRIOR ART on (4): Mathlib at the pin has NumberField.natAbs_discr_eq_natAbs_discr_pow_mul_natAbs_discr_pow — for two linearly disjoint number fields with coprime different ideals the ABSOLUTE VALUE of the discriminant of their compositum is |d1|^[K2:Q]·|d2|^[K1:Q] (via the different; the classical statement is in Khanduja 2019). Statement (4) is the elementary basis-level version: any finite free algebras over any commutative ring, the exact signed discriminant of the tensor basis, with no number-field, integrality or coprimality hypothesis; it neither implies nor is implied by the Mathlib theorem, and is cited beside it. THE INSTANCES (8)-(23), at the two fields cut out by the trinomials x^3 - x - 1 and x^4 - x - 1 — the cubic and quartic members of the family x^n - x - 1, irreducible over the rationals for every n >= 2 by Selmer's theorem (Mathlib), whose real roots above 1 are the plastic number and the quartic root of x^4 = x + 1 — and their compositum. The trace form of a number field K of degree n is (x, y) -> Tr(xy); in the power basis 1, x, ..., x^(n-1) its Gram matrix is the Hankel matrix (Tr x^(i+j)) of the power sums of the roots. (8)-(9) The Gram matrices, entrywise: Algebra.traceMatrix of the power family equals the explicit integer Hankel matrix — power sums 3, 0, 2, 3, 2 for the cubic and 4, 0, 0, 3, 4, 0, 3 for the quartic, from Newton's identities on the coefficients. (10)-(11) The discriminants of the power bases, Algebra.discr of the same families: -23 and -283, both prime. (12)-(13) Explicit diagonalisations: the trace form, as a quadratic form, is equivalent to the weighted sum of squares with weights 3, 2, -23/6 resp. 4, 4, -9/4, 283/36 — one congruence among many, exhibited with its rational change of basis. (14)-(17) The Sylvester signatures as basis-free invariants: sigPos and sigNeg are 2 and 1 for the cubic trace form and 3 and 1 for the quartic, read off from (12)-(13) through Sylvester uniqueness. (18)-(23) THE COMPOSITUM: the tensor product L = K_3 ⊗_Q K_4 is their compositum Q(rho, Q) — the degrees 3 and 4 are coprime, so the fields are linearly disjoint and L is a field, statement (23), from Mathlib's coprime-degree linear-disjointness criterion — and (18)-(22) are the general theorems at this pair: Tr(x ⊗ y) = Tr(x)·Tr(y); the Gram matrix of the tensor power family x^i ⊗ y^j (Fin 3 × Fin 4) is the Kronecker product of the two Gram matrices; the discriminant of that family is (-23)^4·(-283)^3 by (4); the Sylvester signature is (7, 5) by (6)-(7) applied to (2, 1) and (3, 1) — agreeing with the classical (r_1 + r_2, r_2) for the compositum's two real and five complex places (context, not compared). The registered compositum entry PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000005 treats the same field as Q(rho·Q), through the degree-12 minimal polynomial of the product; that Q(rho, Q) = Q(rho·Q) follows by degree count and is context here, never compared. THE CLASSICAL SETTING of the instances: the trace form of a number field with r_1 real and r_2 pairs of complex embeddings has signature (r_1 + r_2, r_2) — for the Hankel form of a polynomial this is Hermite's 1856 theorem (the signature difference counts the distinct real roots), and for the discriminant matrix of a number field it is Taussky's 1968 note; Conner and Perlis's 1984 survey is the standard reference. Here (r_1, r_2) = (1, 1), (2, 1) and (2, 5), so the classical theorem predicts exactly (2, 1), (3, 1) and (7, 5), and the Hermite counts 2 - 1 = 1 and 3 - 1 = 2 match the real-root counts of the two trinomials. That general theorem is NOT formalized: the two-field instances are proved directly by explicit congruence, the compositum instance by the general theorems (1)-(7); the embedding counts r_1, r_2 appear in no compared statement. WHY THESE FIELDS, for the instances: the cubic field is the signature-[1, 1] cubic field of smallest absolute discriminant (LMFDB, sorted by |disc|: 3.1.23.1 first, then 3.1.31.1); its Galois closure is the Artin field of the weight-one newform 23.1.b.a = eta(z) eta(23z), the classical Hecke example with Artin image S_3, whose analytic conductor the LMFDB records as minimal among all classical newforms and whose Stark unit is the root of x^3 - x - 1 itself; its integral trace form — which the compared Gram matrix (8) is, the power basis being an integral basis — is the object of Mantilla-Soler's study of integral trace forms of cubic fields (Algebra & Number Theory 2010). The quartic field is the degree-4 member of the same trinomial family, registered as the degree-4 Mahler-measure minimizer (PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004), with the same profile: prime discriminant, monogenic. The field discriminants: the LMFDB records 4.2.283.1 (defining polynomial x^4 - x - 1, signature [2, 1], discriminant -283, monogenic, index 1) and 3.1.23.1 (reduced defining polynomial x^3 - x^2 + 1, the field generated by -1/rho, signature [1, 1], discriminant -23, monogenic, index 1) list -283 and -23 as the field discriminants; that the power bases are integral bases, so that the compared power-basis discriminants ARE the field discriminants, is cited from those records and not formalized; likewise the tensor power family is an integral basis of the compositum because the two discriminants are coprime (the standard integral-basis theorem for linearly disjoint fields; context only). PRIOR ART on the instances, as of the 2026-09-02 sweep: Mathlib contains no trace-form or discriminant computation for either field. The nearest prior work is the Lean 4 certification framework of Baanen, Chavarri Villarello and Dahmen (CPP 2025) and its 2026 sequel (Chavarri Villarello and Dahmen): they certify rings of integers, FIELD discriminants (as the determinant of the trace matrix of a certified integral basis) and, in the sequel, the signature (r_1, r_2) by real-root counting, for LMFDB entries at large; neither treats the trace form's Sylvester signature, and their published example sets (seven non-monogenic cubic fields unramified outside 2, 3, 5 in the first; the v1 example directory of the second) contain neither of the two fields here (checked 2026-09-02). Relative to that work, the compared discriminants (10)-(11) are the power-basis discriminants derived from the explicit Gram matrices — a weaker notion than the certified field discriminant, which coincides with it here because both fields are monogenic (LMFDB, cited) — and the Sylvester signatures have no counterpart there. The entry is not aware of a formalization, in any surveyed prover ecosystem, of the trace form of a tensor product of algebras, of the signature product rule, or of a number field's trace-form Sylvester signature. The proof modules descend from the author's public pdt-lean development (pinned below), where none of these statements was ever a compared statement. Axioms on every compared theorem: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, audited in-build.

records.title: Ore's and Dirac's Theorems on Hamiltonian Cycles
records.abstract: A complete machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of Ore's theorem (1960) and Dirac's theorem (1952) on the existence of Hamiltonian cycles in simple graphs. Proves Ore's degree-sum condition via maximal path cycle-closure and connectivity arguments, and derives Dirac's minimum-degree theorem as a corollary. To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.title: A proof of Conway's refinement conjecture
records.abstract: A Lean proof of Conway's 1976 refinement conjecture for omnific integers. For omnific integers a, b, c, d with ab = cd, it proves the existence of omnific integers e, f, g, h satisfying a = ef, b = gh, c = eg, and d = fh, including zero and degenerate cases. The proof proceeds through factorisation and refinement theory for generalised-power-series integer parts and connects the generalised-power-series and surreal-number formulations.

records.title: Tverberg's Partition Theorem, 1D Theorem, and Colorful 1D Theorem
records.abstract: A complete, machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of Tverberg's Theorem (Helge Tverberg, 1966) in the distinct-point set formulation across dimensions d >= 1 (with d = 0, r > 1 cases vacuously satisfied due to Finset carrier capacity limits on Fin 0 -> ℝ) via the Sarkaria–Bárány Colorful Carathéodory reduction, the full 1D Tverberg theorem for arbitrary r via symmetric-rank pairing following Mulzer–Werner, and the 1-dimensional Colorful Tverberg Theorem for arbitrary r (Bárány–Larman–Pach 1992). Proves that any (r - 1)(d + 1) + 1 points in ℝ^d can be partitioned into r parts whose convex hulls intersect, and that two disjoint color classes of r points each in ℝ¹ can be partitioned into r colorful pairs whose convex hulls share a common point of intersection. To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.title: Radial harmonic functions on a real inner product space: the classification, the Laplacian of radial functions, and the stability of circular orbits for power-law central forces; Ehrenfest's dimensionality argument (1917) as the application
records.abstract: GENERAL THEOREMS FIRST. Throughout, E is a finite-dimensional real inner product space of dimension n, Δ is Mathlib's coordinate-free Laplacian, HarmonicOnNhd its harmonic functions, and f : ℝ → ℝ is twice differentiable on (0, ∞) (two HasDerivAt hypotheses, with derivatives f', f''). (I) THE CLASSIFICATION OF RADIAL HARMONIC FUNCTIONS: (1) for n ≠ 2 and E ≠ 0, the radial function f ∘ ‖·‖ is harmonic on E ∖ {0} if and only if f(r) = a + b r^(2−n) on (0, ∞) for some real a, b; (2) for n = 2, if and only if f(r) = a + b log r — every radial harmonic function with a twice-differentiable profile is an affine function of the Newtonian potential, constants included, and of the logarithm in the plane. (II) THE LAPLACIAN OF RADIAL FUNCTIONS, away from the origin: (3) Δ(f ∘ ‖·‖)(x) = f''(‖x‖) + (n − 1) f'(‖x‖)/‖x‖, the radial Laplacian; (4) for g twice differentiable on (0, ∞), Δ(g(‖y‖²))(x) = 2n g'(‖x‖²) + 4‖x‖² g''(‖x‖²), the squared-norm parametrization; (5) for every real s, Δ(‖y‖^s)(x) = s (n + s − 2) ‖x‖^(s−2), the indicial identity (its consequence, not itself compared: for E ≠ 0, ‖y‖^s is harmonic away from 0 exactly when s (n + s − 2) = 0, at s = 0 and s = 2 − n, which coincide at n = 2); (6) Δ(log ‖y‖)(x) = (n − 2)/‖x‖²; (7) ‖y‖^(2−n) is harmonic on E ∖ {0} for every n — for n ≥ 3, up to its normalizing constant, the Newtonian kernel away from the origin (the normalization and the distributional identity −ΔΦ = δ at the origin, in Evans's sign convention, which make a normalized multiple of it the fundamental solution proper, are NOT formalized); at n = 2 the power is the constant 1 and the logarithmic case is (8); on the zero space the statement is vacuous; (8) log ‖y‖ is harmonic on E ∖ {0} when n = 2. (III) THE RADIAL EQUATION, the one-variable content of (1)-(2): (9) for n ≠ 2, f'' + (n − 1) f'/r = 0 on (0, ∞) if and only if f(r) = a + b r^(2−n) there for some a, b; (10) for n = 2, if and only if f(r) = a + b log r. (IV) THE STABILITY OF CIRCULAR ORBITS, general in the real exponent: for the effective potential U(r) = a/r² − b/r^p on (0, ∞), a, b > 0, p > 0 real — the radial potential of a body with angular momentum under a central attraction with force law 1/r^(p+1) — (11) U'(r) = 0 iff r^(2−p) = 2a/(bp), the circular-orbit condition (for p ≠ 2 that equation has exactly one positive solution, whence "the circular orbit" below — a consequence of (11), not itself compared; in the plane "the circular orbit r = √(2a/b)" names the point of (19)); (12) at a circular orbit U''(r) = 2a(2 − p)/r⁴; (13) for p < 2 the circular orbit r* = (2a/(bp))^(1/(2−p)) is a local minimum of U (Mathlib's non-strict IsLocalMin) — stable; (14) for p > 2 it is a local maximum — unstable; (15) for p > 2 U has no local minimum on (0, ∞) at all (Ehrenfest's reading, that bounded motion between two radii is then impossible, is not formalized); (16) U''(r*) r*⁴/(2a) = 2 − p, the square of the ratio of the radial to the angular frequency of small oscillations about the circular orbit, which the local step of Bertrand's argument requires to be the square of a rational number for a near-circular orbit to close. The boundary p = 2, where the two terms of U have the same power, is covered by the critical-point and second-derivative identities (11)-(12), whose only hypothesis on the exponent is p > 0, and is excluded from the stability conclusions (13)-(15) and the frequency identity (16), all of which require p ≠ 2; among the instances it is n = 4, where (17) with a ≠ b yields no local minimum (the potential (a − b)/r² has no critical point) while the sub-case a = b, where U vanishes, is excluded; the table's 'unstable' cell at n = 4 is not compared. THE INSTANCES (17)-(23), with p = n − 2 for the Newtonian potential in n ≥ 3 dimensions and the logarithmic potential in the plane: (17) for n ≥ 3 and a ≠ b a stable circular orbit exists iff n = 3 (a ≠ b excludes n = 4, a = b, where U vanishes identically and every point is a non-strict minimum); (18) for n ≥ 5 the effective potential has no local minimum on (0, ∞); (19) in the plane, for a/r² + b log r, the circular orbit r = √(2a/b) is stable; (20) the quantity of (16) is 4 − n for n ≥ 3, n ≠ 4, hence 1 at n = 3; (21) in the plane it equals 2; (22) in the plane its square root is irrational (it is √2 by (21); this statement asserts irrationality only); (23) ‖x‖^(2−n) is harmonic on ℝⁿ ∖ {0} for every n; for n ≥ 3, up to its normalizing constant, the Newtonian kernel away from the origin, with the same disclosure as (7). THE APPLICATION: Ehrenfest's argument of 1917 (KNAW Proceedings 20 (1918) 200-209, §1 and Appendix I) that the stability of planetary orbits singles out three spatial dimensions.
