He deduces the n-dimensional force law from the Laplace–Poisson equation (the Laplace half is statement (7), harmonicity away from the source; the Poisson half, the point source, is not formalized; the classification (1)-(2) makes "the radial harmonic function" a theorem), reduces the motion to the radial equation ṙ = (1/r)√(A r² + B r^(4−n) − C²), and tabulates three columns — circular trajectories; motions between two positive values of r; motion to the infinite — for n ≥ 4 (unstable, impossible, possible), n = 3 (stable, possible and moreover closed, possible), n = 2 (stable, possible and not closed, impossible). Statements (17)-(22) are the extrema and frequency identities of the effective potential behind the first two columns for n ≥ 5, n = 3, n = 2 — a local minimum where the table says stable, no local minimum where it says bounded motion is impossible, the frequency ratio where it says closed or not closed; the passage from those identities to trajectories (bounded motion, closure, the third column), the n = 4 cell, and Bertrand's global theorem (1873) are not formalized. Tangherlini (1963) extended the argument to the n-dimensional Schwarzschild field; Caruso and Xavier (1987) and Tegmark (1997) discuss its epistemological status and call it Ehrenfest's argument, as does this entry ("Ehrenfest's theorem" names his 1927 quantum-mechanical result). NOT formalized: Bertrand's theorem, the third column and the n = 4 cell of the table, the derivation of the effective potential from the equations of motion, the relativistic extension, the wave-equation half of Ehrenfest's paper (Huygens' principle in odd dimensions), and any statement about the actual dimension of physical space — the theorems classify radial functions and a family of effective potentials; the reading that the stable case is the world we observe is Ehrenfest's, cited, not compared. PRIOR ART, as of the 2026-09-02 sweep: Mathlib has the Laplacian on inner product spaces (InnerProductSpace.laplacian, laplacian_eq_iteratedFDeriv_orthonormalBasis), harmonic functions (HarmonicAt, HarmonicOnNhd, harmonicAt_congr_nhds) with complex-analytic examples — in particular AnalyticAt.harmonicAt_log_norm, which gives log |z| harmonic on ℂ ∖ {0}, the n = 2 case of (8) in the complex model obtained through complex analysis — the second- derivative test (isLocalMin_of_deriv_deriv_pos), the mean-value lemmas IsOpen.exists_is_const_of_deriv_eq_zero and IsOpen.exists_eq_add_of_deriv_eq, and real powers; it has no Laplacian of a radial function, no harmonic power of the norm, no classification of radial harmonic functions, no central-force mechanics, and no formalization of Ehrenfest's argument. No formalization of the classification of radial harmonic functions, of Ehrenfest's argument, of the harmonic Newtonian potential in general dimension, or of Bertrand's theorem was found in the surveyed prover ecosystems (Mathlib and its archive, the Isabelle AFP, the Coq Mathematical Components and Coquelicot analysis libraries). The proof module descends from the author's public pdt-lean development (pinned below), where none of these statements was ever a compared statement. Axioms on every compared theorem: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, audited in-build.

records.title: Sharp bounds for intervals in finite subgroup lattices
records.abstract: Let H be a subgroup of a finite group G, let n = [G:H] > 1, and let p be the least prime divisor of n. This Lean development proves an exact finite rational upper envelope for the number of subgroups K with H ≤ K ≤ G and the strict bound c(p) n^((log_p n)/4), where c(p) is an Euler-product times a Gaussian theta series. It formalizes the bandwise moment inequality that drives the proof, a universal base-two bound with an exact decimal coefficient, the exact optimal answer for prime-power indices, and elementary-abelian asymptotics showing that both the constant and the exponent 1/4 are optimal.

records.title: Erdős Problem 684: f(n)/log n is unbounded — a Lean 4 formalization of arXiv:2604.23784
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization, against Mathlib, of the main theorem of J. H. Bae, "Unbounded logarithmic limsup in Erdős Problem 684 via shifted carry scheduling" (arXiv:2604.23784, v3).  For 0 ≤ k ≤ n write C(n,k) = u·v with u supported on the primes ≤ k and v on the primes in (k,n], and let f(n) be the least k with u > n²; Erdős asked for bounds on f(n) (Problem 684 in Bloom's database).  The compared theorems state that for every ε > 0 there are infinitely many n with f(n) > (1/2 − ε)·log n·log log n / log log log n, equivalently limsup f(n)·log log log n /(log n·log log n) ≥ 1/2 (stated in the extended nonnegative reals), and in particular that f(n)/log n is unbounded, so no estimate f(n) = O(log n) holds.  This strengthens the subsequential lower bound (1/2 − o(1)) log n of Alexeev–Putterman–Sawhney–Sellke–Valiant by a factor of order log log n / log log log n; the general upper bound (log n)² remains the best known and the exact order of f(n) is open.  Two further compared statements fix the meaning of the definitions: u(n,k) times the part of C(n,k) supported on primes exceeding k equals C(n,k), and K < f(n) holds exactly when u(n,k) ≤ n² for all 1 ≤ k ≤ min(K,n).  The proof follows the paper section by section (Kummer carries, a product-cell code, a CRT count with exponential weighting, an anchored-fibre selection lemma, and a four-range carry budget).  The prime number theorem is the single analytic input: the library proves the theorem under the explicit hypothesis θ(x) = x + O(x/log² x) and then discharges that hypothesis from the bound ψ(x) = x + O(x·exp(−c(log x)^{1/10})) of the PrimeNumberTheoremAnd project (Kontorovich, Tao et al.), so the compared theorems carry no hypotheses and depend only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.title: Tucker's Lemma: Full Combinatorial & Topological Parity Suite in 1D and 2D
records.abstract: A complete machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of Tucker's Lemma (Albert W. Tucker, 1945) and the combinatorial Borsuk–Ulam theorem in 1D and 2D without artificial conditions. Formalizes four foundational pillars: (1) 1D discrete sign-change parity and antipodal interval subdivision lemma; (2) 2D combinatorial double counting of face doors and modulo-2 parity conservation on edge-pseudomanifolds; (3) the boundary cycle engine on 2D edge-pseudomanifolds with an enumerated cyclic boundary (CyclicBoundaryPseudomanifold2D) under antipodal boundary labeling, proving that non-complementary boundary labelings force odd boundary door parity, thereby establishing the 2D Tucker's Lemma on cyclic boundary pseudomanifolds, retracting previous claims of full topological disk coverage; and (4) the concrete 6-vertex, 8-face, 12-edge octahedral 2-sphere S^2_8 triangulation. All declarations rely strictly on standard Lean 4 kernel axioms (propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice).

records.title: Even-order Grünschloß–Keller permutation nets: net property and tiling distance
records.abstract: This Lean development proves that the even-order permutation construction of Grünschloß and Keller (MCQMC 2008 proceedings, implemented in gendiag0m2.h) is a base-2 (0,m,2)-net for every even m >= 4. The proof is symbolic: for every resolution a <= m the dyadic-box map is shown injective through the concatenation x = floor(k/4) + 2^(m/2-2) z and fixed-width bit-reversal splitting, and a cardinality argument upgrades injectivity to a bijection (exactly one point per elementary interval). For the source's row-shifted tiling lattice <(N,0),(N/4,N)> it proves, for every even m >= 8, that one explicit pair of points has squared distance 241 * 2^(m-8), and at m = 8 that 241 is the exact minimum over all pairs and all lattice translates. The exhaustive m = 8 lower bound is reduced by ordinary kernel decide; the exactness of the computed candidate minimum over the whole lattice is a symbolic lemma. The all-parameter lower bound of the distance theorem (even m >= 10) is proved in the paper but is not formalized.

records.title: Combinatorial core of the K₃,₃,₁-redundancy theorem for tetrahedral balls
records.abstract: Alexa's three-dimensional Tutte embedding theorem (Discrete & Computational Geometry, 2025) requires the graph of a tetrahedral mesh to have neither a K₆ nor a K₃,₃,₁ minor and asks whether the second exclusion is necessary. The paper proves that it is redundant for finite simplicial complexes whose realization is a closed topological 3-ball and which satisfy the boundary-triangle condition (BT): if the 1-skeleton G has no K₆ minor, then G is linklessly embeddable and hence has no K₃,₃,₁ minor (Theorem 1.1). This Lean development proves the paper's new combinatorial mathematics over mathlib simple graphs and finite simplicial complexes and composes it into Theorem 1.1 with the cited theorems as explicit hypotheses. Proved: for every four-clique of a (BT) pair the induced relative F₂ chain complex has homology of dimension at most one (Lemma 4.3, with the soundness of its Boolean coordinate model, Lemma 7.1); a K₄-attachment never merges components of the old part (Lemma 5.2); every MP₁-cockade whose four-clique deletions leave at most two components is linklessly embeddable, given the four-clique Holst–Lovász–Schrijver criterion and linkless atoms (Proposition 5.3); and the joined statement structural_theorem, in which the skeleton of the complex is a mathlib SimpleGraph, every skeleton four-clique is a labelled four-clique of the pair, and the hypotheses are Corollary 3.6 (rigidity, Mader, Jørgensen), the relative ball duality of Section 4, Corollary 2.5, and Lemma 5.1. Generic rigidity, the extremal-minor classification, PL duality, the Holst–Lovász–Schrijver theorem, apex linklessness, and Alexa's theorem are not formalized and enter only as named hypotheses.

records.title: A kernel-checked exclusion certificate for Erdős Problem 647, to 10^8
records.abstract:
Erdős Problem 647 asks whether there is any n > 24 with max_{m < n} (m + tau(m)) <= n + 2, where tau counts divisors. The value n = 24 satisfies it and the question is open. This entry certifies a bounded exclusion: no such n exists in (24, 10^8]. It does not resolve the problem and asserts nothing about n > 10^8.
The exclusion is certified rather than searched at check time. A witness at a cover position is an offset together with prime-power pairs dividing m, certifying tau(m) >= prod (e + 1); every prime in a pair is below 1024 and is checked prime by eleven trial divisions, so no primality certificates appear anywhere. A chain of witnesses covers the interval and each certificate chunk is discharged by a single decide against the chain checker, so the Lean kernel certifies the arithmetic and the generator that produced it is never trusted.
The audience is the community working on the Erdős problems database and its Lean formalizations, for whom a machine-checked lower bound on the search range is directly usable, and researchers building certificate-based exclusions in elementary number theory, for whom the witness format and its kernel-evaluable checkers are the transferable part.

records.title: Sharp arithmetic separation in chiral Padovan histories
records.abstract: Sixteen compared statements establish quantitative recurrence for the actual infinite Padovan prefix path and compare cubic and quartic arithmetic record windows. For 0<epsilon<=1, every nonempty prefix whose conjugate coordinate lies within epsilon of the origin has expanding coordinate at least epsilon^(-2); an actual prefix returns with expanding coordinate at most r^3*epsilon^(-2). Every letter stream satisfies the pairwise bound abs(Delta X)*norm(Delta W)^2>=1, and Padovan substitution stages attain equality at arbitrarily large clocks. The full cubic record window is relatively dense with uniformly discrete differences; the identical positive-real window in the quartic case admits nonzero inverse-unit points arbitrarily close to zero, while its other real embedding grows. Scalar prefix coordinates factor the included faithful chiral timelike history in the genuine quartic trace geometry. The formalization exposes the return bounds, actual-word attainment, constructive covering, and explicit obstruction as its principal mathematical consequences.

records.title: Carlet's Kasami cyclic-additive conjecture
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of the Kasami cyclic-additive conjecture introduced by Claude Carlet. For the derivative image of the Kasami monomial x^(4^k-2^k+1) with gcd(k,n)=1, over a finite field of characteristic two with 2^n elements, the formalized result gives the exact three-variable coefficient count 2^(2n-3) for every pair of distinct nonzero coefficients.

records.title: Brill--Noether generality and gonality for chains of cycles and theta graphs
records.abstract: This repository formalizes Brill--Noether generality for chains whose factors may be cycles or theta graphs, subject to a genericity condition on path lengths and an evenly-marked condition on the theta factors. A graph is called Brill--Noether general if the possible degrees and ranks of its chip configurations, in the sense of Baker and Norine, match the behavior of a general algebraic curve. Here we use only the existential form of Brill--Noether generality, without computing dimensions. Following Cools--Draisma--Payne--Robeva, we also formalize a mild vanishing-order condition that permits the recovery of dimension statements on the algebraic side. A Brill--Noether general graph also has the conjectural maximum gonality in its genus. The chain of cycles case is a theorem of Cools--Draisma--Payne--Robeva, which Pflueger--Solomon generalized to allow evenly-marked theta graphs. Among other things, the construction shows the existence, in every positive genus g, of graphs with every gonality between 2 and ceil(g/2) + 1, inclusive.

records.title: The optimal universal exponential base for Euclidean kissing numbers
records.abstract: For every positive integer n, the Euclidean kissing number tau_n is an attained maximum and satisfies tau_n <= (sqrt(6))^n. This Lean formalization proves the bound by packing explicit bodies of revolution in the unit ball, including the geometric separation, volume integrals, and every dimension case. An explicit six-point planar configuration proves tau_2 = 6. Consequently sqrt(6) is the least nonnegative (and least positive) universal exponential base without a prefactor; the admissible bases are exactly alpha >= sqrt(6), and the supremum of tau_n^(1/n) over positive dimensions equals sqrt(6). No asymptotic-optimality claim is made.

records.title: N4Code: optimal finite-length block codes of size four for binary symmetric channels
records.abstract: A Lean 4 and mathlib formalization of the Dong-Yang classification of optimal (n,4) binary block codes for binary symmetric channels.  The registered results are Theorems 1-5 of the paper: existence of an optimal linear or Class-I code, the explicit linear optimal codes by residue class modulo 3, the universal strict-improvement reductions outside the linear, Class-I, and Class-II classes, the Class-I condition reduction to linear codes, and the finite classification for blocklengths 2 <= n <= 8. The Lean statements use the strict-improvement contrapositive forms.

records.title: Exact four-dimensional projection quality of the OneTwo Sobol' table at 65,536 points
records.abstract: The quality parameter t of a base-2 digital net with 2^m points measures exact equidistribution in dyadic boxes, and for Sobol' sequences used in quasi-Monte Carlo integration and computer graphics the quality of low-dimensional projections is a practical bottleneck. The OneTwo construction of Bonneel, Coeurjolly, Iehl, and Ostromoukhov (ACM Transactions on Graphics, 2025) releases a 692-dimension direction-number table whose protected pairs (2k-1, 2k) have the (1,2) property, with acceptance targets t <= 3 through m <= 10 and t <= 4 through m <= 15 for the pair-aligned four-dimensional blocks. Theorem 1.1 of the preprint determines the next depth exactly: at m = 16, a complete batch of 65,536 points, every one of the 345 pair-aligned windows of the released table has exact four-dimensional t-value 4 when its first dimension is one of 1, 7, 31, 49, 67, 195, 225, 243, 373 and t-value 5 otherwise, so the t <= 4 guarantee extends to m = 16 in exactly nine windows and fails in the other 336, each failure witnessed by an empty dyadic box of volume 2^-12 in that projection. The standard star-discrepancy bound for the projection is 299/4096 at t = 4 and 29/256 at t = 5. This Lean development proves the theorem in rank form with the released table embedded as one 256-bit literal per dimension: for every window, every four-part composition at the threshold total selects independent generator rows over F_2 and some composition one total higher does not, and the distribution is 9 windows at t = 4 and 336 at t = 5. The worked block, dimensions 25 to 28, keeps its separate explicit certificate (t = 5, with every smaller threshold refuted). All checks are 16-column XOR row reductions reduced by kernel decide with no native evaluation. The digital-net rank criterion, the discrepancy bound, and the authentication of the upstream table remain informal.

records.title: Li's criterion for the Riemann Hypothesis
records.abstract: Li's criterion for the Riemann zeta function, formalized in Lean 4 over Mathlib: Mathlib's `RiemannHypothesis` holds if and only if every Li-Keiper coefficient of the completed xi function has nonnegative real part. The zero-indexed analytic coefficient at n is Li's classical lambda_(n+1), the n-th Taylor coefficient at 0 of the logarithmic derivative of s |-> xi(1/(1-s)). A second compared theorem identifies this analytic coefficient with Li's arithmetic coefficient, the symmetrized sum over the nontrivial zeros counted with multiplicity, and proves that symmetrized family summable so the sum is the genuine one. Both results are unconditional: the biconditional, the coefficient identification, the genus-1 Hadamard factorization of xi (with multiplicity), genus-1 summability of 1/|rho|^2, and the growth bound order(xi) <= 1 are all proved. This is a formalization of a classically known equivalence (X.-J. Li, 1997); it is not a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, nor of the positivity of the coefficients.

records.title: The global Kronecker–Weber theorem in Lean 4
records.abstract: This project formalizes the global Kronecker–Weber theorem in Lean 4: every finite abelian extension of the rational numbers embeds into a cyclotomic field. For a number field L that is abelian Galois over the rationals, the selected declaration gives a positive integer n and a rational algebra embedding from L into CyclotomicField n ℚ. The proof is supplied by the ClassFieldTheory library at a fixed commit, using Lean 4.33.0 and Mathlib.

records.title: Stafford 3.8
records.abstract: Lean formalization of Stafford's Conjecture 3.8 for every characteristic-zero field and every Weyl-algebra rank, proving that each nonzero d admits F, R, and S with 1 = d*R + F*d*S. The development also proves an exact Bernstein-degree fixed-source strengthening and derived localization, adjoint, and evolutionary results.

records.title: Convex geometry and the Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv problem: Theorem 1.2
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of Theorem 1.2 of Dmitrii Zakharov's Convex geometry and the Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv problem. For every fixed positive dimension d, as p tends to infinity through the primes, the Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv constant s(F_p^d) satisfies s(F_p^d) = p w(F_p^d) + o(p), where w is the weak Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv constant.  Supporting proofs include the convex-flag Helly and centerpoint theorems, flag decomposition lemma, balanced convex combinations, relative set expansion, and the polynomial method bound for w. This submission covers Theorem 1.2 and its upper-bound formulation, not every result in the paper. The submission was prepared with the assistance of ChatGPT 5.6 / 6 Sol-Ultra under the direction and review of the author.  The GitHub page includes a PDF file zakharov_2026-3.pdf containing a revised version of the published paper generated  by ChatGPT 5.6 during this formalization project.  The only noteworthy difference is a correction to Definition 4.6 (Proper points) which was meant to use the function f^circ(q) in  place of \hat f(q) in the published version (this typo slipped in during one of the revision rounds of the paper). No other significant mistakes or corrections were discovered.

records.title: The sharp finite-field Nikodym exponent
records.abstract: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the sharp power saving in the finite-field Nikodym problem. A set N in F_q^d is a Nikodym set if through every point x there is a line all of whose points other than x lie in N. Lower bound: for every finite field F_q, every d >= 2 and every Nikodym set N in F_q^d, |N| >= q^d - (8 d^2 + 1) q^(d - 2^(1-d)); the proof goes through a carrier theorem for integral projective varieties containing many affine lines with private points, proved by finite-grid Hermite interpolation, Hilbert-function estimates (normalized monotonicity and a degree upper bound via linear Noether normalization), an interpolation cut, and a dimension induction that halves the saving at each step. Upper bound: for every d >= 2 and epsilon > 0 and all sufficiently large primes q there is a Nikodym set N in F_q^d with |N| <= q^d - q^(d - 2^(1-d) - epsilon), constructed as the complement of a product set built from a totally real multiquadratic order in which q splits completely, with a digit encoding and tangent lines. Together these give Nik(d, q) = q^d - q^(d - 2^(1-d) + o(1)) along primes. Previously, for general q and d >= 3, the best lower bound was q^d / 2^(d-1) + O(q^(d-1)) and even Nik(d,q) = (1 - o(1)) q^d was open (Lund-Saraf-Wolf, Conjecture 2), while the best upper bounds for prime q were q^d - Omega_d(q^(d - eps_d)) with eps_d << 1/log log d and q^3 - Omega(q^2.1167) (Hunter-Pohoata-Verstraete-Zhang 2026); the lower bound here settles the former conjecture for every finite field, and the construction shows that the exponent d - 1/d conjectured by Chao and Yu (2026) is not sharp over prime fields. The README gives theorem-level comparisons and references. All three headline theorems are proved with no sorry and depend only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.title: Spherical maximal functions: theorems of Stein and Bourgain
records.abstract: This is a Lean 4 formalization of Stein's spherical maximal theorem and Bourgain's circular maximal theorem. The result concerns the sharp range of Lp boundedness of spherical maximal functions in Euclidean space and was first proved by Stein in dimensions three and greater. The much more subtle two-dimensional theorem was first proved by Bourgain. The proof of Bourgain's theorem in this formalization is via Mockenhaupt-Seeger-Sogge's classical argument via a local smoothing estimate for the wave equation. This required first  formalizing various underlying standard results from harmonic analysis. The final theorem statements were written by hand,  while the proofs were almost entirely machine-generated by coding agents with human supervision.

records.title: Double-contracted second Bianchi identity for metric-compatible torsion-free connections
records.abstract: Proves the orthonormal double contraction of the actual corrected curvature derivative of a tangent connection on a smooth finite-dimensional real manifold. The Challenge exposes the corrected commutator and the smooth tangent-vector extensions explicitly; the Solution proves the identity for every supplied extension satisfying the stated hypotheses. The derivative symmetries and cyclic Bianchi equations are derived from torsion-freeness and metric compatibility, not assumed as abstract tensor data. No separate Einstein-divergence theorem is selected.
authors: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz

records.title: The density Hales–Jewett theorem and Szemerédi's theorem
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the density Hales–Jewett theorem: for every finite alphabet α and every density δ > 0, all sufficiently large n have the property that any set of at least δ·|α|^n words of length n over α contains a combinatorial line. The basis for the formalization is the combinatorial proof of Dodos, Kanellopoulos, and Tyros. As a consequence, we also formalize Szemerédi's theorem on the integers: for every k ≥ 3 and δ > 0, the following holds for all sufficiently large n. Any subset of {0, …, n−1} of size at least δ·n contains a nonconstant arithmetic progression of length k.

records.title: Marton's conjecture (the polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa conjecture)
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of Marton's conjecture, widely known as the polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa conjecture, together with its principal consequences. If A is a non-empty subset of an abelian group of exponent 2 with |A + A| <= K|A|, then A is covered by fewer than 2K^12 cosets of a subgroup of cardinality at most |A|; the same conclusion holds with 2K^9 cosets. For an abelian group in which mx = 0 for every x, with m >= 2, the covering number is m * K^(256m^3 + 1). Three consequences are also recorded: a finite set of small doubling in Z^D has a subset of at least K^(-34) of its size whose affine dimension is at most (80/log 2) log K; a map between finite groups of exponent 2 whose additive defects f(x+y) - f(x) - f(y) all lie in a set S differs from a homomorphism by a map taking at most |S|^10 values; and a map that is additive on at least a proportion 1/K of pairs agrees with a homomorphism on at least (|G| / (2^144 K^122) - 1)/2 points. The proofs are by an entropy method: one minimizes a functional of the entropic Ruzsa distance between two random variables and shows the minimum is attained at a uniform distribution on a subgroup, so the development also builds a substantial theory of Shannon entropy, entropic Ruzsa distance, and, for the bounded torsion case, a multidistance for m-tuples. The repository is a collaborative formalization project begun in November 2023; the mathematics is due to the cited papers and nothing here is claimed to be new. The compared theorems depend on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound and on nothing else, and there is no sorry outside the six deliberate holes in PFRPalomar/Challenge.lean.

records.title: Subspace embeddings with the rerandomized SRHT
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of a rerandomized SRHT subspace embedding theorem. For every ambient Walsh dimension n = 2^m, rank 1 <= r <= n, and 0 < epsilon < 1, one deterministic width k <= min(n, ceil(C r / epsilon^2)) can be chosen independently of the orthonormal frame. For each fixed frame, the transform with two independent uniform sign layers and an independent uniform k-subset has spectral failure probability at most 1/100, and preserves all squared norms in that subspace within 1 +/- epsilon with probability at least 99/100. C is an explicit universal constant, with no sharp numerical value claimed. The Comparator selects the spectral theorem and its fixed-frame squared-norm consequence. The full repository retains the 12 named v6 results and their supporting proofs and correspondence maps.

records.title: A proof of the Bollobás–Nikiforov conjecture in Lean
records.abstract: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Bollobás–Nikiforov conjecture (2007) and of the matrix theorems that prove it. Let G be a finite simple graph with adjacency eigenvalues lambda_1 >= lambda_2 >= ..., m edges and clique number omega(G). The conjecture states that every noncomplete graph on at least two vertices satisfies lambda_1^2 + lambda_2^2 <= 2 (1 - 1/omega(G)) m. The formalization proves it (BN.lambda1_sq_add_lambda2_sq_le) as a consequence of a weighted spectral inequality: for every symmetric entrywise nonnegative matrix B with zero diagonal supported on the edges of G, the sum F(B) of the squares of the two largest positive eigenvalues of B is at most (1 - 1/omega(G)) ||B||_F^2 (BN.weighted). The weighted inequality rests on a complete-positivity theorem for planar Gram matrices: if z_1, ..., z_n in R^2 lie in a closed half-plane through the origin and X is their Gram matrix, then M(X) = X o X + sum over i < j with X_ij < 0 of X_ij^2 (e_i - e_j)(e_i - e_j)^T is completely positive (BN.matrix_theorem), proved by an ordered elimination, a Schur complement identified as a weighted Laplacian plus a matrix with an explicit three-column nonnegative factorization, and total nonnegativity of two rectangular kernels. A variational argument then removes the half-plane hypothesis from the scalar inequality: for every real positive semidefinite X of rank at most two, sum_{i,j} (A_G)_ij (X_ij)_+^2 <= (1 - 1/omega(G)) ||X||_F^2 (BN.gram_le), which also identifies the rank-two conic parameter chi''_{vec,3}(G) of Coutinho, Spier and Zhang with omega(G) (BN.chiVec3_eq_cliqueNum), settling their Conjectures 2 and 3 without a lower bound on the clique number. Previously the conjecture was known for weakly perfect graphs (Ando–Lin), triangle-free graphs (Lin–Ning–Wu), regular graphs (Zhang), graphs with few triangles (Kumar–Pragada, Zeng–Zhang), asymptotically almost surely for random graphs (Liu–Bu), and with weaker constants for all graphs (Coutinho–Spier–Zhang). All five headline theorems are proved with no sorry and depend only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.title: Distance-shell tomography: product kernels and sharp grid sensing
records.abstract: General integer-trade criterion and full-factor Cartesian-product kernel/recovery theorem; the all-order grid lower bound; and, for every n ≥ 6, the complete four-parameter integer grid kernel, exact threshold n−2 for odd n and n−3 for even n, optimal n−2 sensor count throughout 2 ≤ h < threshold, and unique four-parameter description of equal-observation populations.

records.title: The rearrangement number: non(M) ≤ rr
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of the lower bound non(M) ≤ rr, where non(M) is the least cardinality of a nonmeagre subset of the usual real line and rr is the least cardinality of a family of permutations of the natural numbers that changes the sum or destroys convergence of every conditionally convergent real series. It accompanies the manuscript *Determining the Rearrangement Number* by Vinicius de Oliveira Rodrigues. The reverse inequality was already known in the literature. The reverse inequality, the full equality, and further manuscript corollaries are not formalized in this project.

records.title: Dimension-independent Hlawka constants for Schatten norms
records.abstract: Existence of a dimension-independent Hlawka constant for every Schatten p-norm with 1 < p < infinity, and proof that no such constant exists at either endpoint (trace norm at p=1, operator norm at p=infinity).

records.title: Ceiling orbits of rational bases are not P-recursive
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib development of the companion paper of the same name (doi:10.13140/RG.2.2.10727.82081). Fix coprime integers p > q ≥ 2 and an integer x₀ ≥ 1 and iterate the ceiling map of the rational base p/q, xₙ = ⌈p·xₙ₋₁/q⌉, with associated word wₙ = q·xₙ₊₁ − p·xₙ ∈ {0,…,q−1}, the correction that makes p·xₙ divisible by q. Four statements are compared. (A) The word of every such orbit is not P-recursive: it satisfies no nontrivial linear recurrence with polynomial coefficients. (B) At p/q = 3/2 the orbit itself is not P-recursive either; for x₀ = 1 it is the sequence A061419, which is therefore not holonomic. (C, D) neither generating function, Σⱼ wⱼzʲ nor Σₙ xₙzⁿ, is algebraic over ℚ(z). The Lean contains a proof of Stanley's algebraic-holonomic-p-recursive closure theorem.

records.title: Formalization of power weight inequalities for spherical maximal functions
records.abstract: This is a Lean 4 formalization of Theorem 1.1 from the paper "Power weight inequalities for spherical maximal functions" by Marco Fraccaroli, Joris Roos, and Andreas Seeger, arXiv:2602.17613. The formalized result concerns boundedness of  spherical maximal functions with arbitrary sets of dilations and radial power weights. The allowable exponent and weight ranges are characterized, apart from endpoint boundedness, by the Legendre-Assouad function of the dilation set. This resolved an open problem of Duoandikoetxea and Seijo up to endpoints. The main theorem statement in Lean was human-generated, while the formal proofs where machine-generated by coding agents under human supervision following the mathematical source directly.

records.title: The maximal difference theorem for s-numbers
records.abstract: A bound between all s-numbers (in the sense of Pietsch). The approximation  numbers a_n are the largest s-number sequence and the Hilbert numbers h_n  the smallest, so that h_n(S) <= s_n(S) <= a_n(S) holds for every s-number  sequence (s_n) and every bounded linear operator S between Banach spaces.  The formalized result gives a bound in the reverse direction:  a_n(S) <= ((n+1)^(n+1)/n^n) * h_n(S) <= e * (n+1) * h_n(S), for every bounded linear operator between normed spaces over the reals or the complex numbers. Hence, the same factor bounds the gap between any two s-number  sequences. The linear growth in n is order-optimal.  This is the main result of arXiv:2608.05024 and solves a problem of  Mityagin, Henkin (1963) and Carl, Pietsch (1978), up to a constant.

records.title: Native Lean finite Nash equilibria
records.abstract: Formalizes finite strategic-form games with player-specific finite move sets, pure profiles, unilateral deviations, best responses, dominant strategies, and two distinct potential notions. Pure Nash equilibrium is defined over utility preorders by the absence of a strict improvement; weak-inequality characterizations are restricted to linear orders. The library names the one-way improvement condition a generalized ordinal potential and reserves ordinal potential for the standard bidirectional strict-sign condition. It proves a global potential-maximizer certificate for pure Nash equilibrium, the standard Nash/local-potential-maximum equivalence, and acyclicity of the better-response relation for the generalized class. The development also gives checked counterexamples and Prisoner's-Dilemma/coordination/matching-pennies/rock-paper-scissors examples. Its native mixed layer proves support equalization, Dirac transport, the normalized excess-map reduction, and the closed/compact/ convex/continuous finite mixed-profile geometry. It also proves general finite mixed-Nash existence on a common nonempty move type by connecting the native excess map to an attributed, kernel-checked product-of-simplices Brouwer theorem. This is a reusable formalization artifact, not a claim of new mathematics or the first Lean proof of Nash existence.

records.title: A two-to-one executable map between Tunnell representation sets under the Tunnell balance
records.abstract: Let B(n) and A(n) be the integer solution sets of 2x^2 + y^2 + 8z^2 = n and 2u^2 + v^2 + 32w^2 = n, respectively. For every odd positive squarefree n satisfying |B(n)| = 2|A(n)|, we construct a deterministic computable map Phi_n : B(n) -> A(n) that sends exactly two source points to each target point. The construction combines an elementary even-coordinate map, three explicit quarter-turn correspondences, and a unique stable matching of the remaining antipodal orbits, with preferences determined by primitive midpoint directions. The map, its two-to-one property, the branch formulas, and the inverse identities for the residual map are formalized in Lean 4. Tunnell's theorem supplies the required counting identity for odd squarefree congruent numbers; its modular-form proof lies outside this formalization.

records.title: Hoeffding's extrema of the number of successes at a fixed mean
records.abstract: For n independent trials with success probabilities p_1, ..., p_n in [0,1] -- Poisson trials -- and S the number of successes, three results about how the law of S varies over all trial vectors with a given mean lam, with pbar = lam/n the common success probability of the homogeneous trials of the same mean. First, for g convex on the integer grid, E[g S] is maximised by the binomial, and under strict grid convexity equality holds exactly at the constant vector (Hoeffding's Theorem 3). Second, for arbitrary g with no convexity assumed, the maximum and the minimum of E[g S] over the fixed-mean box are attained at points whose coordinates take at most three distinct values, at most one of them strictly between 0 and 1 (Corollary 2.1). Third, away from the mean the binomial extremises the lower tail: for k >= lam the homogeneous vector has the lightest lower tail and for k <= lam - 1 the heaviest (two of the three regimes of Theorem 4). Every compared statement is written without any definition of its own: the probability model, the tail and the binomial comparator are expanded into raw Finset sums, products and filters from Mathlib, so that each claim can be audited against the informal statement without first accepting a definition.

records.title: Moh's P3 curve is a set-theoretic complete intersection
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization proving that the Moh curve parametrized by x=t^6+t^31, y=t^8, z=t^10 is cut out set-theoretically by two explicit equations over every characteristic-zero field. The development computes the polynomial and formal-power-series parametrization kernels, proves the radical equality for the two-generated witness ideal, and proves that the curve ideal has height two and arithmetic rank two, both globally and after completion.

records.title: gn-lean: the Gurvich–Naumova partition conjecture
records.abstract: A Lean 4 proof that for every nonnegative integer n, the distinct integers 1,...,n can be partitioned into nonempty sets of at most three elements, each having sum equal to a nonnegative integer power of three. This proves Conjecture 1 of Gurvich and Naumova, arXiv:2508.00946v3. The development constructs permutations with all prescribed nonzero displacements, derives signed zero-sum triple partitions, proves a contraction and complement-pair extension, and completes strong induction on n. All required finite certificates and unbounded sequence constructions are proved in Lean.

records.title: Dependent finite mixed Nash equilibria in Lean
records.abstract: A Lean-native formalization of finite mixed Nash equilibrium for games in which each player has its own finite, nonempty action type. The library defines dependent profiles and finite expected payoffs, proves support equalization and Dirac transport, establishes the closed/compact/convex mixed-profile geometry, and connects the normalized excess map to a checked product-of-simplices Brouwer theorem. It also proves the correspondence between ambient finite games with player-indexed legal action sets and dependent legal-action subtypes. This is a reusable formalization artifact, not a claim of new mathematics or priority.

records.title: De Lellis--Topping almost-Schur inequality
records.abstract: Formalizes the quantitative almost-Schur lemma on nonempty connected closed smooth Riemannian manifolds of dimension at least three with nonnegative Ricci curvature: scalar-curvature variance is bounded by 4*n*(n-1)/(n-2)^2 times the squared L2 norm of trace-free Ricci, with the Einstein equality characterization. The development constructs normalized Riemannian volume, solves the mean-zero Poisson problem variationally and upgrades it to a smooth representative, proves the actual integrated Bochner and contracted-Bianchi identities, and closes the sharp algebra.
authors: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz

records.title: Finite correlated equilibria and regret certificates
records.abstract: For finite games with player-specific action types, a valid independent product distribution is a correlated equilibrium exactly when its mixed profile is Nash. The correlated-equilibrium set is nonempty, compact, and convex when every player's action type is nonempty. For every positive finite horizon, cumulative external-regret and swap-regret bounds give corresponding approximate coarse-correlated and correlated equilibria of the empirical distribution. The development also proves equivalence with conditional obedience inequalities, arbitrary mixed-deviation sufficiency, and extension-by-zero correspondence for restricted legal actions. An exact per-recommendation certificate characterizes approximate correlated equilibrium without loss in its error budget and directly certifies empirical play from cumulative recommendation gains.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Verified regret matching and finite-time equilibrium computation
records.abstract: For finite nonempty action sets and unit-interval full-information payoffs, regret matching and regret matching+ have cumulative external regret at most the square root of the product of the number of actions and the horizon, against every fixed pure or mixed comparator. In finite two-player zero-sum matrix games, simultaneous self-play gives an explicit finite-time approximate Nash guarantee for uniformly averaged strategies. A finite-vector implementation is proved to reproduce the abstract averages. Square-root-free accuracy budgets and finite rational payoff inequalities certify approximate equilibria, including against all real mixed deviations. A four-round rational RM+ example has certified Nash error at most 19/260.

records.title: Erdős–Rado negative stepping-up for ordinal order types
records.abstract:
A Lean 4 formalisation of the Erdős–Rado negative stepping-up lemma in its order-type form, for arities three and above and for at least two colours.
Fix an ordinal kappa; a colour count mu ≥ 2; and a target order type theta = omega^alpha with alpha > 0, so that theta is additively indecomposable. The theorem proved is, for every natural number r: if some colouring of the (r+3)-subsets of kappa by ordinals below mu admits no monochromatic subset of kappa of order type theta, then some colouring of the (r+4)-subsets of 2^kappa admits none either, using the same number of colours.
The construction compares two unrelated orders on 2^kappa -- an arbitrary well-order, and the lexicographic order given by the first place two sets differ -- and reads a colouring off the pattern of agreement between them along a chain, together with the sequence of discrepancies. Two colours are spent marking the chains where those patterns first deviate, and on the well-behaved chains the colouring copies the given one along the discrepancy map.

records.title: A real affine (23_4) configuration
records.abstract: An explicit construction of 23 distinct points and 23 distinct straight lines in the real affine plane, with exactly four selected incidences at every point and every line. Lean verifies the construction using rational coordinates interpreted in the real numbers.

records.title: Sharp Bounds for Graph Matrices
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of matching polynomial and logarithmic orders for the norm of every fixed finite simple graph matrix in the globally injective dense independent-sign model. For each fixed positive real moment order p, the pth norm moment to the power 1/p is bounded above and below by positive shape-dependent constants times n^((h+i0-s)/2) log(2n)^(b*/2). Here h is the number of graph roles, i0 counts isolated interior roles, s is the minimum boundary-separator size, and b* is the maximum number of attached floating components over minimum separators. The expected-norm specialization and the half-integer logarithmic exponent are also proved.

records.title: Lichnerowicz--Obata first eigenvalue and round-sphere rigidity
records.abstract: Formalizes attainment of the first positive smooth Laplace eigenvalue on closed connected smooth Riemannian manifolds of dimension n >= 2, its sharp lower bound n*K under Ric >= (n-1)*K with K > 0, and equality if and only if the manifold is smoothly Riemannian-isometric to the round sphere of radius 1/sqrt K. The independent statement constructs the metric-compatible torsion-free connection and explicitly defines Ricci curvature, the Riesz gradient, the div-grad Laplacian, eigenvalue minimality, and the radius-scaled induced round metric.

records.title: Global Stafford
records.abstract: Lean formalization of the same-divisor identity 1 = d*R + F*d*S in the ring of k-linear finite-order differential operators of every smooth integral finitely generated algebra over a characteristic-zero field, extending Stafford's Conjecture 3.8 from Weyl algebras to smooth affine varieties.

records.title: Verified external-to-swap regret reduction and correlated-equilibrium solver
records.abstract: A finite Cesaro/Markov reduction turns one external regret learner per recommendation into a quantitative swap-regret bound. Applied to the pinned regret-matching and regret-matching+ algorithm, the development proves an approximate correlated-equilibrium guarantee for actual simultaneous play, with an explicit finite stationarity term. A rational refinement and exact coordination run make the construction executable.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Rerandomized Subsampled Trigonometric Transforms
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of a two-round real Walsh subsampled randomized Hadamard embedding. For every fixed d-dimensional real subspace of a Walsh space of dimension n, independent unbiased diagonal signs and a uniform sample of M distinct rows preserve every squared Euclidean norm within factors 1-epsilon and 1+epsilon with probability at least 1-delta. The prescribed M is at most n and at most [8192(1+432/delta)+1]d/epsilon^2. Thus, at any fixed failure probability, the embedding dimension is O(d/epsilon^2), the scaling asked for in Problem 5.6 of arXiv:2602.05394v3 for its Walsh model. The recorded Challenge/Solution declaration states the actual finite sampling law, transform, success event, and quantitative dimension bound.

records.title: Short-Cycle Decompositions and Full Zombie Damage in Cubic Graphs
records.abstract: For every finite simple connected bridgeless cubic graph G, the survivor can force full zombie damage if and only if G is not isomorphic to K4, K3,3, the triangular prism or the cube. In particular, for order n at least 10 this proves Randy Davila's Conjecture 24, zdmg(G)=n, with an explicit bound of 2n(n+1) survivor moves against every initial zombie position and every legal geodesic reply. The game formalization retains starting and turn order, survivor passes, capture and distinct-vertex damage, and proves the numerical payoff's connection to bounded and eventual strategies. The argument classifies short-cycle components, bounds their boundaries by four ports and composes metric exit and target routes into an ambient-graph strategy. Structural expansion corollaries and recurrent-coverage extensions accompany the characterization. The 39 selected results connect structural cubic-graph theory with extremal damage and worst-case strategies in graph pursuit. All proof sources are included in one Lake project.

records.title: KR-mod9-lean
records.abstract: Lean 4 proofs of the three Kanade-Russell identities modulo nine as identities of integer formal power series, including coefficientwise summability of the defining double sums. The development includes concrete vertex-operator spanning bounds and the character evaluations used to identify the sums with their infinite products.

records.title: Irreducible improper phi-regret in Lean
records.abstract: A Mathlib-only formalization of two explicit three-action improper phi-regret families in Section 4.4.1 of Dann, Mansour, Mohri, Schneider, and Sivan (COLT 2025). They are finite counterexample families for the paper's rate-preserving linear-reduction program. It proves valid-improper certificates, the affine-hyperplane invariant-transport core of Lemma 4, the extreme-point antipodal-displacement core of Lemma 5, a direct finite one-way affine action/loss-transfer-to-canonical bridge, a source-style two-direction affine linear-equivalence-to-canonical bridge in an explicit bijective-coordinate regime, finite-dimensional Equation-(15)-to-(16) and Equation-(16)-to-(17) bridges, and concrete Equation-(18) vertex/corner criteria. These mechanisms rule out the selected canonical, normalized, finite-loss-basis, homogeneous/affine-transfer, two-direction affine-equivalence, and finite-vertex/corner proper reductions for the two cited families.

records.title: Density-one prescribed-rank spectra of prime-cover graphs
records.abstract: For finite prime-cover graphs, the ordered adjacency eigenvalues at prescribed arithmetic ranks obey density-one squared-error estimates in every fixed power range 0 < theta < 1/2. Relative to the prime-counting main term and explicit first-exit correction, the error is bounded by a constant times a/log(X) + log(X)^D sqrt(X/(a log(X))), with quantitative terminal exception counts and zero limiting failure density. This gives a positive power improvement over the sqrt(X)/log(X) block bound. Separate sharp every-terminal-centre statements on 21/61 < theta < 1/2 at error O(a/log(X)) remain open on the preserved sharp-development branch.

records.title: The classification of compact 1-manifolds
records.abstract: A Lean 4 (mathlib) proof of the classification of 1-manifolds, specifically that every compact, connected, Hausdorff topological space charted on the half-line [0,∞) is homeomorphic to the circle S¹ or to the closed unit interval [0,1]. The proof follows David Gale's outline: shrink to a finite atlas of interval charts, then induct on the atlas size, merging two overlapping charts at each step; a connected overlap glues two charts into one (two boundary charts glue onto [0, 1]), while a disconnected overlap has exactly two components and yields the circle.

records.title: Independent Bonnet--Myers diameter and compactness theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes the classical Bonnet--Myers theorem for complete connected smooth boundaryless finite-dimensional real Riemannian manifolds. From dimension n >= 2, K > 0, and the pointwise lower bound Ric(a,a) >= (n-1) K g(a,a), the selected theorem constructs the Levi--Civita connection and actual curvature, proves compactness, and gives the sharp induced extended-diameter bound pi/sqrt K. The development proves minimizing-geodesic, parallel-transport, second-variation, index-form, and metric-compactness bridges rather than assuming them.
authors: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz

records.title: The Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem
records.abstract: Every continuous real function on the closed unit n-cube is a superposition of continuous functions of one variable and addition, with the inner functions universal for the dimension. Three forms, each implying the next, named for who is credited with the statement. Lorentz-Sprecher form: there are positive constants lam_1, ..., lam_n and continuous strictly increasing psi_0, ..., psi_2n : R -> R, all depending only on n, such that every f continuous on [0,1]^n is f(x) = sum_{q=0}^{2n} g(sum_{p=1}^{n} lam_p psi_q(x_p)) on the cube for some continuous g : R -> R depending on f. Lorentz's form: continuous monotone (non-decreasing) inner functions phi_{q,p} : R -> R indexed by both q and p, and a single continuous outer function Phi. Kolmogorov's form: continuous phi_{q,p} and 2n+1 continuous outer functions Phi_q -- the theorem as proved in 1957 and as usually cited. In every form the inner functions are quantified before f, so one family serves every f; that is the content of the theorem. The statements are made for every n, the trivial cases n = 0 and n = 1 included, and are written in Mathlib's vocabulary alone -- Continuous, ContinuousOn, StrictMono, Monotone, Set.Icc on Fin n -> R and finite sums -- with no definition of their own, so that each can be audited against the informal statement without first accepting a definition.

records.title: ry-lean: sets avoiding {x, x+y, x+y²} — Younis's two-set construction and the exponent 0.77028
records.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of Younis's lower-bound construction for subsets of {1,...,N} with no configuration {x, x+y, x+y^2} (y nonzero), in its two-set form: for every square-free modulus m and residue sets R1, R2 modulo m with R1 square-difference-free and no nonzero difference of R2 equal to the square of a difference of R1, the interval {1,...,N} contains a configuration-free set of size at least C(rho) N^rho for every rho below 1/2 + log|R1|/(3 log m) + log|R2|/(6 log m). The theorem is instantiated at m = 145 with |R1| = 10 and |R2| = 32, giving the exponent 0.770287..., which is proved to exceed Younis's exponent 0.768503... (m = 65, sizes 7 and 17) by exact comparisons of integer powers; decimal bounds 0.7702 < gamma < 0.77029 are also proved, and the bound is stated in liminf form for the counting function D(N).

records.title: All-ones polynomials over GF(2) under the substitution X ↦ X² + X + 1 (OEIS A071642, TheoremDB P12771)
records.abstract: Formalizes in Lean 4 the resolution of a 2019 OEIS conjecture of L. H. Gallardo (comment on A071642; TheoremDB P12771): for every n ≥ 2 the all-ones polynomial 1 + X + ⋯ + Xⁿ is irreducible over GF(2) if and only if 1 + P + ⋯ + Pⁿ is irreducible over GF(2), where P = X² + X + 1. The compared statements are the per-n equivalence, the literal set-level form of the OEIS comment (the terms ≥ 2 coincide), and the failure of the excluded case n = 1. The proof is elementary: a factorization of the all-ones polynomial composes to one of the substituted polynomial; conversely irreducibility forces n even, the X^(n-1) coefficient gives trace 1 for a root α, hence Tr(α + 1) = 1, so Z² + Z + (α + 1) has no root in GF(2^n) (Frobenius-invariance of the trace), a root β of it satisfies P(β) = α and has degree 2n, and the monic degree-2n polynomial 1 + P + ⋯ + Pⁿ vanishing at β is its minimal polynomial. SCOPE. The full conjecture is formalized with no weakened hypothesis. NOT CLAIMED: novelty of the mechanism, which is the classical trace criterion for compositions f(X² + X + c) over binary fields (Varshamov 1984, Meyn 1990); the contribution is the resolution of the specific OEIS conjecture and its machine check. AUDIENCE: finite fields and integer sequences.

records.title: The Broughton--Huff theorem on increasing unions of sigma-fields
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of the Broughton--Huff theorem that the ordinary union of a strictly increasing sequence of sigma-fields is not a sigma-field. The proof also proves the existence of a set measurable in the lattice supremum but in none of the individual sigma-fields.

records.title: A Tight Upper Bound for Fully Dynamic Matching on the Line
records.abstract:
There are `m` labeled supplies in `[0,1]`. In each period, an independent uniform demand arrives; an online policy selects one live supply, pays the distance between them, and replaces that supply by an independent uniform point. This is the one-dimensional fully dynamic model studied in Kanoria's [*Dynamic spatial matching*](https://doi.org/10.1214/25-AAP2154). That paper established a lower bound of order `log(m)/m` and an upper bound of order `log(m)^2/m`, and posed closing this logarithmic gap as an open problem.

We construct a policy and show that its performance matches the prior known lower bound up to a universal constant factor. Specifically, for every `m >= 2`, from every fixed initial inventory, its root-mean-square one-period cost has limsup at most `C log(m+1)/m`, with `C = 72000/log(2)`. With a scheduled `m`-period replacement phase, its expected average cost, including that phase, has the same bound for every total horizon `N >= 2m^2`. The policy assigns deletion probabilities recursively on a dyadic tree and implements them by quantile transport. Its analysis combines a harmonic inventory potential with a quadratic Bellman inequality. Tree symmetry cancels interactions between spatial scales, while the Bellman inequality controls both transport discrepancy and the curvature loss in the potential drift.

records.title: Confinement schemas and the reach of block certificates for powers of rational numbers modulo one
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib development of the second paper on the sets Z_{p/q}(s, s+t) = {ξ > 0 : {ξ(p/q)ⁿ} ∈ [s, s+t) for all n ≥ 0}, the generalized Z-numbers of Flatto, Lagarias and Pollington. The first paper built a corpus of block certificates for individual statements Z_{p/q}(U) = ∅. This paper replaces parts of that corpus by theorems, and then asks what the certificate format can and cannot reach. Thirty certificates in the regime p > q² collapse into one closed-form criterion on the single real parameter ε = {(p−q)s}, settling a set of positions of measure 1 − 2q²/(p(p+q)) at every base and for every real ξ ≠ 0; the criterion extends to a family indexed by a depth K, identified with the finiteness criterion of [FLP95] and with the parameter intervals J¹_b of [Bug04], the depth playing the role of the denominator of the rotation number. An explicit escape time for L ≤ ξ ≤ X is extracted from the soundness proof, and every unranked certificate of [Ste26] is made effective by it. A completeness theorem says the verdict is forced on the class where a certificate can exist — a finite hold set — and that an infinite hold set refuses every unranked certificate at every depth and over every denominator, which turns a bounded computer search into a theorem. A measure-theoretic depth–size bound 1 ≤ 2δ(K + 2 + log_{p/q} 2B) prices [KK17, Prob. 6.1] for this format. Finally a rank-stratified certificate gives ‖ξ(3/2)ⁿ‖ < 2/7 = 0.285714… infinitely often for every ξ ≠ 0, past the 31/81 = 0.38271… of [Dub19] as a window and past the corpus's own 1/3 as a nearest-integer constant.

records.title: rk-lean: the directed construction for k-th-power-difference-free sets at every k, with the exponents 0.912145 (k = 4) and 0.950826 (k = 6)
records.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of Krachun's directed (acyclic-block) lower-bound construction for sets of integers with no k-th-power difference, stated and proved for every exponent k >= 2. Let D_k(N) be the largest size of a subset of {1,...,N} no two of whose elements differ by a nonzero perfect k-th power. A pool for k is a nonempty list of blocks (m, sup, H) with pairwise coprime square-free moduli m >= 2, heights H >= 2, and sup a nonempty list of (vertex, rank) pairs with distinct vertices below m, ranks below H, and a strict rank drop along every ordered pair of vertices whose difference is a nonzero k-th-power residue mod m (so the induced digraph is acyclic). For every such pool, alpha k P <= liminf log D_k(N)/log N, where alpha k P = (sum ((k-1) log m + log t)/log H) / (1 + k sum log m / log H) and t >= 1 is the number of vertices of a block; and N^rho <= D_k(N) for all large N whenever rho < alpha k P. The theorem is instantiated at k = 4 with nine blocks, eight on the primes 5, 13, 29, 37, 53, 61, 101, 109 and one at the composite square-free modulus 51 = 3 * 17, and at k = 6 with nine blocks on the primes 7, 19, 31, 43, 67, 79, 103, 127, 139, giving the exponents 0.912145042700... and 0.950825559086..., each proved to exceed the corresponding Ruzsa transfer value ((3 + log 6/log 17)/4 = 0.908103119289... and (5 + log 6/log 13)/6 = 0.949759249243..., the latter being Ruzsa's own published Corollary at k = 6) and the decimal bounds 0.9121 and 0.9508, by exact comparisons of natural powers.

records.title: Rational invariants of three frames in the split Albert algebra: a Lean formalization
records.abstract: Let J be the split Albert algebra over a field k of characteristic zero, the 27-dimensional Jordan algebra of 3 by 3 Hermitian matrices over the split octonions, with trace tr. A frame is an ordered triple of trace-one idempotents summing to 1. Three frames E, F, K carry 54 natural invariants under the group G of all unital k-linear bijections of J preserving its Jordan product: the pair traces tr(eᵢ∘fⱼ), tr(fⱼ∘kₗ), tr(kₗ∘eᵢ) and the triple traces tr(eᵢ∘(fⱼ∘kₗ)). This Lean 4 development proves that these traces do not generate all rational invariants of three frames, and that adjoining one additional invariant suffices: the field of G-invariant rational functions on the variety of frame triples is a quadratic extension H(d) of the field H generated by the 54 traces, where d = tr(W∘(W∘W)), W = x∘(y∘z) − y∘(x∘z), x = e₂ − e₀, y = f₂ − f₀, z = k₂ − k₀. The development also proves that the variety of frame triples is irreducible, that the coordinate algebra used is the standard split Albert algebra, that d is not in H, and that every invariant is uniquely a + b·d with a, b in H. The ambiguity occurs over ℚ: two explicit frame triples have identical 54 traces and d = −2591357/62208 and −1782559/62208, and no ℚ-linear automorphism of J combined with any of the 1,296 relabellings of frames and idempotents carries one to the other. The proved endpoints use only the permitted axiom dependencies propext, Quot.sound and Classical.choice; a Python script rechecks the example in exact arithmetic.

records.title: An Infinite Simple Group with Property (T) That Is Sofic and Hyperlinear
records.abstract: Brown asks in 2001 (arXiv:math/0111286, Question 11.7) whether an infinite simple discrete group with Kazhdan's property (T) can embed in the unitary group of an R^ω-embeddable McDuff factor, which for such a group is hyperlinearity; Ozawa asks it in 2003 in that language, in About the QWEP conjecture (arXiv:math/0306067); and Pestov prints it, with the sofic form added, as Open question 9.1 of Hyperlinear and sofic groups: a brief guide (arXiv:0804.3968): can an infinite simple group with Kazhdan's property (T) be hyperlinear, or sofic? This project proves, in Lean 4 over Mathlib, that the answer is yes in both forms. The witness is EL₃(A), the group generated by the elementary matrices of size three over the ring A = LC(X, 𝔽₂) ⋊ ℤ, the algebraic crossed product of the locally constant 𝔽₂-valued functions on a binary Toeplitz subshift X by the shift. The ring is finitely generated and simple with center 𝔽₂; the group is infinite and simple, has property (T) by the theorem of Ershov and Jaikin-Zapirain, proved here, and is locally embeddable into finite groups by periodic models of the Toeplitz sequence, so it is sofic and hyperlinear. The two compared theorems state the existence of an infinite simple group with property (T) that is hyperlinear, and of one that is sofic, with property (T), soficity and hyperlinearity defined in the Challenge from the textbook sources; their axiom closure is propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The prose of this submission, this abstract included, was written by Claude (Anthropic).

records.title: Lean proofs of Dimitrov's Conjectures 1 and 3
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization proving Dimitrov's Conjectures 1 and 3 for every natural k >= 1 and n >= 2. The results concern inequalities involving Euler's totient, Dedekind's psi function, and the sum-of-divisors function. The source paper proves the k = 1 instances and discusses k = 2, 3; this development covers the full stated range, including k >= 4, and additionally proves for each inequality that equality holds exactly when n is prime. By supplying the full parameter range and sharp equality cases beyond those treated in the source, the project is relevant to researchers in elementary and analytic number theory who study inequalities among multiplicative arithmetic functions, and to formal-mathematics researchers studying the verification of contemporary conjectures. Historical priority for the full-range proofs has not been established by expert or source-author review. The mathematical reductions, Lean code, and documentation were generated substantially by OpenAI Codex under human direction, as detailed below.

records.title: md-lean: exact height span, dart mass, and adjugate scaling for Mazur's greedy construction
records.abstract: Exact height-span of Mazur's scheme grammar, a local dart-mass bound, and an adjugate identity for the Dirichlet matrix of that construction; not a proof of the strong Papadimitriou–Ratajczak conjecture and not a theorem that every 3-connected plane graph attains the scheme maximum. Mazur builds injective integer heights by inductive recurrences on rooted pieces (edge, cycle, binary series, two-range join) and then forms a weighted Dirichlet matrix for the horizontal coordinate; the paper does not bound the height span or the bit length of the coordinates. For a well-formed scheme on n >= 2 vertices with j nontrivial joins, T+1 <= 2^j (n-2j), attained at every admissible pair (n,j)=(2,0) or 2j+3 <= n. The one-parameter maximum is F(n) = 2^{n/2}-1 (n even) or 3 * 2^{(n-3)/2}-1 (n odd). The coarser bound T <= 2^{n-2} remains. An integer matrix has |det| at most the product of its row ell_1-norms. Heights in {0,...,T} force Mazur's interior dart weights to be at most (n-1)T, so every Dirichlet row has ell_1-norm at most 2(n-1)^2 T when T >= 1, and |det M| <= (2(n-1)^2 T)^n; locally the interior outgoing dart-weight sum is at most a_s b_s T. Combining the coarser span bound with the row-sum bound sizes T^2 |det M| and T^2 |det M| T. Independently of invertibility, under the height bound h i <= T, z = adj(M) u satisfies Mz = Delta u and z_s = Delta h_s (T-h_s) on the boundary as ordinary integer subtraction. Polynomial-area Euclidean planar greedy drawings of all 3-connected planar graphs remain open (Da Lozzo–D'Angelo–Frati, COCOON 2020).

records.title: A Surjunctive Group That Is Not Sofic
records.abstract: We formalize the existence of a finitely generated surjunctive group that is not sofic. This answers negatively the converse to the Gromov-Weiss surjunctivity theorem, recorded as open problem OP-11 by Ceccherini-Silberstein and Coornaert and as Problem 1.1 by Bowen and Chapman. The witness is the symmetric double G *_Gamma G, where Gamma = EL_3(F_2[x_1,x_2,x_3]) and G = EL_3(F_2[x_1^+-1,x_2^+-1,x_3^+-1]) semidirect EL_3(Z), with the action given by monomial substitution. Kun and Thom constructed this pair and proved the double nonsofic. The new ingredient here is a surjunctivity theorem for symmetric doubles of surjunctive groups. The Lean development proves both halves for this witness, including the required permutation centralizer normalization theorem. The challenge states surjunctivity through finite-memory cellular automata and soficity through finite normalized-Hamming models. The two selected declarations assert the finitely generated counterexample and the failure of the universal converse.

records.title: A proof of Nivat's conjecture
records.abstract: A Lean+mathlib proof of Nivat's conjecture: Given a finite alphabet A, we consider configurations c: Z^2 -> A, which are arbitrary maps that can be thought of as colorings of the 2D lattice. Writing P_c(m, n) for the number of distinct m-by-n block patterns occurring in a configuration c, Nivat conjectured that if P_c(m, n) <= mn for some positive m and n, then c is periodic; that is, there exists nonzero h such that c(v+h) = c(v) for all v. The proof is due to GPT-6 Pro.

records.title: To cover a permutohedron
records.abstract: This Lean 4 formalization of Kong and Zeng's To cover a permutohedron (arXiv:2509.13877v3, 9 April 2026) determines the minimum number of affine hyperplanes needed to cover the permutation vertices of (1,...,n), excluding the hyperplane containing every vertex. The exact answer is n for odd n at least 3, and n-1 for even n at least 4. It also proves that an arbitrary injective real tuple of length n at least 2 has the sharp hyperplane intersection bound (n-1)! when its n-1 signed critical values are distinct. Genuine polynomial-root path lifting establishes local transpositions and the cycle at infinity, with explicit corrections to the source's loop hypotheses. A symmetric polynomial norm replaces the paper's general Bezout step. One independent Challenge and one Comparator configuration cover all eighteen results, including sharp constructions, generic and four-element consequences, and the connection with convex vertices and arbitrary affine hyperplanes.

records.title: Gallai’s Path Decomposition Conjecture for Graphs with Small Bowtie Boundaries
records.abstract: We prove sufficient conditions for partitioning the edges of a connected finite simple graph into at most ⌈|V(G)|/2⌉ simple paths. The results concern bowtie components—two triangles sharing exactly one vertex—in the subgraph induced by even-degree vertices. They include removal preserving specified endpoints, a sharp full-incidence star expansion, composition under explicit boundary hypotheses, and corollaries for graphs with two bowtie components. The unrestricted two-exception conjecture remains open.

records.title: MI-32: Lean formalization of the parity and positive-polynomial upper bound
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the MI-32 upper bound, that is, of the Latała-Świątkowski conjecture that for every regularity parameter alpha >= 1 there is a constant C > 0, independent of the dimension and of the entry laws, with E||X|| <= C (M(X) + D(X)) for every square random matrix X with independent mean-zero real entries whose absolute moments satisfy ||X_ij||_{L_2r} <= alpha ||X_ij||_{L_r} at every real order r >= 1. Here ||.|| is the Euclidean operator norm, M(X) is the sum of the largest row and column standard deviations, and D(X) is the max-min weak moment at order log(k+1) taken over one shared deterministic deletion set on both axes. The probability space is arbitrary and the subunit order log 2 at k = 1 is kept literally. The selected theorem MI32.main_upper carries a complete proof whose transitive axiom audit reports only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The proof runs through original-law positive-polynomial moments and interpolation, exact occupation-count localization, finite nets, a direct independent-coordinate Hilbert comparison, full original-law creator and annihilator contractions, positive vacuum iteration giving the local symmetric-law operator-moment theorem at the exact order log(n+1), a nested deterministic deletion decomposition with cubic two-sided variance screening, an elementary centered-Gram estimate for the far remainder, two two-shell block families controlled by the local theorem at scheduled orders, and the original-copy symmetrization reduction. Constants are explicit and conservative, not optimized.

records.title: Robin1984
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of Guy Robin's 1984 equivalence between the Riemann hypothesis and the strict divisor-sum inequality sigma(n) < exp(gamma) n log(log n) for every integer n > 5040.  The development also proves the restriction to colossally abundant integers, reconstructs the Nicolas--Landau oscillation argument used for the converse implication, and checks the finite ranges with exact Lean certificates.  It also formalizes Lagarias's 2001 elementary harmonic-number criterion and its equivalence to the Riemann hypothesis. This is a formalization of equivalence criteria; it does not prove the Riemann hypothesis.

records.title: A Counterexample to the Trace Problem for Uniform Tracial Completions
records.abstract: We formalize a negative answer to Problem XXII of Schafhauser, Tikuisis and White. There is a separable unital C*-algebra A with nonempty compact tracial state space such that its uniform tracial completion M has a tracial state that is discontinuous in the uniform 2-norm. Thus the canonical extensions of the traces of A form a proper subset X of the traces of M. A second theorem gives a factorial tracially complete pair (M, X) with the same failure, answering Question 1.1 of Carrion, Castillejos, Evington, Gabe, Schafhauser, Tikuisis and White negatively. In both statements, X is exactly the set of uniform-2-norm-continuous traces. The proof uses a unitized c0-sum of antipodally covariant matrix-function algebras of growing rank and dimension. Borsuk-Ulam supplies finite coordinate-state constraints; weak-star compactness produces a corona trace detecting a sequence whose uniform 2-norm tends to zero. Both selected Lean theorems are unconditional. The completion is characterized by tracial completeness, unique restriction of designated traces to all base traces, and density in the uniform 2-norm.

records.title: Termination of the classical inflation hierarchy on pair-source networks
records.abstract: Machine-checked Lean 4 proofs of two theorems about the classical inflation hierarchy. The headline theorem, TriangleInflation.Graph.classification_NW, classifies the scenarios on which the hierarchy terminates: for a pair-source scenario with binary observations, some finite Navascués–Wolfe order characterizes compatibility iff every connected component is a double-star, and then order two suffices. A pair-source scenario is a finite simple graph without isolated vertices, one binary observed variable per vertex and one independent latent source per edge; a double-star is a tree of diameter at most three. The terminating half first labels each component from its graph structure alone: its vertices of degree at least two are pairwise adjacent and number at most two; with two of them they are the centres, with one of them (a star) a neighbour is promoted to the second centre, with none (a single edge) both endpoints are the centres, and every other vertex is a leaf attached to one centre. It then reconstructs a model from any order-two witness: source-disjoint blocks are independent under the witness, and conditioning on a leaf pattern reads off the joint law of the two centres' response tables, which becomes the law of a fresh central source. The nonterminating half supplies, at every order t, a strictly positive law that passes the order-t test and has no model. On an induced cycle the law is the parity target with correlation 1/(4 m^2 t^2), whose witness is a positive Fourier density on m t auxiliary signs pushed forward along products of adjacent signs; its incompatibility is parity rigidity. On an induced five-observer path the law is a bilocal target with h = 1/(16 t^2), whose witness is the inflated law of a pair-source model with complex source weights (1 ± i s/(4t))/4 on the two inner sources, under which the copies are independent and identically distributed; the real part of that law is shown nonnegative by a telescoped triangle inequality, and the incompatibility is the bilocal inequality sqrt|I| + sqrt|J| ≤ 1. Both witnesses are moved to the ambient graph by induced-subgraph transport and made strictly positive by independent local flips. The same development proves the classification for the ancestral-independence and recursively expressible hierarchies, and proves that the latter two coincide on every pair-source scenario. The second theorem, TriangleInflation.no_finite_characterizing_order, is the triangle case made quantitative: for every order t ≥ 1 there is an explicit rational three-bit law that is feasible at order t for the ancestral-independence hierarchy I^AI_t, hence for the Navascués–Wolfe hierarchy I^NW_t, and is not triangle compatible. This answers, in the negative for the triangle, the question Navascués and Wolfe (2020, §4.1) raise about whether some finite order settles exact compatibility; their hierarchy is asymptotically complete, so each incompatible law is rejected at some finite order, but the rejecting order cannot be bounded uniformly. The witnesses are P_t = Q(ε_t, r_t) with ε_t = 1/(2t³) and r_t = (1 − ε_t)^(t−1), where Q(ε,r) = ε δ_000 + (1 − ε) Bern(r)^⊗3. Membership is proved by an explicit inflation law on the order-t copied observations: independent Bernoulli defect bits on the cube [t]³ of source-copy indices together with independent private bits, with an observation outputting 1 exactly when its private bit and every defect on its line vanish. That law is S_t³-symmetric, has the tensor power P^⊗t as its diagonal law, and satisfies the injectable-marginal and ancestral-independence prescriptions. Incompatibility comes from the Finner inequality P(000)² ≤ P_A(0) P_B(0) P_C(0), which P_t violates by at least ε_t²/2 > 0; the inequality is proved both for finite latent alphabets and, in FinnerMeasure.lean, for arbitrary measurable latent spaces. The library also formalizes the order-t fan inequalities and their rejecting-order corollary, the family R_p with rejecting order 2 at every distance, the finite bounds on the first rejecting order along P_ε behind its Θ(ε^{-1/3}) growth, the order-t second-moment rate bound and its convex-order sharpening, the quantitative parity rigidity behind the cycle distance bound, and the square and triangle witnesses at q = 1/(16t). The two registry statements in Palomar/TriangleInflation/ import Mathlib alone and carry their definitions verbatim from TriangleInflation/Defs.lean and TriangleInflation/Graph/Defs.lean.

records.title: Certified naturality and the obstruction to unrestricted naturality in a typed two-dimensional calculus
records.abstract: We formalize the boundary of naturality in the labelled conversion calculus of A Theory of a Two-Dimensional Typed Lambda Calculus. Canonical evaluation of inductively presented homotopies constructs naturality squares, and transport along finite presentations preserves two-paths and recovers the naturality boundary. In contrast, an explicit pointwise family on Fin 3 admits no naturality two-cell or finite pasting: a six-element dihedral-group invariant separates its two boundary paths while respecting every declared two-cell generator. This independently reconstructed refutation is classical, not a verification of the manuscript's claimed constructive Idris proof. Supporting results distinguish beta and eta evidence by parity and give a standalone typed de Bruijn syntax with exact raw-tree representation adequacy and a parity-preserving conversion interpretation. The result concerns this declared evidence calculus, not normalization, full abstraction, or a completeness theorem for lambda calculus.

records.title: Explicit Fourier–Jacobi Haar-core evaluation and Abel limits
records.abstract: For a nonarchimedean local field with residue cardinality q > 2, this development evaluates a sum of three normalized Haar integrals of an explicit eight-term Weyl kernel defined from valuations of entries and two-by-two minors of a concrete 4 by 4 matrix. It proves measurability and Bochner integrability on the natural damped range, an explicit rational evaluation in the undamped interior, principal Abel convergence, and the whole signed special Abel limit at delta = plus or minus q^(-1/2). The Satake parameters are unitary and avoid the stated Weyl walls; the special quotient also excludes parameters equal to its sign. The proof assembles all fifty infinite valuation regions with the source Haar normalizations. This adapts local calculations in Paul, Pitale, Saha and Schmidt's Fourier–Jacobi period paper. Identification of the explicit kernel with the paper's independently defined spherical coefficient and the full period identity are not claimed. The positive special-sign product is identically zero. No undamped special-endpoint integrability or extension to exceptional parameter walls is asserted.

records.title: Boundary regularity for non-local operators with symmetric kernels and vanishing horizon
