records.abstract: This Lean 4 formalization proves the two main theorems of the paper 'Boundary regularity for non-local operators with symmetric kernels and vanishing horizon' (arXiv:2504.00567v1). For a fractional order s in (1/2,1), the paper studies a nonlocal operator with symmetric kernel whose interaction horizon depends on the distance to the boundary and on a horizon parameter sigma in (0,1], and shrinks near the boundary. The formalization proves that weak solutions u to the Dirichlet problem with zero Dirichlet data and bounded right-hand side are in the Hölder space C^{2s-1} up to the boundary. Furthermore, it is proven that the quotient u/d_Omega^{2s-1} is also Hölder continuous up to the boundary. Both results include norm estimates controlled by the essential supremum of the right-hand side.

records.title: Integral Matrices of Fixed Rank over Number Fields: Lean formalization
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of the fixed-rank asymptotic count for integral matrices over a number field and the convergence of moments of lifts of algebraic codes. The public results preserve the submission PDF's main scale, error terms, echelon-integral limit, and denominator normalization. The intermediate-rank height-counting input attributed to Schmidt is an explicit hypothesis; it is not silently assumed as an axiom.

records.title: Erdős Problem 190: every canonical N exceeds (Ck)^k for large k, and H(k)^{1/k}/k → ∞ under the existence hypothesis — a Lean 4 formalization of the qualitative statement of arXiv:2604.20588
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization, against Mathlib, of the qualitative statement of J. H. Bae, "A resolution of Erdős Problem #190: the canonical van der Waerden number satisfies H(k)^{1/k}/k → ∞" (arXiv:2604.20588, v2), Corollary 1.2, via the elementary argument of its Section 4.3.  Let H(k) be the least N such that every finite colouring of {1,…,N} contains a monochromatic or a rainbow k-term arithmetic progression; Erdős and Graham (1979) asked whether H(k)^{1/k}/k → ∞ (Problem 190 in Bloom's database).  The compared theorems state that for every C there is K such that for all k ≥ K every N for which [N] is canonical for k satisfies (Ck)^k < N (divergence, and its Filter.Eventually form); this is a statement about canonical N only and by itself says nothing about H(k) (it holds vacuously for a k with no canonical N, where H(k) = sInf ∅ = 0).  Combined with the existence of a canonical N for every k — the Erdős–Graham theorem, via Szemerédi's theorem, which is not formalized — it gives H(k) > (Ck)^k for all large k, i.e. H(k)^{1/k}/k → ∞; that conditional conclusion is stated as H_divergence, with the existence as an explicit hypothesis on H(k) = sInf {N | canonical}.  The fourth compared theorem is the explicit bound behind the argument: for k ≥ 12 there is a prime p with (k−1)/2 < p ≤ k−1 such that every canonical N exceeds p^(p − ⌊k/3⌋)·⌊⌊k/3⌋^(k−1)/(16k²)⌋ (integer divisions, as in the Lean statement).  The proof composes the Erdős–Lovász lower bound W(r,k) − 1 ≥ r^(k−1)/(16k²) for van der Waerden numbers (obtained from the symmetric Lovász local lemma, applied with a number of colours r₀ = ⌊k/3⌋ growing with k), the restricted Blankenship–Cummings–Taranchuk recurrence W(r,k) − 1 ≥ p·(W(r−1,k) − 1) for primes r ≤ p ≤ k, Bertrand's postulate, and elementary asymptotics.  The paper's main theorem, the explicit rate H(k)^{1/k}/k ≥ (1/e − ε(k))·k/log k obtained with the Baker–Harman–Pintz prime-gap theorem, is not formalized (that theorem is not available in Mathlib); the formalized argument gives the weaker rate k^{1/6−o(1)}, which suffices for the qualitative statement.  The compared theorems depend only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.title: B. C. Carlson's approach to special functions of applied mathematics
records.abstract: Lean formalization of selected results in B. C. Carlson's theory of special functions as complex Dirichlet averages. The registry selection establishes joint entire-parameter continuation of holomorphic averages on convex open scalar domains; joint holomorphy and native-integral agreement for the Gamma-regularized R and L functions on principal slit-node domains; Euler inversion and Euler-Poisson equations; and Gamma-regularized adaptations of both quadratic R transformations for all complex exponent and Dirichlet parameters with positive-real-part unsquared variables. The L function is related to R by exponent differentiation. The repository also supplies Pochhammer, several-complex-variable, simplex-integration, and Dirichlet foundations, which are not separately selected registry claims. This is a snapshot of an ongoing development, not complete coverage of Carlson's 1977 book or 1987 L-function article.

records.title: Constructive families and an extension theorem for binary permutation X-rays
records.abstract: We prove permutation realization for every admissible binary X-ray profile whose rank deviations from the odd staircase lie in [-2, 2], at every order and without a bound on density slack. We also prove the one-sided families with all deviations at least -1 or all deviations at most 1, with at least 2^u realizations, where u counts positive or negative deviations respectively. For n >= 1, if a label multiset L is realizable at order n, then Q(L) = {3, 2n+1} multiset-union (L+2) is realizable at order n+2. If every source label lies in [2, 2n-2], then h(L) <= h(Q(L)), where h counts permutation realizations. Repeated source labels are allowed. A least-order counterexample to the unrestricted conjecture must have first deviation at least 3 or last deviation at most -3. The unrestricted conjecture remains open.

records.title: CoarseGraining
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of the coarse-graining approach to quantitative stochastic homogenization of divergence-form elliptic equations: function-space, deterministic, probabilistic, and homogenization-scale theory up to the quenched minimal-scale theorem. The public main result is a uniformly elliptic, isotropic specialization of the quenched homogenization comparison estimate in Armstrong-Kuusi, "Renormalization Group and Elliptic Homogenization in High Contrast" (Inventiones Mathematicae, 2025), independently checked using Audit/QuenchedComparison/comparator.json, together with four further comparator-checked specializations under Audit/.

records.title: MarkovProcess
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of continuous-path Markov processes associated with conservative Feller transition semigroups on nonempty locally compact Polish spaces. A uniform Kolmogorov displacement-moment bound yields a unique measurable kernel from each starting point to continuous-path space, with the prescribed finite-dimensional distributions. The library also develops strong Markov properties, generators and resolvents, stopping and killing, and Brownian motion as an example. The existence and uniqueness theorem is independently checked using Audit/ContinuousMarkovProcess/comparator.json.

records.title: Formalization of norm-variation of multiple ergodic averages for commuting transformations
records.abstract: This is a Lean 4 formalization of norm-variation of multiple ergodic averages for commuting transformations,  including Tao's norm-convergence theorem. At the heart of the argument is an explicit real-variable estimate for twisted multilinear averages. This formalization is based on the blueprint available at arXiv:2608.27321. The statements of the main theorems have been hand-formalized,  while the proof was autoformalized during a one-week period using coding agents under human supervision.  This produced roughly 107k lines of code (excluding comments and blank lines) and includes proofs of several  prerequisite theorems currently not in mathlib such as multilinear complex interpolation,  the Calderón transference principle, and properties of Wiener space functions.

records.title: The exponential map is chaotic
records.abstract:
In 1926, Fatou conjectured that the Julia set of the complex exponential map is the entire complex plane; in other words, the dynamical system described by the map is unstable under perturbation at every point in the plane.  Misiurewicz proved this conjecture in 1981. In 2015, Shen and Rempe published "The Exponential Map Is Chaotic: An Invitation to Transcendental Dynamics", giving an elementary and conceptual proof of Misiurewicz's theorem and deriving its dynamical consequences, without requiring advanced results  from complex analysis or dynamics.
This project formalises these results in Lean 4: density of escaping points, points with dense orbits, and repelling periodic points; eventual covering of compact subsets of the punctured plane; Devaney chaos; spherical non-equicontinuity; and the fact that the Julia set is the whole complex plane.

records.title: Davis-Kahan 1970: the four Section 2 rotation-of-eigenvectors theorem families
records.abstract: Machine-checked Lean 4 presentation of the four headline theorem families in Section 2 of Davis and Kahan (1970): sin-Theta, tan-Theta, sin-2-Theta, and tan-2-Theta. The Palomar Comparator exposes five selected source-facing declarations: the residual sin-Theta estimate, the residual tan-Theta estimate, both the residual and whole-space sin-2-Theta estimates, and the residual tan-2-Theta estimate. The statements retain the paper's standing separable ambient Hilbert-space scope, permit finite or infinite ambient dimension, and are generic over RCLike scalars to cover the real and complex cases. Their norm quantifier is presented in the Challenge by a dimension-coherent symmetric norming function; the included formalization proves via Fan dominance that the corresponding inequalities yield the source-facing universal unitarily invariant norm estimates.

records.title: Chain Bounding
records.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of the core results of "Chain bounding, the leanest proof of Zorn's lemma, and an illustration of computerized proof formalization" by Guillermo L. Incatasciato and Pedro Sánchez Terraf, published at the American Mathematical Monthly (preprint freely accessible at http://arxiv.org/abs/2404.11638). It formalizes the order-theoretic notion of _good chains_ for an "expander" of subsets of a poset: the comparability of good chains, the existence of a greatest good chain, the well-ordering of good chains for an expander of the form C ↦ C ∪ {f C}, the Chain Bounding Lemma (there is no assignment of a strict upper bound to every chain of a poset), the Unbounded Chain Lemma, and — as a novel, unified alternative to the classical ordinal-based arguments — derivations of both Zorn's Lemma and the Bourbaki–Witt fixed point theorem from Chain Bounding.

records.title: ns-lean: Naslund's Conjecture 13 is false at q = 3, k = 2, for every n congruent to 0 mod 4 with n >= 8
records.abstract: A Lean 4 proof that square-difference-free subsets of the polynomials of degree below n over F_3 can be larger than 3^(3n/4). Call A square-difference-free when no two of its elements differ by a nonzero square, and let D_3(n) be the largest size of such a set inside P_{3,n}. A ten-word code S in F_3^4, in which no two words differ by a vector with every coordinate in {0, 1}, drives a lift that carries a square-difference-free subset of P_{3,m} to one of P_{3,m+8} with 810 times as many elements. Iterating it from the bases {0} and B_4 = {a T^3 + b T + c (1 - T^2)} gives square-difference-free sets of size 810^e in degree below 8e and 27 * 810^e in degree below 8e + 4, so the conjectured bound 3^(3n/4) fails at every n divisible by 4 with n >= 8, and 16/21 <= liminf log D_3(n) / (n log 3).

records.title: A formalization of Chang, Liu, and Liu's proof of Chvátal's conjecture
records.abstract: A Lean 4 + mathlib formalization of Fan Chang, Hong Liu, and Miao Liu's paper "A proof of Chvátal's conjecture via a sharp correlation inequality" (arXiv:2609.19123v1). It formalizes their star theorem for hereditary set families, sharp Boolean Fourier correlation inequality, antipodal corollary, sharpness results, and weighted strengthening. The formalization was completely prepared by GPT-6.

records.title: Sectorial asymptotics for centered Riemann-xi coefficients
records.abstract: Formalizes the exact centered-xi coefficient normalization, a uniform sectorial saddle-point asymptotic, and relative-error derivative estimates through order six. These are the analytic inputs used by a two-thirds hyperbolicity-wedge theorem for Jensen polynomials of Riemann's xi-function. This Palomar topic does not itself state the final Jensen-polynomial hyperbolicity theorem.

records.title: Resonance-cluster analysis for a proposed counterexample to Fried's conjecture
records.abstract:
A Lean 4 formalization of the theorem FriedCrossing.fried_counterexample_of_resolvent_inputs, the machine-checked reduction behind a proposed codimension-one failure of Fried's identity ζ(0) = τ_R for acyclic characters on a closed hyperbolic 3-manifold with b₁ = 1. For a simple illustration of the method with figures, see docs/counterexample_intuitive_view.pdf.
The Mechanism: Near (g_hyp, ρ_triv), along the conformal family g_τ = e^{−2τb}g_hyp with characters χ_θ, the Ruelle resonances near 0 form two small clusters: a rank-2 cluster in degree 1, encoded by a 2×2 matrix M(θ,τ), and a rank-4 cluster in degree 2, encoded by a 4×4 matrix A(θ,τ). A branch is one eigenvalue of a cluster matrix followed continuously in (θ,τ). Degree 1 has the closed branch and the twin s_nc(θ,τ), which starts at the double point s*(θ) < 0 and travels at rate r₀ > 0 towards 0. Degree 2 has the two locked branches (the same eigenvalues, lifted by d₀) and two pure branches, the roots of Q = X² − e₁X + e₂; the pure branch nearest 0 is z(θ,τ). At the crossing metric τ = σ(θ) the twin and z reach 0 together, the twin as a pole of ζ and z as a zero, so ζ stays regular at 0 and ζ(0; g_σ) = τ_R · (rate of the twin)/(rate of z). The twin's rate is at most 2r₀ and z's exceeds 2r₀, so ζ(0; g_σ) ≠ τ_R. Fried's identity would need the two branches to arrive at the same speed. The whole Lean argument is bookkeeping of these four branches.
What is Proved: The theorem is a conditional reduction. Its objects are two abstract resolvent families on Banach scales (structure fields = the cited facts: local uniform boundedness and two-sided inversion of the generator modulo inclusions, CDDP Lemma 4.3; smooth generator), complex structures, and nondegenerate frames; the cluster matrices M, A are DEFINED from them as real parts of the frame matrices A(p)⁻¹B(p) built from contour integrals of matrix elements of the resolvent. Its hypotheses are, in six groups, the properties of that data which the argument uses, each cited: (1) two independent states at s*(θ) in the degree-1 cluster at τ = 0, with s*(0) = 0, s* continuous, s*(θ) < 0 for θ ≠ 0 [DGRS (7.6), BuOl Cor 5.1, DFG Thm 2; independence = rederivation A2 of the informal account]; (2) the first-variation formula B·∂_τM(0,0) = diag(0,p) with r₀ = B_cc p/det B > 0 [CDDP (4.22), (1.3)]; (3) the degree-2 cluster at τ = 0 has spectrum {s*, s*, s*, −s*} [DGRS (7.6), k = 2]; (4) at θ = 0 the degree-1 cluster is singular and the degree-2 cluster has spectrum {0, 0, 0, tr M} [CDDP Cor 4.1, DGRS Lemma 7.1]; (5) every eigenvalue of M is an eigenvalue of A [DGRS Lemma 7.1]; (6) for any functions ζ₀, F, any τ_R ≠ 0 and dimension vector c: ζ₀ = F·z/s_nc off the crossing with F continuous and ζ₀(σ) = F(σ) at it [CD (6.5) at λ = 0], ζ₀ = τ_R wherever s_nc ≠ 0 [DGRS Thm 2 + Fried 1986], exactness of C₀¹ → C₀² → V₃ at each crossing [DR Thm 2.1], c₀ = c₄ = 0 and c₃ = c₁ [DGRS Lemmas 7.4, 7.2], c_k the dimensions. The conclusion: there are θ₀, δ > 0 such that for 0 < |θ| < θ₀ the twin crosses 0 at exactly one σ ∈ (0, 2|s*|/r₀], the ζ-order at 0 is zero, the zero branch has slope ∂_τe₂/e₁ of modulus > 2r₀, |e₁(θ,σ)| ≤ K₁|θ|σ, and ζ₀(σ) = τ_R · (pole rate)/(zero rate) ≠ τ_R, with the torsion identity of the zero cluster.
Dependencies: The identification of the abstract data with the geometry — that the resolvent families are those of the twisted deformed generator L_X + iθω(X) on the anisotropic spaces of g_τ, that ζ₀(τ) is the Ruelle zeta function of g_τ at 0, that τ_R is the Reidemeister torsion of χ_θ, and that the defined matrices are the cluster matrices (their imaginary parts vanish) — is the informal layer, taken from the cited papers and the accompanying note, and is not formalized. Nothing about manifolds, flows, anisotropic spaces or zeta functions is in Lean. Granting the six groups as cited, the theorem exhibits a counterexample to Fried's identity in the form stated by DGRS for acyclic unitary representations, at a non-generic metric where ζ is regular at 0 and zero-resonant states exist with cancelling multiplicities; the refined identity of CD Thm 4 holds there. Whether the six groups hold as cited has not been independently verified by a mathematician other than the author.

records.title: Superdiffusion
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of the quantitative theory of advection-diffusion in self-similar random incompressible flows: the superdiffusive asymptotics of the effective diffusivity (Theorem A), the renormalization of the generator (quantitative homogenization of the Dirichlet problem at every scale, Theorem B), and the anomalous large-scale regularity theory (Theorem C) of Armstrong-Bou-Rabee-Kuusi, together with the sensitivity and coarse-matrix-derivative theory, the diffusivity recursion, and the diffusion-process theory that support them. The formalization consumes the public CoarseGraining homogenization library as its analytic base and the public MarkovProcess library for the general theory of continuous strong Markov processes of Feller semigroups. The three headline theorems are independently checked using the SuperdiffusionAudit/ comparator pairs.

records.title: Endpoint estimates for Stein's purely quadratic Carleson operator
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of four principal endpoint assertions from Fragkos, Krause, and Lacey's Endpoint Estimates for Stein's Purely Quadratic Carleson Operator: two failures of modular estimates below t log₂ t, a full-modulation L log L endpoint estimate, and a lacunary L (log₂ L)² log₄ L endpoint estimate.

records.title: Komlós conjecture
records.abstract: Lean4 formalization of the Komlós bound with constant 36 following the Lovett—Karingula exposition. The Komlós statement gives signs for finitely many vectors of Euclidean norm at most 1 so that the signed sum has supremum norm at most 36. The Beck–Fiala statement gives a vertex colouring with edge discrepancy at most 36√t when every vertex belongs to at most t edges.

records.title: gnm-lean: the number of partitions of {1, ..., n} into sets of at most three elements with power-of-three sums
records.abstract: A Lean 4 classification of the number of good partitions of an initial interval, where a good partition of {1, ..., n} is a set of pairwise disjoint nonempty blocks of at most three integers covering {1, ..., n}, each block summing to a power of three, and count n is the number of them. With N_u = {1, 2, 3, 4} union {3^t - 4, 3^t - 2, 3^t - 1, 3^t, 3^t + 1, 3^t + 2, 3^t + 3, 3^t + 5 : t >= 2} and E_2 = {13} union {3^t - 3 : t >= 2} union {3^t - 6 : t >= 3}, the four compared theorems say that for n >= 1 the count is 1 exactly on N_u, is 2 exactly on E_2, and is at least 3 elsewhere, and that the count is 2 at every 3^t - 6 with t >= 3. The source proves uniqueness for every n in N_u, records exactly two partitions at 3^t - 3 and at 13, and conjectures, immediately after that theorem, more than two at every other n, reporting a computer check up to n = 844; the family 3^t - 6 (first member 21) refutes that conjecture as printed, and the converse of the uniqueness statement is proved here. The lower bounds are three explicit partitions transported by four constructions each of which keeps a recoverable component; the exact values are exhaustive enumerations at twenty values n <= 86, kernel-checked and complete by a theorem about the search, carried to every power of three by stabilization above a threshold.

records.title: Yu-Wang-Samworth 2015: population-gap eigenspace and singular-subspace perturbation bounds
records.abstract:
A machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of the principal population-gap perturbation results of Yi Yu, Tengyao Wang and Richard J. Samworth, "A useful variant of the Davis-Kahan theorem for statisticians" (Biometrika 102 (2015) 315-323). This single Palomar entry compares both conclusions of Theorem 2 and both displays of Corollary 1 for eigenspaces of real symmetric matrices, together with the right- and left-singular-subspace conclusions of Theorem 3 for general real matrices and two supporting equivalences between its Gram-eigenvector formulation and the paper's paired singular-vector equations.
The common idea is that every separation hypothesis in Theorems 2 and 3 is stated entirely in terms of the population object. Theorem 2 uses the population eigenvalue gap min(lambda_(r-1)-lambda_r, lambda_s-lambda_(s+1)); Theorem 3 applies the same idea to the squared singular spectrum, with the additional factor (2 sigma_1 + ||A-hat-A||_op). No sample eigenvalue or singular-value gap is assumed, so the sample frame is arbitrary among admissible orthonormal frames at the selected block, including under multiplicity.
The selected results have deliberately different source dispositions. Theorem 2 is source-exact. Corollary 1 writes out the unit normalization inherited from its introduction as the d=1 case of Theorem 2; the standalone printed display omits that normalization and its second conclusion is false without it. Theorem 3 is source-corrected: its printed convention sigma^2_(rank(A)+1) := -infinity makes the denominator infinite at a rank boundary and yields a false assertion. The compared statement instead uses the ambient Gram-spectrum convention used by the paper's own proof, with singular values zero past rank, while retaining the printed restriction 1 <= r <= s <= rank(A). Because this one entry contains that correction, its source relationship is conservatively recorded as `adapts`.

records.title: Birnbaum’s principles in Venn diagrams: Extended version with Lean verification
records.abstract: We reformulate Birnbaum's theorem as a statement about classes of statistical procedures that preserve statistical relations, and show that the proof reduces to the propagation of evidential equality along chains of conditionality-related inference bases (experiment–observation pairs). For finite parameter spaces with at least two points, the sufficiency relation and the conditionality relation are incomparable, yet the corresponding preservation classes are nested. The class of likelihood-invariant procedures with codomain [0, 1] is strictly contained in the class of sufficiency-invariant procedures. The lower-tail likelihood-ratio p-value illustrates this strict inclusion.

records.title: Sharp symmetry bounds for real plane algebraic curves (Theorem 1)
records.abstract: Let C be an infinite real plane algebraic curve defined by a polynomial of degree d >= 2 that is irreducible over the complex numbers, and suppose C is not a circle. Its group of Euclidean symmetries is finite, the orientation-preserving part is cyclic of order at most max(d, 2d - 4), and the full group has order at most 2d. Both bounds are attained in every degree d >= 2. For d >= 5, curves attaining the rotation bound are exactly, up to orientation-preserving similarity, the curves Re(z^(d-2)(|z|^2 + a)) = 0 with |a| = 1 and a not real; conversely each such curve with d - 2 >= 3 attains the bound. This entry formalizes Theorem 1 of the note; the note's second theorem (Mobius symmetries and genus of the extremal family) is not part of this entry.

records.title: Several complex variables: local theory, Hartogs phenomena, Weierstrass theory, domains of holomorphy and pseudoconvexity
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization, on top of Mathlib, of the classical function theory of several complex variables on open subsets of finite-dimensional complex normed spaces, with values in complex Banach spaces wherever the statements allow. The compared statements cover: Cauchy's integral formula on polydiscs, Osgood's lemma, the equivalence of holomorphy and analyticity, the Cauchy-Riemann equations, Cauchy estimates, the identity theorem, the maximum modulus principle, holomorphic dependence of integrals and the Cauchy-Pompeiu identity; the theorems of Weierstrass, Montel and Vitali and an estimate for holomorphic L^p classes; the holomorphic inverse and implicit mapping theorems; Reinhardt domains, logarithmic convexity, the characterization of convergence domains of power series, Laurent expansion, and continuation from Reinhardt and circular domains; Hartogs-Taylor expansion, Hartogs' continuity theorem, Hartogs' theorem on separate analyticity, removability of isolated singularities, the two Riemann extension theorems and Hartogs' extension theorem for compact holes; elementary analytic sets and their regular points; the local ring of analytic germs, Weierstrass division and preparation, and the Noetherian and unique factorization properties of the germ ring; injective holomorphic maps, Cartan's uniqueness theorem, linearity of biholomorphisms of circular domains, transitivity of the automorphisms of the ball and the inequivalence of ball and polydisc; holomorphic hulls, domains of holomorphy, Thullen's lemma, the Cartan-Thullen theorem and Bochner's tube theorem; subharmonic and plurisubharmonic functions, the Levi form, pseudoconvexity of domains of holomorphy, Levi's theorem and local peak functions; Runge domains and polynomial hulls. All results are classical; none is claimed to be new.

records.title: A convex body variant of Soberon's counterexample to the Grünbaum conjecture.
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of a geometric strengthening/variant of Pablo Soberón's counterexample to the Grünbaum four-hyperplane mass-partition conjecture. The formalized result constructs a convex body K in R^4 with nonempty interior such that no four affine hyperplanes divide K into sixteen sign cells of equal four-dimensional volume.  Equivalently, the obstructed mass can be chosen to be uniform Lebesgue volume on a convex body.  The proof adapts Soberón's explicit cubic/quartic tensor obstruction and replaces the smooth positive density used in the source by a small Wulff-body perturbation of the Euclidean ball.

records.title: NKBesicovitch
records.abstract:
Lean proofs of Hausdorff dimension at least n-(n-k)/p_c^k for all (n,k)-Besicovitch sets with 1<=k<=n, and positive Lebesgue measure for Lebesgue measurable such sets when p_c^(k-1)+k>n. Here a Besicovitch set contains a translated unit k-disk in every k-dimensional direction, and p_c is the unique root in (2,3) of p^3-2p^2-2p+2=0.
Building on Bourgain's arithmetic-combinatorial approach, Nets Hawk Katz and Terence Tao's New bounds for Kakeya problems (2002; preprint 2001) established the Minkowski-dimension bound 1+(n-1)/beta_c, where beta_c=p_c/(p_c-1)=1.67513... satisfies beta_c^3-4*beta_c+2=0. This is exactly n-(n-1)/p_c, so the numerical exponent itself is not new. They also proved the distinct Hausdorff bound (2-sqrt(2))*(n-4)+3. A Minkowski lower bound alone does not imply the same Hausdorff lower bound: Hausdorff dimension is at most Minkowski dimension.
Richard Oberlin's subsequent X-ray work (2006 preprint; published 2010) gave the Hausdorff bound n-(n-k)/(1+sqrt(2))^k and positive measure when (1+sqrt(2))^(k-1)+k>n. Later polynomial-partitioning work by Hickman, Rogers, and Zhang improved Kakeya bounds in many dimensions while retaining the large-dimension leading coefficient 2-sqrt(2).
The claimed advance here is a continuous projection estimate with joint measurable parameter selection, developed from the supplied September 2026 manuscript. Its mixed-norm X-ray and plate maximal consequences, together with a countable-cover argument, give the Katz-Tao numerical bound for Hausdorff dimension and replace 1+sqrt(2)=2.41421... by p_c=2.48119... in Oberlin's displayed dimension and positive-measure ranges. For k=1 the resulting Hausdorff bound is approximately 0.596968*n+0.403032, with a larger leading coefficient than 2-sqrt(2)=0.585786.... This is an improvement in sufficiently high dimensions, not a claim to the best bound in every dimension. The formalized hypotheses require only unit disks, and the Hausdorff theorem requires neither measurability nor boundedness of the set.
Both geometric theorems and the exact bounds 2.481<p_c<2.482 are proved with only the standard Lean axioms. The comparisons above identify the improvement over the cited results; independent mathematical review and confirmation of novelty against the full literature remain pending. Final sandboxed Comparator and independent-kernel verification are pending.

records.title: Bounds 1.6855 and 3.879 for the planar centred Hardy-Littlewood maximal constant over squares
records.abstract:
Let c_d be the weak type (1,1) constant of the centred Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator over axis-parallel cubes in R^d: the least C such that alpha |{Mf > alpha}| <= C ||f||_1 for every integrable f and every level alpha. Its value is unknown for every d >= 2; in the plane the previously published lower bound is c_2 >= 3/4 - sqrt(2)/4 + sqrt(6)/2 = 1.62119... (Aldaz 2000) and the best known upper bound is 4.
This development proves c_2 >= Phi = 1.68550999335552518..., an explicit algebraic number of degree 16, from a lattice with unequal masses: columns at spacing h = (5 + sqrt 22)/6 carrying masses alternating 1 and w = (17 + 4 sqrt 22)/9, rows at spacing h + 1. It also proves 1.685 < Phi < 1.686, the classical covering bound c_d <= 2^d in every dimension, and an upper bound below the classical one in the plane, c_2 <= 3.879, by comparing the maximal operator with an explicit kernel for the Cauchy generator -|D_u| - |D_v|.

records.title: BKARForestFormula
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Brydges-Kennedy-Abdesselam-Rivasseau forest interpolation formula: for a finite vertex set V and a C-infinity function rho on the edge-coupling space of the complete graph on V, the value of rho at the all-ones coupling equals the sum, over all acyclic edge subsets (forests) F, of the integral over the unit cube [0,1]^E(F) of the mixed partial derivative of rho in the edge variables of F, evaluated at the path-minimum interpolation point x^F(u); the empty forest contributes rho(0). The flagship theorem is additionally restated Mathlib-only and re-proved in the leanprover/comparator challenge/solution format using Audit/ForestFormula/comparator.json.

records.title: Irrationality of the 7-adic zeta value ζ₇(3)
records.abstract: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib proof that the 7-adic zeta value ζ₇(3) is irrational. Here ζ₇(3) = L₇(3, ω⁻²) is the Kubota–Leopoldt value, equal to the 7-adic limit of the Euler-corrected Bernoulli numbers −(1 − 7^{w−1}) B_w / w over the weights w = 6·7^{n+1} − 2. The same is proved for η = ζ₇(3)/2. The proof is a determinant irrationality argument on the modular curve X₀(7), in four parts: independence of seven explicit germs attached to the weight −2 seven-adic Eisenstein series, with a uniform zero estimate; a seven-adic annular saving; an auxiliary-prime denominator estimate; and an Archimedean energy estimate with a kernel-checked numerical margin. It also uses an internal proof of the geometric continuation of the target series to every radius below 49, via a twisted U₇ matrix bound and initial overconvergence obtained from classical Eisenstein approximants. The Lean endpoints depend only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The mathematical argument has not been refereed. The work is human-directed, with extensive AI assistance in both the mathematics and the Lean development; see the automation section and PROVENANCE.md.

records.title: definable-saturated
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the relative consistency of ZFC + CH together with the following assertion. There is a countably saturated elementary extension of the natural-number arithmetic structure of cardinality aleph one; all such set-sized presentations are isomorphic; and no such presentation is ordinal definable. The class is defined without parameters. Removing CH from the asserted theory gives a consistent negative answer to MathOverflow question 382009 about definability up to isomorphism versus an ordinal-definable copy. Every notion in the final sentence is internal to the first-order model of set theory.

records.title: An interval-moment criterion for square-difference-free integer sets
records.abstract: We prove a general interval-moment criterion for square-difference-free integer sets and apply it to obtain an improved unconditional lower bound in Sarkozy's theorem, with exponent 0.75806746. If D(N) is the largest size of a subset of {1, ..., N} containing no two distinct elements whose difference is a square, then for every epsilon > 0 and all sufficiently large N we prove D(N) >= N^(0.75806746 - epsilon). The exact exponent is 37903373/50000000. The reusable criterion starts from finite digit sets in pairwise coprime square bases, with ordered intervals and width-moment inequalities. A strict surplus in the component exponents yields the asymptotic bound through finite stopping words, rank rounding, the Chinese remainder theorem, and interpolation between geometric scales. Both the general criterion and its numerical application are formalized in Lean. All nine concrete components are proved: six prime chains, a 25-state binary recursion, and the two complete composite witnesses for 215 and 437. Every required ordering, numerical moment, lifting, and asymptotic argument is checked, with no remaining finite-certificate hypotheses. The repository includes self-contained PDF and LaTeX write-ups of the full result and a simpler companion construction attaining exponent 0.758001 that explains several core ideas, together with exact computational certificate programs. The simpler construction is not separately formalized or a selected submission statement.

records.title: Finite tight Blackwell approachability-to-improper phi-regret reduction in Lean
records.abstract: A Mathlib-only nonempty finite-simplex, algorithmic specialization of Theorem 4 in Dann, Mansour, Mohri, Schneider, and Sivan (COLT 2025). It realizes the tensor action space as a joint simplex, defines the source improper comparator by adding a mixed-constraint tensor of the canonical action marginal, proves that comparator escapes the action set, and proves exact finite-horizon equality between approachability loss and improper phi-regret under explicit causal strategy translations in both directions. It also proves that every joint action is a mixture of at most one rank-one tensor per constraint index.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Erdős 689: eventual double covering by prime residue classes
records.abstract: A complete Lean 4 proof of Erdős problem 689: for all sufficiently large n, one residue class per prime p ≤ n can cover every integer from 1 through n at least twice. The proof follows the argument for Theorem 1.1 in Chojecki’s April 2026 manuscript “A greedy matching proof of Erdős’s two-fold residue-class problem.” The formalization directly proves the required three-prime counting estimate using Fourier analysis, replacing the manuscript’s invocation of Green–Tao, and verifies the sieve bounds and greedy-matching construction in Lean.

records.title: Critical Poisson fields and information-adapted conditioning
records.abstract: Poisson laws for the actual run field with positions, all excesses and signs; hard and soft small-prime conditioning, deterministic masks and statistics, stable recorded variables, uniform quenched convergence, and an information-adapted cutoff that respects a prescribed conditioning floor.

records.title: Typical dictionaries, exact marks and compound Poisson clusters
records.abstract: Poisson comparisons for word dictionaries, including mean distances for uniformly sampled fixed-size and affine dictionaries with each dictionary held fixed inside the comparison. Exact excesses and signs, category aggregation, geometric marks and compound Poisson cluster laws are retained.

records.title: Improved SparseStack Constants
records.abstract: Complete Lean proof of the revised SparseStack main theorem through its retained-count route. For every fixed real isometry, the actual independent uniform signed-bucket sketch with the rounded C=80, B=169/20 prescription has Gram-norm failure probability at most delta. The same prescription satisfies s<26.35 q/eps and m<176.9(d+q)/eps^2. All physical channel estimates and the all-order scalar certificate are proved.

records.title: A formal proof of the Kung–Traub conjecture
records.abstract: For deterministic stationary root-finding methods without memory, the Kung–Traub bound 2^(n-1) for n >= 1 real or complex scalar derivative observations, the bound given by the first group size times the product of one plus each subsequent size for prescribed positive groups, and entire counterexamples, including one real witness defeating every larger real exponent simultaneously. A concrete inverse Hermite method attains 2^(n-1) for n >= 2 on open real intervals and has that exact order on exp(x)-1. Supporting constructions are included.

records.title: Threshold staircases and the Poisson–Gaussian bridge
records.abstract: Joint Poisson–Gaussian limits for conditioned run counts, with an autoregressive Gaussian target and independent normal innovations. Quantitative results give local Poisson probabilities, a Gaussian distribution-function bound, moderate deviations, and relative local or tail estimates for the multiplicative source under the stated information budgets. The whole integer-level point process has locally finite but infinite total mass; its complete upper-half laws, conditioning on a fixed count and extreme phases are included. The two upper-half law assertions include proved measurability and probability normalization; conditioning on every finite count has positive mass. The intrinsic probability estimates are proved internally. Their arithmetic applications use, as applicable, the prime number theorem, scalar Stein bounds, the Poisson process estimate of Arratia, Goldstein and Gordon, and Barbour's corrected multivariate Stein bounds.

records.title: Erdős 973: power sums cannot all be exponentially small
records.abstract: A complete Lean 4 proof of the negative answer to Erdős problem 973: power sums of complex numbers on or outside the unit circle cannot all be exponentially small. For each fixed C > 1 and all sufficiently large n, any n such numbers have some order 2 ≤ k ≤ n+1 with |∑_i z_i^k| > C^(-n), even without the original condition z₁ = 1. The proof follows the residual-polynomial method in Tan, Wang, Huang, and Chen’s August 2026 paper “Residual bounds for Schur-stable polynomials,” using a fixed-degree polynomial test. This submission provides a complete machine-checked proof of the negative answer previously obtained by Luo, Yang, and Zhu.

records.title: Fischer's 24-vertex zero-forcing counterexample
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of Mikko Fischer's explicit connected 24-vertex subcubic graph with independence number 9 and zero-forcing number 11. The formalization verifies the exact graph and both numerical invariants, yielding an existential counterexample to the proposed bound Z(G) <= alpha(G) + 1 for connected graphs of maximum degree at most 3.

records.title: The order-six stable-marriage finite-poset bound
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of the finite-poset theorem that any finite poset with at most fifteen elements, width at most three, and the CI2 common-incomparability condition has at most forty-eight antichains.

records.title: Microscopic boundary, prefixes and longest runs
records.abstract: The exact left-border probability is 2^(-pi(L)), and the microscopic non-vacancy probability satisfies 0 <= q_L/2^(-pi(L)) - 1 <= 2^(-pi(L)/256) for sufficiently large L. The results give conditional localization and uniqueness, stability under changes of mesoscopic cutoff, and a quantitative Poisson law for runs contained in a finite prefix. They yield the critical longest-run distribution and asymmetric almost-sure envelopes for all integer prefix lengths. The exact border identity needs no literature hypothesis. The asymptotic results use, as applicable, scalar Stein bounds, the prime number theorem, the uniform prime-divisor estimate of Laishram and Shorey, Shorey's square-product exclusion, and the divisor bound of Nicolas and Robin.

records.title: Microscopic–bulk crossover and conditional affine laws
records.abstract: Conditioned on the presence of a run contained in a finite prefix, the first such run has a mixture law combining a microscopic border contribution with a uniform bulk location, geometric excess and fair sign. The results retain the marked record, describe both location scales in finite and infinite phase regimes, and determine the sign bias. Under compatible affine conditions on small primes, the border probability is exactly 2^(-d), where d is the row-space deficit. Affine localization and sign bias use the rank information budget without future neutrality; the full marked-clock limit also requires eventual neutrality for each fixed finite future prefix. Approximation uses the prime number theorem, the Poisson process estimate of Arratia, Goldstein and Gordon, and the stated Laishram–Shorey, Shorey and Nicolas–Robin estimates. The exact affine border identity needs none of these literature hypotheses.

records.title: One-Sided Affine Obstructions in Complete Bipartite Hat Guessing
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of manuscript Theorem 2.4: for every finite field K with |K| at least 4 and every m at least 1, a coordinatewise-affine strategy on the class of size |K|-1 cannot be completed to a winning strategy by arbitrary deterministic rules on the opposite class of size m, with respect to the fixed finite-field labeling.

records.title: An atomic decomposition of one-dimensional metric currents without boundary
records.abstract: This project formalizes all five main results of arXiv:2502.09871, "An atomic decomposition of one-dimensional metric currents without boundary" (Chen, Goodman, Hernandez, Spector), in Lean 4 against Mathlib.

records.title: Microscopic signed fields and empirical Poisson laws
records.abstract: Quantitative comparison of the actual position/excess/sign field at growing intensity, retaining the original small-prime conditioning; same-grid dyadic restriction and common measurable readouts. Along literal dyadic scales, empirical window counts converge almost surely to Poisson, while empirical full vectors have a positive total-variation obstruction.

records.title: Regular configurations, Palm deficits and the cumulant obstruction
records.abstract: Arithmetic regular configurations with private prime pivots, exact source–target Palm mass identities, ordinary deletion and normalized deficit bounds. The independent target is regular with probability tending to one, while absolute cumulant activity has a positive normalized lower bound on prime scales for original and stronger retained sets.

records.title: Lower bounds for sets without perfect-power differences
records.abstract: Let D_k(N) be the largest size of a subset of {1, ..., N} with no positive k-th-power difference. We prove D_k(N) >= c_k N^alpha_k for every N >= 1, with positive constants c_k and exponents 0.75806770413, 0.9142, and 0.95295 for squares, fourth powers, and sixth powers. The proofs use a general interval-moment criterion for every positive integer k. We also prove arithmetic lifting results, exact product and prime-depth laws for interval capacity, and existence of the binary square capacity limit. The square construction refines Naslund's published example while retaining its binary transition rules. All selected statements are proved in Lean.

records.title: Unrestricted Boolean multiplicative complexity of four-term polynomial multiplication
records.abstract: Formalizes the exact minimum AND-gate counts 0, 1, 3, 6 and 9 for binary polynomial multiplication with zero through four coefficients per operand. XOR and constants are free, and AND inputs may reuse arbitrary earlier nonlinear wires. The principal result excludes eight-gate four-term circuits and matches an explicit nine-gate construction. Separate research workflows check selected n5 quadratic results and n6 upper bounds and reductions; their open unrestricted/bilinear lower bounds are not claims of this submission.

records.title: A transexponential o-minimal structure
records.abstract: The real field expanded by the function $x\mapsto A(1+x^2)$, where $A$ is a normalized analytic Abel function for $e^x-1$, is an o-minimal structure that defines a function that grows faster than any finite iterate of the exponential function.

records.title: SCOPE and REACH with almost-surely finite stopping times
records.abstract: SCOPE and REACH are integrable unbiased estimators of an outcome-before-stopping probability for autoregressive models on countably infinite vocabularies. REACH is the conditional expectation of a two-stage Monte Carlo estimator given the outcome-free backbones. Its variance bound against ordinary Monte Carlo is derived from that Rao–Blackwell identity and the law of total variance, for every positive sample count. The development also proves the stopping-time property, almost-sure finiteness, and the bridge between the two sampling experiments.

records.title: A counterexample to the unrestricted form of Eden's conjecture
records.abstract: For every c > 4, an explicit polynomial ODE on Euclidean five-space has a compact global attractor and uniformly negative divergence. Its finite-time local Lyapunov dimension at every positive real time and its asymptotic Kaplan--Yorke dimension have maximum 4 + 4/c, attained precisely on an invariant two-torus with irrational angular flow. The maximum over equilibria and periodic points is 3. All singular-value exponents exist, and local dimensions converge pointwise. This disproves the unrestricted form of Eden's conjecture; the attractor is not assumed transitive.

records.title: Small undecidable groups and fixed-size Adian–Rabin families
records.abstract: Lean 4 proofs of the algebraic results in Small undecidable groups and unrecognizable 4-manifolds (arXiv:2609.10461v1): existence of a group with a three-generator, nine-relator presentation and unsolvable word problem; an effective family of four-generator, eleven-relator presentations with undecidable triviality; and an effective family of two-generator, ten-relator presentations with undecidable triviality. These are Theorems 1.1, 1.3, and 1.4 of the paper. The four-manifold consequences in the paper are outside the formalized scope.

records.title: CaffarelliKohnNirenberg
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg partial regularity theory for suitable weak solutions of the three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with forcing in L^q, q > 5/2: the L^3 epsilon-regularity theorem (Theorem A), the gradient epsilon-regularity criterion (Theorem B) and the vanishing of the one-dimensional parabolic Hausdorff measure of the singular set (Theorem C). The three theorems are proved using only the standard axioms, restated together in a Mathlib-only comparator challenge and proved from the library theorems. The manuscript being formalized is in the repository and was corrected alongside the development.

records.title: Zero density theorems for short intervals
records.abstract:
Explicit zero-density results for the Riemann zeta function in short intervals, formalized in Lean 4 over Mathlib.  Count the nontrivial zeros whose imaginary part lies in a window (t-h, t+h], with multiplicity and with a zero on either horizontal edge counted for half.
Seven statements are submitted, and all seven are mechanically checked.  Two are zero-density bounds for the edge strip Re s > 1-alpha, valid for 0 <= h <= t^(2/3), proved by two different mechanisms -- Jensen's formula and Littlewood's lemma, the source's Theorems 2 and 3.  Neither dominates the other over the whole parameter range.  Two turn those into bounds on the fraction of the window's zeros lying in that strip, and are antitone in both h0 and t0, so one evaluation bounds every larger window: Corollaries 4 and 5.  The remaining three are the headline corollary, Corollary 1 -- for every alpha in (0, 1/6) there are h0 and t0 beyond which a definite fraction of the window's zeros, bounded below by an explicit POSITIVE constant, have real part in the middle band [alpha, 1-alpha], away from both edges of the critical strip.  One states it with the constant named, one with the constant existentially quantified as the source phrases it, and one at the explicit parameters alpha = 1/16 with a sharper radius, where the limiting constant is 9/25.
The positivity is proved, not assumed, and needs no numerics: every term of the constant except the leading one carries a factor 1/h or 1/log t, so it tends to a limit fixed by one rational inequality, which the radius 1/2 discharges for every admissible alpha.  The factor of two relating the two edge strips is the reflection rho -> 1 - conj(rho), proved in the development to be a multiplicity-preserving involution of the zero set.
The results are conditional and their hypotheses are in the signature, not hidden.  They are of two kinds, kept apart in the development because a reader is entitled to weigh them differently.  Sixteen are published explicit bounds on zeta and Gamma transcribed from other authors; eleven are finite numerical certificates established outside Lean by arb ball arithmetic or mpmath on explicit compact boxes, which Mathlib cannot currently reproduce because it has no verified evaluation of zeta and the margins reach 9e-17.  The source's tables give the numerical values of the constant; they are not load-bearing for its sign.
`comparator.json` names exactly those seven and is the authority on what is checked.  Beyond them, the wider development supplies what they rest on: the Littlewood short-interval theorem (Theorem 32), the argument-integral machinery (Theorem 31), the appendix of explicit zeta bounds, the Laurent expansion of zeta'/zeta, and the reflection step.

records.title: Positive density of Collatz convergence at every rate above 3/log(4/3)
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of eighteen selected Phase 1 statements, led by a single positive lower natural-density constant for the set of positive integers reaching 1 within c log x ordinary Collatz steps, valid for every fixed c > 3/log(4/3). It also covers fixed-target hitting, the exact target criterion, individual-root consequences, vanishing-clock-loss variants, depth-eleven density bounds, exact finite fan allocation, real-moment comparison, target profiles, and bounded actual reference entropy with explicit tail estimates and zero normalized growth. Density witnesses and levels are existential. Full optimized formulas, complementary capacity, the Renyi-order right limit, amplified roots, and convergence of every positive integer remain outside the formalized scope.

records.title: Unit-distance graphs of dimension four with nine edges
records.abstract: A graph has dimension n when n is the least number such that its vertices can be placed injectively in ℝⁿ with every edge of length one (Erdős, Harary and Tutte). House proved that a graph of dimension four has at least nine edges, and that nine is attained only by K_{3,3}. This project proves the second half in Lean 4, in the form google-deepmind/formal-conjectures states it as erdos_1007.variants.dimension_four_extremal: a graph of dimension four with nine edges and no isolated vertex is isomorphic to K_{3,3}. The proof follows Chaffee and Noble's proof of House's theorem. On the way it proves that K_{3,3} has dimension exactly four and that every graph with at most eight edges has a unit-distance representation in ℝ³ (Chaffee–Noble, Theorem 6).

records.title: Verified finite automata for finitely generated subgroups of F₂
records.abstract: Source-based formalization of the classical Stallings finite-graph recognition theorem. It gives an executable finite folding construction for every finite list of words in the rank-two free group, with exact subgroup-membership correctness. The least deterministic fold congruence is computed by finite exhaustive search; there is no complexity claim or implementation of core trimming, subgroup bases, intersections, or index algorithms.

records.title: The Favard-length decay exponent of the four-corner Cantor set is at least 1/4
records.abstract: For the four-corner Cantor set approximants K_n = C_n × C_n, where C_n is the union of the 2^n intervals of length 4^{-n} with left endpoints sum_{j<=n} w_j 4^{-j}, w_j in {0,3}, let α_Fav be the supremum of the a >= 0 for which the Favard length Fav(K_n) = (1/π) ∫_0^π |π_θ(K_n)| dθ is at most C n^{-a} for all n >= 1. This project proves in Lean that every a < 1/4 is admissible, so 1/4 <= α_Fav, together with the classical bound α_Fav <= 1. The previous best lower bounds were 1/6 (Nazarov-Peres-Volberg, 2010) and 1/5 (Marshall, arXiv:2509.02882 v2, 2026, whose v1 claim of 1/4 was withdrawn). The new ingredient is a joint negative-moment estimate for the low-frequency cosine product. The argument comes from an unpublished AI-assisted manuscript, and this formalization is its first complete proof.

records.title: Absence of bounded-orbit wandering domains
records.abstract: We prove that transcendental entire functions do not have bounded-orbit wandering domains. This answers a major open question in the field. The proof builds upon Zihao Ye's new proof of Sullivan's No Wandering Domains theorem, and was obtained with assistance by generative AI.  We also formalise a stronger theorem, which shows that locally defined holomorphic functions do not have orbits of simply connected wandering domains. The formalisation includes a number of classical results that were implemented as auxiliary results, including results concerning the hyperbolic metric for a finitely punctured sphere, and its area.

records.title: The quasi-isometry classes of Galton–Watson trees: Lean formalisation
records.abstract: Lean 4 formalisation of the automorphism-matching theorems and the quasi-isometry classification of Galton–Watson trees from the paper "The quasi-isometry classes of Galton–Watson trees" by Jayadev S. Athreya and Sascha Troscheit (arXiv:2609.23882). The audited statements are: the i.i.d. matching theorem on the binary tree (leaf and full bounds, and the existence of a root-fixing automorphism of the infinite binary tree matching two independent i.i.d. labellings with probability at least 1 - 16 η_{5/2}, where η_{5/2} is the one-site potential of the label law); the general Markov matching theorem for typed label processes on the binary tree, in its finite-type and zero-compatible forms at finite and at infinite height, with a failure probability at most a constant multiple of the one-site defect; the complete classification, up to quasi-isometry, of Galton–Watson trees with finitely supported offspring law conditioned on infinite diameter, into the ray class, the binary-tree class, one chain class for each branching semigroup, and the bushy class, with two independent conditioned trees almost surely quasi-isometric exactly when their laws share a class, together with the finite class, so that over the unconditioned laws two trees are almost surely quasi-isometric exactly when both are finite or both are infinite with laws in the same class; the mutual embeddability theorem, that a Galton–Watson tree with finitely supported supercritical offspring law, conditioned on infinite diameter, almost surely admits quasi-isometric embeddings into the binary tree and from it; and, for offspring supported on {1,2}, almost sure quasi-isometry together with an explicit exponential bound on the failure probability of a (D^2+3)-quasi-isometry. The statements are made in Challenge.lean over Mathlib alone and discharged by Solution.lean from four library targets.

records.title: Erdős 1007, dimension five: fifteen edges, attained by K6 and K1,3,3
records.abstract: The least number of edges of a graph of Euclidean dimension five (Erdős–Harary–Tutte) is 15, and both K6 and K1,3,3 attain it (Chaffee and Noble 2016). These are formal-conjectures' erdos_1007.variants.dimension_five and dimension_five_extremal. A graph has dimension n when n is the least dimension in which its vertices can be placed injectively with every edge a unit segment. The lower bound is Chaffee and Noble's Theorem 10: every graph with at most fourteen edges has such a placement in ℝ⁴. Its proof removes a vertex of degree at most three, joins that vertex's neighbours to one another, places the smaller graph by induction, and returns the vertex to one of the infinitely many points at distance one from its neighbours. A graph whose degrees are all at least four has at most seven vertices, and those graphs are handled case by case. For attainment, K6 has dimension five because six points at pairwise distance one fit in ℝ⁵ but not in ℝ⁴. K1,3,3 has dimension five by Theorem 8: it has an explicit placement in ℝ⁵, and an orthogonal-complement count rules out ℝ⁴. The supporting results are in GraphDimension, a separate Lean library on the dimension of graphs, which this repository pins by revision. The question belongs to discrete geometry and extremal graph theory, specifically the study of unit-distance representations and the dimension of graphs.

records.title: Classical Seifert–van Kampen theorem for the fundamental groupoid
records.abstract: Proves that for every topological space X and open cover X = U ∪ V, the inclusion-induced square of Mathlib's ordinary continuous-path fundamental groupoids for U ∩ V, U, V, and X is a pushout in Cat. The statement retains all points as objects and assumes no basepoint, connectedness, or separation conditions. The proof uses continuous paths and endpoint-preserving homotopies, specializes an auxiliary preorder to the indiscrete relation, and proves a natural equivalence with Mathlib's ordinary fundamental groupoid. It constructs the categorical descent functor by path subdivision and proves homotopy invariance by a square subdivision; it does not invoke the imported directed van Kampen theorem.

records.title: A left PCI left V-domain that is not right PCI and not a right V-domain
records.abstract:
A countable domain R that is a left PCI ring (every cyclic left module not isomorphic to R is injective) and a left V-ring (every simple left module is injective), but is not right Ore, not a right PCI ring and not a right V-ring. Consequently the opposite ring of R is a right PCI ring that is not left PCI.
This answers in the negative the question of Faith (1973), Cozzens and Faith (Simple Noetherian Rings, 1975) and Damiano (1979) whether every right PCI ring is left PCI, and the question, going back to Cozzens and Faith (1975), whether a left V-domain must be a right V-domain.
The ring is an Ore extension K[t; σ, δ] over a free field K (Cohn's universal field of fractions of a free algebra over the rationals) with a non-surjective endomorphism σ, built by iteratively adjoining free solutions of the pseudo-linear equations that govern divisibility of the cyclic modules R/Rf.
The mathematics, the accompanying paper and the Lean code were produced by AI models (Anthropic's Claude) at a human's direction; no human expert has checked the mathematics.

records.title: Dimension-independent Hlawka constants for Schatten norms
records.abstract: For every Schatten p-norm with 1 < p < infinity, a finite Hlawka constant exists that does not depend on dimension, and at both endpoints (trace norm, p = 1; operator norm, p = infinity) no constant exists. For complex diagonal matrices and every real p >= 256, the sharp constant is an explicit maximum over a one-parameter cyclic family: it holds in every dimension and cannot be lowered in any dimension at least three.

records.title: lean-LCS: locally convex spaces, duality, and closed graph theorems in Lean 4
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization, built on Mathlib, of the basic theory of locally convex topological vector spaces over the real or complex numbers. It covers barrelled, quasi-barrelled, bornological and ultrabornological spaces; the closed graph and open mapping theorems for barrelled spaces, and Pták's closed graph and open mapping theorems; duality theory with the bipolar, Alaoglu–Bourbaki, Mackey, Mackey–Arens, Banach–Dieudonné and Krein–Šmulian theorems and Grothendieck's completeness theorem; semi-reflexive, reflexive and Montel spaces with their permanence properties; completeness of strong duals; countable strict inductive limits, with the Dieudonné–Schwartz theorem; Milman's converse to the Krein–Milman theorem; and webbed spaces with De Wilde's closed graph and open mapping theorems. The Palomar entry compares 52 theorems from these areas; their statements and the notions they use are in Challenge.lean. The results are classical textbook and research results; the formalization proves them without sorry and without additional axioms.

records.title: Shapley value axiomatic characterization
records.abstract: Formalizes finite TU cooperative games, the Shapley value formula, and the four axioms of efficiency, symmetry, the null-player property, and additivity. It proves that the Shapley value satisfies all four and proves uniqueness via unanimity games and Möbius inversion over the Boolean lattice. This is a reusable formalization artifact, not a claim of new mathematics.

records.title: Weighted support criteria for reciprocal Mersenne subseries
records.abstract:
For an infinite set A of positive integers and an integer base b at least 2, consider the reciprocal Mersenne subseries X_A(b) = sum over a in A of 1/(b^a - 1). For a finite nonempty set P of primes, write h_P(a) for the P-part of a. The principal theorem proves irrationality when sum over a in A of h_P(a)/(a*(b^h_P(a) - 1)) converges. The base-two condition implies irrationality at every integer base at least 2 for every infinite subset of the host support. This is a sufficient support criterion, not a solution of the universal Erdős problem. It includes reciprocal-summable supports; the paper credits Erdős for that earlier stated all-base criterion and makes no identification with his suggested weakenings.
The five selected statements also give cofinally arbitrarily small positive weighted displacements, a strengthened positive divisor-cover criterion, and two common-average mixed-support extensions, one using an arbitrary positive weight budget. The proof averages displacements along multiples of a finite divisibility modulus, with another average controlling incomplete periods. Rationality would instead separate every positive displacement from zero. These extensions retain their explicit cover, summability, positivity and infinite-subset assumptions. Full support and all odd exponents are outside the weighted criterion; failure of the criterion is not a rationality assertion. The paper's achievement-set geometry, rational-membership tests and finite-denominator results are outside this registration. This entry supplies independently stated Challenge declarations and matching Lean proofs, with links to the complete paper and reasoning record; it makes no claim of independent human peer review or a novelty verdict.

records.title: Tree stacking equals the Csernák--Soukup estimator on nontrivial finite trees
records.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of the corrected nontrivial-tree form of the Csernák--Soukup tree-stacking conjecture. For every finite tree with at least two vertices, the exact-size stacking number equals the explicit rooted-distance-and-degree estimator. The one-vertex case is excluded because the source stacking-number convention restricts admissible thresholds to t >= 2 while the displayed estimator is 1 on the one-vertex tree.

records.title: Nonnegativity cutoffs for level-one modular forms
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of the qualitative well-definedness of the nonnegativity Sturm bound A(k) for real level-one modular forms. For every weight k at least 12 and divisible by four, the formalization proves that a finite initial segment detects coefficientwise nonnegativity and that its optimal endpoint is attained as the greatest possible first negative Fourier-coefficient index.

records.title: An exact counterexample to the D-unstable-core conjecture for parameter-rich reaction networks
records.abstract: Vassena and Stadler conjectured that a reaction network with parameter-rich kinetics cannot have a Hurwitz-unstable Jacobian unless it contains a D-unstable core, a minimal square child-selection submatrix that becomes unstable under positive column scaling. We show that this conjecture is false. We construct a consistent reaction network with four species and five reactions and an admissible reactivity matrix for which the Jacobian has an eigenvalue with strictly positive real part, yet the network has no D-unstable core. Consistency is witnessed by a strictly positive stoichiometric kernel flux, and reactivities are positive exactly on reactant incidences. The counterexample and the resulting negation of the universal necessity statement are proved in Lean 4 with Mathlib.

records.title: Nash bargaining solution axiomatic characterization
records.abstract: Formalizes two-player bargaining problems with compact convex feasible sets, the four Nash axioms (Pareto optimality, symmetry, invariance to positive affine transformations, independence of irrelevant alternatives), and the Nash product. It proves existence and uniqueness of the Nash product maximizer, shows the maximizer satisfies the four axioms, and proves Nash's characterization: any bargaining solution satisfying the four axioms selects the Nash product maximizer. This is a reusable formalization artifact, not a claim of new mathematics.

records.title: Sunflower bounds
records.abstract: Lean proofs of the ALWZ and Rao–Bell–Chueluecha–Warnke sunflower bounds, robust-sunflower upper and lower bounds, the BCW spread and satisfying results, and the classical Erdős–Rado theorem. The submission compares ten explicit finite statements, including second-moment and Janson routes to the ALWZ bound.

records.title: Formalization of Scott's Measurement Structures and Linear Inequalities in Lean 4
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / mathlib formalization of Dana Scott's 1964 paper *Measurement Structures and Linear Inequalities* (Journal of Mathematical Psychology 1 (1964), 233–247). The paper derives necessary and sufficient conditions for three finite representation problems — intransitive indifference, ordered differences, and subjective probability — from the general solvability criterion for finite systems of linear inequalities. The development also covers Scott's ordered-group and signed-charge remarks, literal vector cancellation, and the KPS obstruction to de Finetti's five axioms. Every compared equivalence is described predicate-by-predicate in Challenge.lean and the README, including its numerical-representation side and its qualitative cancellation, permutation, reversal, probability, or Kelley-cover side. The additional infinite theorem is a new, stronger modern characterization first stated in this project; it adapts Kelley's 1959 countable-cover/separation method and is not attributed to Scott. The Lean development was drafted with AI-agent assistance under Lars Warren Ericson's direction and review. Dana S. Scott, Vijay D'Silva, and Brian Milnes are co-authors of the formalization report. There is no sorry outside the deliberate holes in Challenge.lean, no project-defined axiom, and Mathlib is the only Lake dependency.

records.title: HighContrastHomogenization
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of "Homogenization at a polynomial scale in high contrast" by Armstrong, Kuusi and Loher. The paper studies elliptic equations in random media whose conductivity can vary greatly. It proves that their large-scale behavior becomes predictable at a length bounded by a polynomial in the parameters measuring contrast and randomness, improving earlier bounds. The formalization includes quantitative convergence estimates, approximation by an effective constant-coefficient equation, and large-scale regularity results. It builds on the CoarseGraining library.

records.title: Pascal Minus-One GCD
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of p-adic valuations for the restricted binomial gcd G(N;m) = gcd{C(N,k) : 0 < k < N, m divides k}. The principal submitted result gives the complete valuation formula for primes p congruent to -1 modulo m, including the mixed-parity digit-sum branch and the exceptional p = m - 1 valuation-2 case. The repository also proves the complementary p congruent to 1 branch, a prime-power scaling reduction, and complete prime-by-prime formulas for m = 3, 4, and 6.

records.title: Irrationality of the Riemann zeta value at five
records.abstract: Formalization of the irrationality claim for the real value of the Riemann zeta function at five in Aabir Fauzan's September 2026 preprint. The two compared statements assert irrationality of this zeta value and of the sum of reciprocal fifth powers. The development constructs integer polynomials using normalized Hankel determinants, proves positivity and decay estimates, and derives irrationality. The paper's quantitative irrationality-measure claim is not part of this submission.

records.title: Unistationarity of Type II_l autocatalytic cores with positive degradation
records.abstract: We prove that every source-minimal Type II_l autocatalytic core with l >= 3, reversible mass-action kinetics and strictly positive species degradation has at most one positive stationary state. The result covers the literal weak source grammar, including its separated cyclic realizations and the fully coincident three-species case. Any two positive concentration states satisfying the stationary equations of the same core are equal. The uniqueness theorem is proved in Lean 4 with Mathlib.

records.title: Attainment of 2n-1 positive steady states in sequential distributive phosphorylation
records.abstract: For every integer n >= 1, the standard sequential distributive n-site phosphorylation mechanism admits positive reaction rates and 2n-1 distinct positive stationary states with common positive kinase, phosphatase and substrate totals. The construction establishes a uniform lower bound on the number of positive equilibria of the full mass-action system.

records.title: Linear-size autocatalytic sets are asymptotically absent in the sparse binary polymer model
records.abstract: In the sparse binary-polymer model with reversible ligation and cleavage, fix the food-length bound t, a nonnegative catalysis intensity lambda, and a linear reaction budget Cn. As the maximum polymer length n tends to infinity, the probability of a nonempty reflexively autocatalytic and food-generated reaction set with at most Cn channels tends to zero. The probability that some molecule catalyses a nonempty food-generated reaction set that constructs that molecule also tends to zero. These statements address the linear-size and single-molecule self-construction questions for the sparse catalysis law.

records.title: Heights, Siegel's lemma, Roth's theorem and the Subspace Theorems in Lean
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib development of Schmidt's Subspace Theorem and the theory beneath it, following Bombieri–Gubler, Heights in Diophantine Geometry (Chapters 1–7), and Schmidt's route in general. Two libraries, sorry-free and within Lean's three standard axioms. ArithmeticHeights builds heights of points, polynomials, matrices and linear subspaces, Northcott and Kronecker, Minkowski's second theorem, Siegel's lemma and the Bombieri–Vaaler theorems. DiophantineApproximation builds on it Roth's theorem over a number field with several places (and Ridout, the p-adic form, targets at infinity, moving targets), the geometry of numbers of approximation domains, and the Subspace Theorem: parametric, with coefficients in K, with algebraic coefficients, for S-integral points, and in Vojta's general-position form. It then proves the applications — Schmidt's simultaneous approximation, a transcendence criterion, unit equations, decomposable-form, Thue–Mahler, hyperelliptic and norm-form equations, the Corvaja–Zannier gcd bound — and Evertse's quantitative steps: systems of inequalities, the gap principles, the count of small solutions, and the passage from height intervals to subspaces. Twenty-six headline statements are compared: seven forms of Siegel's lemma and Bombieri–Vaaler, seven of Roth's theorem, seven of the Subspace Theorem, and five of Evertse's counting of the subspaces.

records.title: At least one of the 2-adic zeta values ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9), ζ₂(11) is irrational
records.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof that at least one of the 2-adic zeta values ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9), ζ₂(11) is irrational. The theorem has no hypotheses, and its proof uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The values are defined through the Volkenborn integral: zeta2 s = J(s−1)/((s−1)·2^s), where J(s) is the 2-adic limit of the Riemann sums 2^(−N) Σ_{x<2^N} (x+1/2)^(−s), and the theorem also proves that these limits exist. By Lemma 2.8 of Lai, Sprang and Zudilin (IMRN 2026), zeta2 s is the Kubota–Leopoldt value ζ₂(s) = L₂(s, ω^(1−s)) for s ≥ 2. That identification is cited, not formalised; it only involves a non-zero rational factor, which does not affect irrationality. The result sharpens Theorem 1.1 (case s = 3) of L. Lai (Int. J. Number Theory 2025), which shows that at least one of ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9), ζ₂(11), ζ₂(13) is irrational. The proof uses linear forms S_n = −∫ R_n'''(t+1/2) dt in 1, ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9), ζ₂(11), with R_n(t) = 2^(16n)(2t+n)(t+1/2)_n^8/(t)_(n+1)^8. Their denominators are controlled by a one-power saving that comes from Andrews' multiple-series transformation (proved here in Lean) and by the prime number theorem (proved here from a vendored Lean proof of the Wiener–Ikehara theorem). The exact 2-adic valuation of S_n along n = 2^m − 1 shows that S_n ≠ 0, and Lai's irrationality criterion concludes. The mathematics and the Lean code were produced by AI agents under human direction and have not been refereed.

records.title: Arrow's impossibility theorem (general finite version)
records.abstract: Formalizes Arrow's impossibility theorem for finitely many voters and finitely many alternatives (at least three): every social welfare function satisfying unanimity and independence of irrelevant alternatives is dictatorial. The proof follows the classical decisive-coalition argument: field expansion (a coalition decisive for one pair is decisive for every pair) and group contraction (a decisive coalition with at least two voters contains a smaller decisive coalition), iterated down to a singleton dictator. This is a reusable formalization artifact, not a claim of new mathematics.

records.title: Same-ground RAF realizability of finite interior operators and the four-reaction threshold for the empty-or-at-least-three family
records.abstract: Addressing the RAF-realizability question in Section 4 of Mike Steel's Interior Operators and Their Relationship to Autocatalytic Networks (arXiv:2305.16714v4, 2023), we characterize which interior operators on the subsets of a finite set E are maxRAF operators of catalytic reaction systems whose reaction set is exactly E. An interior operator is represented by its family of fixed sets, a union-closed family containing the empty set. A same-ground realization is a system with one reaction per element of E, finitely many molecule types, a food set and a catalysis relation; it realizes the empty set together with its RAFs, the nonempty reaction sets whose reactants arise from food by iterated closure under the selected reactions and whose reactions are each catalysed by a molecule of that closure. Such a family has a same-ground realization if and only if it is the intersection of an accessible union-closed family A and a predecessor-support family. Here A contains the empty set, is closed under unions, and every nonempty member of A has an element whose removal leaves a member of A; the members of A need not cover E. A set S is supported by a predecessor map P on E when every element e of S has some element of S in P(e), loops allowed. The family consisting of the empty set and all subsets of size at least three has a same-ground realization if and only if E has at most four elements. This gives the sharp threshold for the family considered in Proposition 5 and its subsequent remarks in Steel (2023). Both results are formalized in Lean 4 with Mathlib.

records.title: At least one of the 2-adic zeta values ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9) is irrational
records.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof that at least one of the 2-adic zeta values ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9) is irrational. The theorem has no hypotheses, and its proof uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The values are defined through the Volkenborn integral: zeta2 s = J(s−1)/((s−1)·2^s), where J(s) is the 2-adic limit of the Riemann sums 2^(−N) Σ_{x<2^N} (x+1/2)^(−s), and the theorem also proves that these limits exist. By Lemma 2.8 of Lai, Sprang and Zudilin (IMRN 2026), zeta2 s is the Kubota–Leopoldt value ζ₂(s) = L₂(s, ω^(1−s)) for s ≥ 2. That identification is cited, not formalised; it only involves a non-zero rational factor, which does not affect irrationality. The result sharpens Theorem 1.1 (case s = 3) of L. Lai (Int. J. Number Theory 2025), which shows that at least one of ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9), ζ₂(11), ζ₂(13) is irrational, and it implies the companion result, formalised in a separate repository, that at least one of ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9), ζ₂(11) is irrational. The proof uses linear forms S_n = ∫ R_n'''(t+1/2) dt in 1, ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9) built from the shifted well-poised rational functions R_n(t) = (2t+n) Π_{m=1}^{6} (t+1/2−h_m)_(n+2h_m) / (t)_(n+1)^6 with h = (n/40)(−17, 1, 2, 3, 5, 6). The 2-adic size of S_n comes from Lai's and Sprang's Δ-calculus. The size of the coefficients comes from a contour-integral representation and a saddle-point bound, whose numerical inequalities are certified in Lean. The odd part of the denominators is bounded by Legendre-type counts at the poles, the vanishing of R_n at half-integers, kernel-checked certificates and the prime number theorem (proved here from a vendored Lean proof of the Wiener–Ikehara theorem). If both values were rational, the valuations of the coefficients at the prime n − 1 (an idea of Lai and Sprang) would make S_n non-zero for infinitely many n, and Lai's irrationality criterion gives the contradiction. The mathematics and the Lean code were produced by AI agents under human direction and have not been refereed.

records.title: MAF composition criteria, exact enumeration of child-selection autocatalytic cores, and degradation regions of linear diluted source networks
