records.abstract: We establish three sets of results addressing published questions about the composition, enumeration and degradation of autocatalytic reaction networks. In response to the composition questions of Gagrani, Wang, De Decker and Lacoste (arXiv:2603.02627, Discussion and outlook), we give exact criteria for strict increases in the maximum amplification factor (MAF) under reaction addition, nonnegative species aggregation and shared-species coupling, assuming nonnegative inputs and attained MAFs. A block direct sum attains the larger component MAF, while an explicit example shows that component MAFs alone do not determine the MAF of a coupled network. Addressing the CS-core enumeration direction of Golnik, Gatter, Stadler and Vassena (arXiv:2603.02770, Section 6), we prove exact reconstruction from a complete list of ordinary-core anchor matchings, each unique on its vertex set, by alternating-path generation and certified rational semipositivity filtering. We establish existence of the certified test, its rejection of the empty matching, and an explicit nonempty instance for A → 2A. For the arbitrary-degradation question discussed by Nandan, Nghe and Unterberger (arXiv:2507.15546, Section 6), we characterize growth, criticality and extinction for irreducible linear diluted source networks with nonnegative unary reaction data and species degradation d ≥ 0: the real spectral bound of A − diag(d) is positive, zero or negative exactly when d is componentwise strictly below, equal to or strictly above (Av)_i/v_i for some positive v. We also characterize partial-actuation stabilizability of Metzler matrices through a positive-vector certificate on the unactuated block. All eleven selected statements are formalized in Lean 4 with Mathlib.

records.title: Gibbard-Satterthwaite theorem (strategy-proof social choice)
records.abstract: Formalizes the Gibbard-Satterthwaite theorem for finite electorates and finite alternative sets with at least three alternatives: every onto, strategy-proof social choice function is dictatorial. The proof constructs a social welfare function and reduces to Arrow's impossibility theorem.

records.title: Erdős Problem #1220 in Lean 4: the affirmative statement is not provable in ZFC
records.abstract: Erdős problem #1220 (erdosproblems.com/1220; Erdős–Hajnal 1971): let λ be a singular cardinal such that both λ and cf(λ) are ℵ₀-inaccessible (μ^ℵ₀ < κ for all μ < κ); does λ → (λ, ℵ₁)² hold?  This formalization settles the question as asked on erdosproblems.com in the negative sense "not provable": ZFC does not prove that every such λ satisfies λ → (λ, ℵ₁)² (erdos1220_not_provable : ¬ (ZFC ⊨ᵇ Erdos1220)), i.e. there is a model of ZFC with a singular λ, λ and cf(λ) ℵ₀-inaccessible, and λ ↛ (λ, ℵ₁)².  Shelah and Stanley (Sh:258, Ann. Pure Appl. Logic 36 (1987)) showed that a negative answer is consistent with ZFC.  This project formalizes that consistency result: the comparator target erdos1220_not_provable : ¬ (ZFC ⊨ᵇ Erdos1220) is stated for literally the same first-order theory ZFC, language and ZFSet interpretation as elliotglazer/erdos501's comparator challenge (imported from its statement module Erdos501.FOL.Statement), together with a faithfulness theorem erdos1220_sentence_faithful: in Mathlib's ZFSet the sentence Erdos1220 holds iff the Mathlib-level statement Erdos1220.Problem1220 holds.  The witness is the ground-model singular strong-limit cardinal λ = ℶ_{𝔠⁺} (cf λ = 𝔠⁺; λ and cf λ are ℵ₀-inaccessible without any deep cardinal-arithmetic input), not ℵ_{𝔠⁺}.  The forcing is the Shelah–Stanley §3 forcing, formalized as block-preserving, block-covering histories of basic conditions (weak extension order), with the μ⁺-strategic closure (hence μ-distributivity) and the (2^μ)⁺-chain condition proved in ZFC without GCH (Δ-system lemma for (2^μ)⁺ sets of size ≤ μ, blueprint counting (2^μ)^μ = 2^μ).  In the Boolean-valued model of its regular-open algebra (built with the Lean 4 port of Han–van Doorn's Flypitch vendored by erdos501) the hypotheses on λ are preserved, the generic colouring of [λ]² has neither a red homogeneous set of size λ nor a blue homogeneous set of size ℵ₁, and Flypitch's completeness theorem turns this into a two-valued model of ZFC satisfying ¬Erdos1220.  Both targets are proved from propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only and pass the Lean comparator.  Only the negative direction is claimed: independence (consistency of a positive answer) is NOT claimed.

records.title: Myerson-Satterthwaite impossibility theorem (continuous bilateral-trade version)
records.abstract: Formalizes the continuous-type bilateral-trade impossibility result: no mechanism can satisfy ex post efficiency (almost surely), Bayesian incentive compatibility, interim individual rationality, and weak ex ante budget balance when buyer and seller supports overlap. The proof uses payoff equivalence and envelope identities, together with the strict rent-gap identity B + C > S.

records.title: Hamilton cycles in Cayley graphs of polylogarithmic degree
records.abstract: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the following theorem: there are absolute constants C, n0 > 0 such that every connected Cayley graph Cay(G, S) on n >= n0 vertices whose degree d = |S| is at least C (log n)^13 / log log n contains a Hamilton cycle (Lovasz.hamiltonian_of_polylog_degree). Here G is a finite group, S is a connection set (S = S^-1 and 1 not in S, so the graph is |S|-regular), log is the natural logarithm, and connectivity is equivalent to S generating G. The theorem is a case of the Lovász conjecture (every connected vertex-transitive graph has a Hamilton path) in its Cayley-graph form (every connected Cayley graph on at least three vertices is Hamiltonian). For arbitrary connected Cayley graphs the previously published degree thresholds were linear degree (Christofides, Hladký and Máthé, 2014) and degree at least n^(1-c) (Bedert, Draganić, Müyesser and Pavez-Signé, 2026). The proof follows the source manuscript: it extracts a connected bipartite template with spectral gap of order (log n)^-2, allocates the vertices to weighted translates of the template by signed rounding (a robust signed integrality theorem derived from the capacitated b-matching polytope, swap rounding, and a trace-exponential matrix concentration bound), connects the pieces by a sparse matching chosen by mutual nominations and a signed circulation, absorbs the outside matching inside every piece with Hamilton routers built from even-cycle comparators, and merges cycles. Every lemma of the manuscript is proved in the repository, as are the classical results it uses without proof (normalized Cheeger inequality, Haxell's hypergraph matching theorem, the b-matching polytope, Watkins's connectivity bound, the Nash-Williams–Tutte tree-packing theorem, Hoffman's circulation criterion, scalar Chernoff bounds); Hall's theorem is taken from Mathlib, and matrix Bernstein is avoided by deriving the one lemma that used it from the manuscript's own concentration bound. The source manuscript is an unpublished research draft that describes its own proof as not independently verified; this formalization is, to the maintainer's knowledge, the first verification of the theorem. The proved theorem has no sorry and depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.title: Existence of a Model Companion for Groups of Exponent 3: Lean Formalization
records.abstract: This project formalizes the existence of a model companion for the first-order theory of groups satisfying x^3 = 1. Its principal group-theoretic result gives a uniform, explicit bound on the number of generators needed to witness a failure of amalgamation with an existentially closed exponent-three group. The development follows the accompanying manuscript through free groups, associated graded Lie algebras, strict extensions, and the bounded-amalgamation criterion.

records.title: Metric TSP subtour-LP integrality gap
records.abstract: Lean proofs that every metric TSP instance on at least three vertices has a Hamiltonian tour costing at most (3/2 - 2.05522e-30) times any feasible subtour-LP objective, with one strictly larger saving uniform over all instances. The submission also exposes the exact finite-layer saving and a KKO-framework bound using GKL capacity estimates.

records.title: Uniform Minor-Arc Cancellation for Primes at the X^{2/15+ε} Scale
records.abstract: We prove uniform cancellation in prime-weighted exponential sums at the 2/15 scale, improving the 8/33 local Fourier scale in the Matomäki–Radziwiłł–Tao machinery for averaged prime-pair correlations. On the minor-arc part of every centered arc of radius 1/(2H), the squared von Mangoldt exponential sum over X < n <= 2X has integral at most C X (log X)^(-A), for every A > 0 and epsilon > 0, once H >= X^(2/15+epsilon) and X is large enough. The center may lie anywhere on the circle. The same cutoffs and constants work for every center and are chosen before X and H. This gives uniform minor-arc cancellation at the 2/15 threshold. Since 2/15 < 8/33, the admissible H is smaller, so the frequency windows of length 1/H are wider and the shift-averaging intervals are shorter. The constants C and X0 are ineffective because the proof uses Siegel's theorem. The development also contains an internal proof of the epsilon-form of Guth–Maynard's large-value estimate for Dirichlet polynomials. The recorded 20 September Lean 4.30 kernel replays checked 100,596 declarations for MAP and 75,874 for Guth–Maynard, using only standard axioms. The formal statement is AllCenterMAP.map_two_fifteenths, manuscript Theorem 1.1.

records.title: Corvaja–Zannier 2004: rational approximations to the powers of an algebraic number
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the whole of P. Corvaja and U. Zannier, On the rational approximations to the powers of an algebraic number: solution of two problems of Mahler and Mendès France (Acta Math. 193 (2004)), built on the repository's libraries ArithmeticHeights and DiophantineApproximation, whose Subspace Theorem it uses. The library CorvajaZannier2004 is sorry-free and within Lean's three standard axioms. It proves the Main Theorem (finitely many non-pseudo-Pisot δqu that are very close to integers, u in a finitely generated group of algebraic numbers), Theorem 1 (Mahler's question: if ‖αⁿ‖ < lⁿ infinitely often, some power of α is a Pisot number), Lemmas 1–5, Theorem 2 (Mendès France's question: the period of the continued fraction of αⁿ tends to infinity unless α is a unit or a square root of a rational, and is bounded for units), and the Appendix (the word "algebraic" cannot be dropped from Theorem 1). Eleven statements are compared.

records.title: Equivalence of the RAF abundance conjecture and Frankl's union-closed sets conjecture
records.abstract: In a catalytic reaction system with finitely many reactions, a RAF is a nonempty set of reactions whose reactants are produced from the food set by iterated closure under the selected reactions and whose reactions are each catalysed by a molecule of that closure. Steel (arXiv:2305.16714v4, Section 4) asked whether some reaction always lies in at least half of the RAFs. Call a reaction food-ready if all its reactants are food, and abundant if it lies in at least half of the sets in the family formed by the RAFs and the empty set. If some RAF U consists entirely of food-ready reactions, then some reaction of U is abundant, with no condition on the other reactions. If every reaction of the system, except at most two, is food-ready and the system has a RAF, then some reaction is abundant. Finally, the statement that every catalytic reaction system with finitely many reactions and a RAF has an abundant reaction is equivalent to Frankl's union-closed sets conjecture in the form: every finite union-closed family containing the empty set and a nonempty set has an element lying in at least half of its members.

records.title: Zero forcing number of the generalized Petersen graphs P(n,3)
records.abstract: A Lean 4 proof that the zero-forcing number of the generalized Petersen graph P(n,3) is exactly 8 for every natural number n >= 13. The formalized result is the statement recorded as Conjecture 5 in Arnav Krishnan's July 2026 correction preprint; this repository supplies and kernel-checks a proof of that conjectured statement rather than formalizing a proof already given in the cited preprint.

records.title: The Four Color Theorem (Lean 4 port of Gonthier's Coq proof)
records.abstract:
A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the Four Color Theorem, ported from Georges Gonthier's Coq proof by Claude Opus 5.5, Anthropic's AI model, working as an agent under the direction of Robert D. Barish. The main theorem, FourColor.RealPlane.four_color, states that every simple map of the real plane can be colored with at most four colors so that adjacent regions get different colors. The map may have infinitely many regions, bounded or not; each region must be open and connected, and two regions are adjacent when their closures share a point that lies in the closure of no third region. As in Coq, a compactness argument reduces the theorem to finite maps, which are turned into planar bridgeless hypermaps. A smallest hypermap that cannot be four-colored cannot exist: discharging shows that it would contain one of the 633 configurations of Robertson, Sanders, Seymour and Thomas, and each of these is reducible.
The port differs from the Coq proof in three main ways. Its statement uses Mathlib's real numbers rather than an arbitrary model of Coq's axiomatized reals; the two are equivalent, because all such models are isomorphic and the definitions use only the order. Coq checks that the 633 configurations are reducible with a procedure on trees of colorings, run by its virtual machine. The port replaces it with a new bit-parallel engine whose certificates, generated during the build, are checked by the Lean kernel itself. Finally, the case analysis of the unavoidability proof, written as tactic scripts in Coq, becomes case trees checked by a checker proved correct once. Every computation is carried out by the Lean kernel, without native_decide, and the proof uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.title: Péterfalvi's Problem for p = 3: No Group Satisfies Hypothesis (B)
records.abstract: Glauberman and Norton (Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 119, 1993) end their paper on a combinatorial problem that arises in the proof of the Feit–Thompson odd order theorem with a question of Péterfalvi: can the hypothesis of their Proposition 9 be satisfied for p = 3? The same question is Problem 1 in Appendix C of Bender and Glauberman, Local Analysis for the Odd Order Theorem (1994). Let F be the field with p^q elements, P its additive group, U its group of units of norm one over the prime field, H the semidirect product P ⋊ U, and P₀ the image of the additive group of the prime field in H. Hypothesis (B) asks for an injective homomorphism σ from H into a group G, a finite abelian subgroup Q of G whose order is prime to p, and an element y of Q, such that σ(P₀) normalizes Q and σ(P₀)^y normalizes σ(U). Proposition 9 also assumes condition (A): q does not divide p − 1. This project proves in Lean 4 that the answer is negative: for every prime q with q ∤ 3 − 1, no group G, finite or infinite, satisfies hypothesis (B) with p = 3. It also proves Péterfalvi's example from the same paper, which shows that SL(2, 2^q) satisfies hypothesis (B) with p = 2, so the hypothesis is not empty. The proof is new. It turns a witness of hypothesis (B) into relations between three copies of the additive group of the field with 3^q elements, and it rules out these relations by arithmetic in that field.

records.title: Global class field theory in Lean 4.35.0-rc2
records.abstract: For every finite abelian extension L/K of number fields, the idèle class group C_K modulo the image of the idèle-class norm from C_L is isomorphic as a topological multiplicative group to Gal(L/K). The Challenge defines the norm as the determinant on the relative adèle algebra and descends it through principal idèles; the included ClassFieldTheory development supplies the proof of the resulting reciprocity theorem.

records.title: Local class field theory in Lean 4.35.0-rc2
records.abstract: For every finite abelian extension L/K of a nonarchimedean local field, the multiplicative group K× modulo the field-norm subgroup N_{L/K}(L×) is isomorphic as a topological group to Gal(L/K). The registered declaration is the finite norm-quotient form of local reciprocity proved in the included ClassFieldTheory development. Stronger compatibility, normalization and existence results in that development are documented separately and are not part of the compared declaration.

records.title: Lean Formalization of Interpreting Lambda Calculus in Domain-Valued Random Variables (CSL 2026)
records.abstract: Formalization in Lean 4 / mathlib of the existing paper by Furber, Mardare, Panangaden, and Scott, Interpreting Lambda Calculus in Domain-Valued Random Variables (LIPIcs, Vol. 363, CSL 2026, Article 48). This repository formalizes that published mathematics; it does not present the paper's results as new mathematics originating in this repository. Three capstones sit on top of the rest of the paper: Theorem 26 (internal λ-interpretation in SetoidF_A), Corollary 34 (the Engeler model with numerals in V^A), and Theorem 43 (two fair-coin subsets of ℕ that are incomparable under the λ-definable many-one preorder). Domain-theory background is imported from a vendored copy of scott1972. The Palomar Challenge locks Theorem 43 as csl2026 and proposition_36_i on the Engeler graph model. Full Corollary 34 remains kernel-checked in the library and is not represented by a weaker Mathlib-only proxy. Lean is written by AI agents under the direction and review of the author. Dana Scott gave the author the paper. This formalization does not claim that the paper's authors participated in it or endorsed it. There is no sorry outside the deliberate holes in Challenge.lean, no project-defined axiom, and Mathlib is the only Lake require.

records.title: Conditional Hilbert-space classification of Gromov--Hausdorff space
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of the implication from five explicitly stated literature inputs to a homeomorphism between the ordinary Gromov--Hausdorff space of nonempty compact metric spaces and real square-summable sequences. The proof constructs invariant full-support probability assignments, finite dimensional local models, global AR domination and discrete approximation. The five literature inputs are assumptions, not theorems proved in this snapshot.
